There is no reason to expect accidents involving wild animals on new roads

text: Several deer run across the road in front of your vehicle. What must you reckon with?
explanation: If several deer flee across the road in front of your vehicle, you have to expect the following: several animals could follow. The entire herd could also turn in the opposite direction and switch to the other side of the roadway again.
options: There could be stragglers following the herd
The herd may come back and cross the road again
There is no reason to expect any more animals

text: At which time of the day do you have to reckon with increased wild animals crossing?
explanation: Expect more deer crossings during the morning and evening twilight. This transitional period between day and night is characterized by diffuse light conditions.
options: At dusk
At dawn
At noon

text: Which dangers must you reckon with above all in rural areas?
explanation: Where farming is practised, tractors and other agricultural vehicles travel at slow speeds and/or over width. Often the roadway is also dirty with soil or manure.
options: Soiled roadways
Slow farm vehicles
Excessively wide farm vehicles

text: A farm tractor is approaching you at dawn with its headlights switched on. What must you reckon with?
explanation: In agricultural vehicles, the lights are sometimes broken. They can also be covered up by dirt or tarpaulins. The width of the vehicles is not easy to assess. In addition, these vehicles can have up to two trailers.
options: The tractor can carry large work equipment which is difficult to see
Despite the headlights being switched on, it is not always possible to discern the width of the tractor
2 wide trailers can be attached to the tractor

text: What must you observe when you enter a tunnel?
explanation: Before entering a tunnel, you must note the following: there is a light obligation in a tunnel. Therefore, turn on the dipped beam to see and be seen better. If you have sunglasses, take them off. You must not switch on the fog lamp in the tunnel.
options: Drive with dipped headlights also during the day even in well lit tunnels
Take off your sunglasses
Switch fog headlamps on

text: What must you do in case of a traffic jam in a tunnel?
explanation: If there is a traffic jam in a tunnel, stop and turn off the engine. By keeping a safe distance of about five metres, you reduce the risk of poisoning, preserve a manoeuvring option and allow rescue vehicles to pass. Switch on the hazard warning lights to warn following drivers. Only leave your vehicle after an appropriate loudspeaker announcement.
options: Switch hazard warning lights on
When traffic comes to a standstill, keep a safety distance of approximately 5 m to the car ahead
Secure and leave vehicle immediately

text: What can impair your attention when driving through a tunnel?
explanation: When passing through a tunnel, the following factors may interfere with your attention: the lack of visual stimulus and the monotony of speed, as well as the lights of oncoming traffic. In this case, an orientation on the right side of the road is helpful; avoid looking directly into the light of oncoming traffic.
options: Reflections of light from oncoming traffic
Length of the tunnel
Good road markings

text: What must you observe particularly when driving through a tunnel?
explanation: Driving noises in a tunnel are considerably louder due to the reverberation of the tunnel walls. You can also hear the noise of the ventilation system. This has an irritating effect on you as a driver. Your eyes first have to get used to the different visibility conditions. The increased light reflections from oncoming traffic make things more difficult. The emergency signage is also distracting.
options: You may be distracted by very loud noise
Signs for safety installations such as emergency exits and emergency telephones
You may be distracted by light effects

text: Which basic code of conduct must you observe in a tunnel?
explanation: The following rules of conduct are mandatory in all tunnels: on the entire route no U-turns are allowed. Regardless of the lighting situation, the dim light must always be switched on. The instructions of the tunnel staff must always be followed. Personal protection antecedes the protection of vehicles and their security.
options: Drive with dipped headlights also by day even in a well lit tunnel
Do not make a U-turn
Follow instructions and information from the tunnel personnel

text: Why are you required to stop here?
explanation: You want to turn left. A van approaching from the opposite lane also wants to turn into this road. The vehicle has priority. Likewise, you must pay attention to pedestrians who want to cross this street.
options: - the van
- the pedestrian
- the cyclist

text: What should you do now?
explanation: The white reversing lights of the vehicle that turned in front of you indicate that it would probably turn back to its original lane in reverse. Since you cannot tell if you have been noticed by the driver, you should reduce your driving speed and be ready to brake. Refrain from an evasive maneuver due to oncoming traffic.
options: Slow down and be ready to brake
Continue driving as before
Swerve to the left

text: You want to turn right. What should you do?
explanation: Before you can turn, you have to check in the rear-view mirror if the road is clear. It is also advisable to look over your shoulder: this is the only way to be aware of dangerous situations located in the blind spot of the mirror. Keep in mind that other road users - cyclists or pedestrians - whose way you cross, always have priority.
options: Allow the cyclist to pass through the junction
Check way is clear by glancing over your shoulder
Take the turn ahead of the cyclist

text: What should you anticipate?
explanation: The other road users can react to this situation with all the different scenarios described. All are equally dangerous. Therefore, extreme caution and slow driving is required.
options: The motorbike could swerve to the left
The person beside the van could encroach further onto the road
Pedestrians could cross the road in front of the van

text: Ahead of the motorbike a car is seeking to reverse on the road. What should you anticipate?
explanation: Car drivers often underestimate the speed of approaching motorcyclists; the same happens to the driver here while he's pulling out of a parking space. The action alternatives of the motorcyclist - braking or dodging - are both dangerous for him on a snow-slicked road surface. He could fall. Also consider the longer braking distance in this weather.
options: That the car continues to reverse
That the motorbike will suddenly brake
That my braking distance will be longer than normal

text: You are driving quickly along a main road and some distance ahead you see a deer close to the carriageway. What should you do?
explanation: If the deer is not yet on the road, you should under no circumstances perform emergency braking. This would unnecessarily endanger other road users and force them to unpredictable reactions. Nevertheless, you should reduce the speed of your vehicle and keep it ready to brake: the animal could run without warning on the road.
options: - reduce speed
- be ready to brake
- perform an emergency braking manoeuvre

text: Why are you particularly at risk, if you are riding a two-wheeler?
explanation: Especially in restrictive visibility conditions such as fog and darkness, the small silhouette of the two-wheeled driver leads to the fact that he is recognized late or not at all. In addition, the small design makes it difficult to estimate its speed. In the event of a collision, two-wheelers generally offer less protection than most other motor vehicles.
options: Because I can be easily overlooked
Because my speed can be underestimated
Because I am at greater risk of injury in the event of an accident

text: Driving on a very busy road with several lanes, you have manoeuvred yourself into the lane for taking a left turn. Now instead of turning left, you want to turn right. What should you do?
explanation: A lane change or turning right could endanger other road users due to the heavy traffic. You must therefore turn left and take a small detour. Watch out for lane markings that prohibit you from changing lanes.
options: I turn left
I reverse with my hazard lights turned on
Driving a wide curve, I turn right

text: There is a tunnel on my route. What should I know?
explanation: If there is a tunnel on your route, you should know the appropriate traffic signs and behavioral measures in the event of a breakdown or an accident: in this case, alert the tunnel monitoring center and follow the next escape route. First, turn off the engine of your vehicle and leave the ignition key in the lock for rescue operations.
options: I should know how I park and leave my vehicle if I am unable to continue driving
I should know how escape routes are indicated in tunnels
I can be sure that help will arrive promptly in the event of emergencies

text: While driving through a tunnel, you notice a fire in your vehicle. You are not able to exit the tunnel. What should you do?
explanation: If a fire in your vehicle prevents you from leaving a tunnel: Park the vehicle unlocked with the engine switched off and the ignition key remaining in the lock. Alarm the tunnel monitoring center. Take the next escape route on foot.
options: - turn on the hazard warning system
- switch off the engine
- leave the key in the ignition

text: While driving in a tunnel you were forced to bring your vehicle to a halt due to a fire. What should you do now?
explanation: If you have to park your vehicle in a tunnel due to a fire, you should: stop the engine, leave the key in the ignition switch and quickly trigger the fire alarm at the emergency call station. Leave the tunnel as fast as possible on the next escape route.
options: I trigger the fire alarm at the emergency call point
I extinguish the fire as best I can
I lock my vehicle

text: What should you anticipate?
explanation: You see that the truck wants to turn in front of you. The vehicle obscures the view of the traffic, so you need to adjust your speed. The truck probably swings out to take the curve. He might stop abruptly to let pedestrians or other road users pass.
options: - will swing outwards even more
- will come to a sudden stop
- will remain stationary in the right-hand lane

text: What must you watch out for now?
explanation: You want to turn right, so does the car driver in front of you. The pedestrian traffic light of the cross street into which you want to turn shows green, and the pedestrian has priority. It is possible that your car in front will pull up and stop soon after to let the pedestrian pass. On the right you can also see a cyclist. The cyclist could drive past your vehicle on the right and circle your turning vehicle on the left. Avoid this danger.
options: For the vehicle on the road ahead
For the bicycle
For the motorbike

text: Why are you required to stop here?
explanation: The cyclist must be given priority because she is on the right-of-way. Wait until the cyclist has passed the vehicles and driven through.
options: Because of the cyclist
Because of the green car
Because of the pedestrian

text: Why are you required to stop here?
explanation: The traffic on the main road is jammed. The red car drives around the parked vehicles to turn left. You have to wait and let this car pass as it has priority.
options: Because of the red car
Because of the cyclist
Because of the pedestrian

text: What is the right course of action now?
explanation: When an animal walks on the road from the right, an evasive maneuver is a natural reflex. However, this can have far more fatal consequences than keeping the track. An evasive maneuver to the right may lead into the roadside ditch, one to the left may lead to a collision with oncoming traffic. It's safest to continue straight ahead.
options: I keep a tight hold of the steering wheel and keep it pointed straight ahead
I swerve to the left
I swerve to the right

text: What should you do now?
explanation: You can see that the animal is about to run on the road. Horns may help stop it. In addition, you should initiate emergency braking to reduce a potential collision. Do not dodge! This rather leads to accidents with personal injury than a collision with an animal.
options: I perform an emergency braking manoeuvre
I sound my horn
I swerve to the left

text: What must you look out for when the traffic lights turn green?
explanation: While you wait at the red light, a motorcyclist pushes past the waiting vehicles. When the traffic light switches to green you should pay attention to the motorcyclist and let him pass before he initiates a risky overtaking maneuver. But you should also let the pedestrian cross the road, which is still on the road despite it being green.
options: For [the pedestrian]
For the motorbike
For oncoming traffic

text: What must you be prepared for in this situation?
explanation: The truck blocks your view. You can therefore recognize neither the oncoming traffic nor traffic signs behind the truck. Approach the vehicle at low speed. Look for oncoming traffic (they have priority) and keep your distance to the open driver's door when driving around. The driver of the truck could suddenly get out and jump onto the road.
options: That oncoming traffic will appear
That the truck driver will jump down onto the carriageway
That traffic signs are concealed behind the truck

text: What should you do when driving through a tunnel?
explanation: When driving through a tunnel, proceed as follows: Make sure to pay attention to the safety distance and orient yourself on the right-hand side of the road in order to avoid glare from oncoming traffic. Get an overview of safety devices so you know where the nearest emergency exit and emergency telephone are located.
options: In a tunnel with oncoming traffic, I position myself towards the right-hand edge of the roadway
I memorise the safety features such as emergency exits and emergency telephones
I drive with a reduced distance to the vehicle ahead, so that I can use its tail lights as a guide

text: What must you watch out for now?
explanation: You intend to turn left. Two cyclists move in the same direction. You must pay particular attention to these, as they could also turn into the street without notice.
options: For [the cyclist] on the left
For [the cyclist] on the right
For [the green car]

text: What should you do now?
explanation: Since the dog (from the right) seems to be walking into the street, please perform emergency braking and keep the steering wheel straight and steady.
options: I perform an emergency braking manoeuvre
I hold the steering wheel straight and firmly
I steer to the left

text: For what should your prepare yourself in this situation?
explanation: Please be prepared for people behind the bus to enter the lane and for the bus to swerve and briefly enter your lane.
options: As it begins moving, the bus will swing out onto my side of the road
People will cross the road at the rear of the bus
The quad suddenly starts to move

text: What kind of behaviour must you anticipate from cyclists?
explanation: All 3 answers are correct. Cyclists use one-way streets in both directions, they may not have lights in the dark or they may ride on the wrong side of cycle paths.
options: - one-way roads in both directions
- the wrong side of cycle paths
- no lights when it is dark

text: What must you be prepared for here?
explanation: The traffic sign indicates a rambler parking area, which means that people can walk across the roadway and vehicles can drive off or onto the parking area at any time.
options: People walking on the road
Oncoming vehicles turning left
Vehicles turning onto the road

text: Why are you required to stop now?
explanation: As you do not have a full view of the traffic situation and must give the cyclist the right of way, you must stop and carefully feel your way in.
options: Because of [the cyclist]
Because the traffic situation is confusing
Because of the [yellow] truck

text: You want to continue driving straight ahead. What is the correct course of action in this situation?
explanation:
You are coming from a priority road first. As there are no other traffic signs, right is before left. The red car is driving on your right and therefore has the right of way. 
The electric scooter does not have right of way, so to avoid an accident you should let it cross anyway.
options: I allow the [red] vehicle to turn
I allow the electric scooter to cross the road
I am the first to cross over the junction

text: I want to re-join the road. What is the correct assessment of this situation?
explanation: As the vehicle parked behind you is very large, you will only see vehicles coming from behind at a late stage and you yourself will only be recognised by other drivers at a late stage.
options: - drivers only see me late
- I only see vehicles late
- drivers give my priority in re-joining the road

text: Why is it dangerous to carry on driving past this accident scene?
explanation: The traffic situation is unclear, sudden braking manoeuvres by gawpers and pedestrians crossing the road must be expected.
options: Because secondary accidents can occur
Because pedestrians can be overlooked
Because the traffic movement situation is unclear

text: What must you watch out for when turning right here?
explanation: The cyclist has the right of way. When turning right, you must always pay attention to whether pedestrians or cyclists are approaching. They are allowed to cross the street in front of you. Use the rearview mirror and also look over your shoulder to be able to see the blind spot.
options: [For the cyclist]
For oncoming traffic
For the motorbike

text: What is the right course of action now?
explanation: The scooter does not seem to see you coming and takes the right of way. To avoid an accident, you must immediately perform emergency braking.
options: I perform an emergency stop
I pass quickly through the junction
I brake slightly

text: What must you anticipate in this situation?
explanation: Since the obstacle is on your side, you must wait in this case. In addition, the cyclist will overtake the parked car and therefore swerve to the left.
options: [The cyclist] will pull out to the left
Oncoming traffic
[The cyclist] will dismount to allow me to pass

text: You are driving through a tunnel. What special aspect applies here?
explanation: In a tunnel, the emergency exits and SOS emergency telephones are clearly signposted and illuminated. In an emergency, you should use the facilities. You can easily be distracted by the different lighting, the lights of other road users and the much louder noises in the tunnel.
options: - I can be distracted by loud vehicle noise
- the safety devices, like emergency exits and emergency telephones are signposted
- I can be distracted by lighting effects

text: What is the right course of action now?
explanation: The vehicle that is still parked wants to enter the road and has obviously overlooked you. You should slow down to avoid an accident.
options: I brake
I swerve out to the left
I accelerate because I have priority

text: What should you anticipate now?
explanation: The [yellow] vehicle will stop, so you must be ready for the driver to open the door. The cyclist will probably move to the left to overtake the yellow vehicle. You must also expect the truck to drive off.
options: The driver of the [yellow] vehicle opens the driver-side door
The [blue] truck pulls out to the left
[The cyclist] pulls out to the left

text: You are driving on a section of road where a traffic jam has been reported. What is the right course of action?
explanation: You should be extra attentive on curves and before hilltops, because the traffic situation is difficult to see. You should also continue to follow the traffic reports.
options: I continue to follow the traffic reports
I take particular care when driving around bends and on the approach to summits
I apply the emergency brake assist to safely stop before the tail end of the traffic jam

text: Why are you required to stop now?
explanation: The "Give way" sign in combination with the additional bicycle sign shows you that you must pay attention to possible cyclists and give them the right of way. Therefore, you must now stop and let the cyclist pass.
options: Because of the cyclist
Because of the pedestrians
Because of the truck

text: What is the correct course of action in this situation?
explanation: If a cyclist suddenly comes from the left, you must do an emergency stop.
options: I perform an emergency braking manoeuvre
I continue driving, ready to brake
I accelerate

text: While driving, a deer crosses the road in front of your vehicle. What should you be aware of?
explanation: A deer is very unpredictable, maybe it runs back into the forest, maybe it will stop in the middle of the street. You should therefore reduce your speed and follow what is happening, as other animals can also step on the road.
options: Other animals might follow the deer
The deer might stop in the middle of the road
I can scare off the deer by turning on my main beam lights

text: What is the right course of action?
explanation: As the lorry in front of you is parking in reverse, you must continue to slow down. You can only change lanes when the lane to your left is free. Stay in your lane for the time being and continue braking.
options: I continue braking
I remain waiting in my lane for now
I steer to the left now

text: What should you anticipate in this situation?
explanation:
You are driving on a turning priority road. Anyone leaving a priority road must give way to vehicles following the priority road.
The yellow car flashes and turns left. Although it does not have right of way, at its high speed it will not be able to stop without coming into your lane. You should therefore brake and give up your right of way to avoid a collision. The obligation to avoid accidents takes precedence over all right of way rules.
options: That [the yellow car] will turn left
That I will have to yield my right of way
That [the pedestrian] will cross the road

text: What is the right behaviour now?
explanation:
In the left side mirror you can see that a car behind you is about to overtake. At the same time, the person on the bike on the right in front of you could move onto the road. A truck is also coming towards you on the opposite lane. All three factors lead to a narrow roadway and thus increase the risk of accidents.
In this situation you have to brake to avoid a collision with the overtaking car and the cyclist.
options: I brake
I swerve to the left
I continue to drive steadily

text: What is the right course of action in this situation?
explanation: The cyclist from the left does not seem to slow down, so brake sharply.
options: I brake very sharply
I sound my horn and continue driving
I steer to the right

text: Why must you brake now?
explanation: Because the cyclist wants to be in your lane, brake because of the cyclist.
options: Because of [the cyclist]
Because of [the red vehicle]
Because of the bus stop

text: What must you watch out for now?
explanation: The cyclist on the right is riding on the roadway. There is a cyclist on the left whom we must let go first as a result of our turning procedure.
options: For [the cyclist] on the left
For [the cyclist] on the right
For the [blue] car

text: What should you anticipate in this situation?
explanation: As you are driving behind a large vehicle, it can quickly happen that you are overlooked by oncoming traffic. The danger sign warns of rolling gravel on the road.
options: The driver of the [yellow] car fails to see me
There are loose chippings on the roadway
The tractor in front of me, will turn right

text: You are driving outside of a built-up area. What is the correct course of action in this situation?
explanation:
This is not a protected cycle path. You may therefore continue to use the cycle path.
When entering another road, you must make sure that the road is clear. There is a "Give way" sign here. This means that the cyclists on the other side of the road have the right of way and you must wait. You should check for yourself that the road is clear.
You must still make sure that the road is clear for crossing.
options: I only continue driving once I have reassured myself that the road is clear
I do not have to reassure myself that the road is clear, because [the cyclist] is moving
I may no longer continue using the cycle path

text: Why should you be ready to brake now?
explanation: The brown vehicle has just stopped, there is a high risk that a person will get out hastily and carelessly in the next moment. Therefore, you must be ready to brake.
options: Because the driver of the brown vehicle could exit the vehicle
Because [the pedestrian] could walk out onto the road
Because the bus could move across onto my lane

text: What is the right thing to do in this situation?
explanation: The cyclist is obviously crossing the road without paying attention to the traffic situation and without braking. Use emergency braking to avoid a collision.
options: I perform an emergency braking manoeuvre
I continue driving, ready to brake
I move towards the right

text: A motorist has had too much alcohol to drink and therefore must not drive. How is it not possible for him to recover his ability to drive in a short time?
explanation: After heavy consumption of alcohol, there's no quick way to restore your ability to drive. Neither sleeping nor walking is enough. The alcohol concentration in the blood also does not change by drinking strong coffee. The body breaks down only about 0.1 permille alcohol per hour.
options: - sleeping for half an hour
- drinking two cups of strong coffee
- going for a walk for half an hour

text: Which substances can impair fitness to drive in a similar way to alcohol?
explanation: Drugs, in particular, change perceptions and impair the ability to respond quickly and appropriately. Because of this, drug use of any kind make you unfit to drive. Even some medicines can impair your driving abilities. If you are prescribed medication by the doctor, pay attention to the instructions in the instruction leaflet.
options: Certain medicines and intoxicants
A cup of coffee
A cup of tea

text: What can impair fitness to drive?
explanation: Anything that negatively affects the sense organs can reduce the ability to drive. In addition to drugs, this includes medications, so you should read the package leaflet before taking them. At a blood alcohol level of 0.3 permille, you are already unfit to drive. Fatigue is one of the most common causes of accidents. Here your attention and concentration cease, and this can lead to so-called microsleep.
options: Fatigue
Alcohol and other intoxicants
Certain medicines

text: In general, how long does it take before an alcohol level of 1.0 per mille (100 mg/100 ml) is cleared from the blood stream?
explanation: The rule of thumb is: 0.1 permille is being broken down per hour. After 10 hours, 1.0 permille are completely degraded.
options: 10 hours
5 hours
1 hour

text: What can increase the intoxicating effect of alcohol?
explanation: The effect of alcohol is enhanced by medication. Especially large amounts of alcohol in combination with sleeping pills, painkillers or tranquilizers can be life-threatening. If you drink alcohol on an empty stomach or consume a large amount of alcohol in a short period of time, the alcohol enters your blood immediately: you are suddenly dead drunk.
options: Sleeping pills, pain killers or sedatives
Drinking on an "empty" stomach
Downing alcoholic drinks in one

text: What can be the effects of even small quantities of alcohol?
explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol affect your central nervous system and worsen your perception: your hearing and vision, your ability to react and perform, your sense of balance. Your willingness to take risks increases, dangers are no longer recognized by you. You think you are roadworthy, even if that is not true.
options: Delayed reactions
Reckless driving
Impairment of hearing and vision

text: What effects can drugs have?
explanation: Drug substances affect the central nervous system and distort sensory perception. Although you will feel more efficient under the influence of drugs, your real performance will be reduced and makes you unable to drive. Compared to other intoxicants, drugs are more addictive.
options: Intoxication
Dependence, addiction
Prolonged improvement in physical and mental capabilities

text: Which drugs can make a person temporarily unfit to drive even when consumed on a single occasion?
explanation: The use of drugs even in small quantities leads to temporary inability to drive. Unlike alcohol, there are no limits for drugs. Driving under the influence of drugs can mean the loss of your driver's license.
options: Hashish, marijuana
Heroin, cocaine, amphetamines
LSD

text: When is a drug-dependent person fit to drive a motor vehicle again?
explanation: Anyone who was caught driving under the influence of drugs had to hand in his driver's license. If he is a drug addict, the person must live drug-free for a full year before he can get back his driving license. Proof of this is given by the Appraisal Body (Ger. Begutachterstelle für Fahreignung (BfF)) in form of a report.
options: After he/she can be shown to have stopped taking drugs for at least one year and is not likely to have a relapse
If he/she has not taken drugs for one month
If he/she has not taken drugs for six months

text: How is the intoxicating substance in hashish broken down by the body?
explanation: Drugs such as hashish are not broken down evenly in the body - in contrast to alcohol, for example. Therefore, one cannot make a reliable prediction in this regard.
options: Unevenly over an indeterminate period
Evenly, 0.1 per mille per hour
Evenly, 0.1 gram per hour

text: What are the consequences for a person driving a motor vehicle under the influence of drugs (e.g. hashish, heroin, cocaine)?
explanation: Driving a vehicle under the influence of drugs such as hashish, cocaine or heroin may result in: withdrawal of the license, a fine and/or imprisonment. Imprisonment may amount to up to five years if other persons were endangered. In order to get your driving license back, you have to undergo a medical-psychological assessment (MPA).
options: Confiscation of driving licence or driving ban
Fine and/or imprisonment
Compulsory medical/psychological examination

text: What are the possible effects of hashish consumption?
explanation: The consumption of hashish leads to states of intoxication in which the feeling for time and space is lost. Attention is lowered, the perception of the environment is clearly obscured. There may be sensory illusions and states of confusion, as well as hallucinations.
options: Intoxication with dangerous hallucination and reduced reaction capability
Intoxication with confusion and depression
Improved judgement of time

text: What are the possible effects of hashish consumption?
explanation: The use of hashish puts the user in a state of intoxication in which the ability to assess risks is lost. The feeling for time and place is lost and hallucinations as well as misperceptions can be the result. Distances and speeds can no longer be estimated correctly. The willingness to take risks as well as the tendency to misjudgments are increasing rapidly.
options: Diminished awareness of danger
Increased likelihood of mistakes in assimilating information
Misjudgement of speed and distance

text: Who is not allowed to drink alcohol when driving motor vehicles?
explanation: During the probation period or before the age of 21, a limit of 0.0 permille applies to you before each journey and while driving a motor vehicle: an absolute alcohol ban.
options: All drivers under 21
All drivers during their probation period
All drivers

text: Are drivers during their probation period allowed to be under the influence of alcohol when driving motor vehicles?
explanation: During the probationary period you must not drink any alcohol if you want to drive a motor vehicle. In general, you should stick to 0.0 permille when participating in traffic.
options: No, definitely not
Yes, up to a blood alcohol level of 50 milligrams if they have not committed any alcohol related traffic violation
Yes, up to a blood alcohol level of 30 milligrams if they have not committed any alcohol related traffic violation

text: Why can fitness to drive be impaired even by just a small quantity of alcohol?
explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol have a negative effect on vision, responsiveness and perception. The willingness for hasty actions increases and the estimation of distances as well as attention declines.
options: Because this reduces the field of vision
Because this diminishes spatial vision
Because this reduces the reaction time

text: How can the consumption of cannabis products affect driving performance?
explanation: The consumption of cannabis products is counterproductive to the ability to drive. Regardless of individually different manner of reactions and behaviors after consumption, the ability to focus on traffic generally decreases while the sensitivity to glare increases.
options: The awareness of other traffic decreases
Concentration on driving decreases
The glare sensitivity decreases

text: Why is consuming drugs even just once, dangerous for driving on public roads?
explanation: Drugs usually cause perceptual disorders. Even the one-time use of drugs can lead to a high lasting several hours. You as a consumer would be unfit to drive.
options: - can result in my unfitness to drive
- can result in an intoxication state lasting for several hours
- can cause faulty perceptions

text: How long does cannabis and its degradation products remain detectable in urine?
explanation: Cannabis and its breakdown products are traceable in your urine for a period between ten days and three months after consumption. The exact amount of time depends on the consumption frequency and the accuracy of the test.
options: For some weeks
Several days at most
Only for a few hours

text: Why is an individual unfit to drive after consuming the drug crystal meth?
explanation: "Crystal Meth" has a negative effect on the driving ability for the following reasons: The drug causes delusions. It caters the overestimation of one's own performance and sudden exhaustion. Even the consumption of small amounts makes you unfit for driving.
options: Because of the possibility of experiencing hallucinations
Because it is possible to over-estimate personal capabilities
Because of the possible sudden onset of fatigue

text: How can your fitness to drive be quickly restored following the excessive consumption of alcohol?
explanation: As alcohol degrades very slowly in the body, nothing can restore your driving ability in the short term.
options: Nothing can achieve this
By drinking two cups of coffee
By doing 15 minutes of sport

text: What can affect ability to drive in a similar way to alcohol?
explanation: Alcohol, drugs and medication have a negative effect on our reaction time, inhibition and motor skills.
options: Medications
Drugs
Soft drinks

text: How can the consumption of cannabis products affect the driver?
explanation: After cannabis use, your perception is clouded and your ability to concentrate decreases.
options: It reduces the awareness of other traffic
It reduces the ability to concentrate on driving
It reduces sensitivity to glare

text: What effects can result from taking drugs?
explanation:
Drugs lead to noise. This also changes the perception of a person. These intoxicating states can cause various impairments, such as the impairment of the concentration and an incorrect assessment of the speed.
Furthermore, there may be an increase in the risk of risk, since it is very common to misjudge critical situations or your own driving ability.
options: Impairment of concentration
Increased readiness to take risks
A miscalculation of speeds

text: Consuming what substance before or while driving, can make you unfit to drive?
explanation:
For all drugs and substances listed here, consumption will lead to driving inability.
Drugs and alcohol at the wheel lead to a significant risk to road traffic because they significantly restrict attention and concentration. In addition, taking alcohol and drugs can have numerous physical and psychological effects, as can the misjudgments of critical situations or the overestimation of one's own driving ability.
options: Cocaine
Alcohol
Hashish

text: When ambient temperatures are high, this negatively affects driver concentration during long journeys and accident numbers rise. Which of the following is it advisable to do, so that you remain alert and can drive safely, even during high summer?
explanation: When temperatures are high, make sure you drink enough water and take regular breaks to exercise.
options: I plan for regular breaks
I drink enough
I try to perform my trips around noon

text: You should refrain from driving any vehicle if you are experiencing what physical symptoms?
explanation:
If you feel ill, you should take a break or let other people drive to ensure the safety of all road users.
Dizziness, nausea and fever affect your concentration and your ability to drive, so wait until you feel better to avoid endangering yourself and other road users.
options: Nausea
Dizziness
Fever

chapterName: Basic Rules About Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: Participation in road traffic requires caution at all times and consideration towards other road users. What does this mean for you?
explanation: Always count on the mistakes of others as well as your own. Stick to an anticipatory driving style at all times and do not insist on your right of way in any case. This would violate the principles of traffic regulations and endanger other road users.
options: - reckon with improper conduct on the part of others
- drive with foresight
- insist on your right of priority at all times

chapterName: Basic Rules About Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: To which road users must you show particular care?
explanation: You must be particularly careful towards the following road users: all those who are not or are no longer able to cope with the demands of road traffic. This means that the principle of trust is abolished, due diligence towards children, elderly and/or frail people, disabled or drunk cyclists is up to you.
options: To persons with obvious disabilities
To children
To taxi drivers

text: When may you use the right-hand hard shoulder?
explanation: The right side strip may be used in the following cases: 1. for holding and parking, 2. for slow moving vehicles such as mopeds or agricultural tractors and machinery. These should use the right side strip to avoid traffic obstructions and traffic jams. The side strip must be attached and have a sufficient width. It is forbidden in any case to use the side strip for overtaking.
options: For stopping and parking
For driving a slow-moving vehicle
For overtaking

text: You have manoeuvred into the left lane by mistake, but would like to take a right turn. What is the right course of action?
explanation: With a solid line as a road edge marking, you must under no circumstances turn right. Rather, you must stay in your lane and continue straight or turn left.
options: I continue driving straight ahead or turn left
I move carefully into the right-hand lane
I drive straight ahead and turn right at the intersection

text: When driving on main roads, which vehicles must use the hard shoulders where possible?
explanation: Slow-moving vehicles such as tractors, mopeds must use the hard shoulder. Other vehicles that go faster than 45km/h need to remain on the road
options: Slow-moving agricultural tractors and machinery
Mopeds
Small-engine motorcycles

text: What should you do in this situation?
explanation: In a street where vehicles park on both sides, the range of movement is limited. With only one lane, vehicles are equally important in both directions. Nevertheless, you should drive into a gap here to let an oncoming vehicle pass.
options: - into the gap to allow the oncoming vehicle to drive past
- onwards, because the oncoming vehicle has to reverse
- backwards, because the oncoming vehicle has right of way

text: A horse-drawn carriage is coming towards you. What should you do?
explanation: Drive as far to the right as possible when you encounter a horse-drawn carriage. Do not honk and do not drive at high motor speed. The animals could be sensitive to noise and be frightened. It might happen that they break out and run on your side of the road.
options: - Avoid making noise
- drive as far to the right as possible
- switch on parking light

text: What is correct in this situation?
explanation: At the traffic sign "Intersection or junction with right-of-way", you must follow the right-of-way rule "right before left". This applies to the nearest intersection.
options: - the "right-before-left" right-of-way rule applies
- I have right of way
- a traffic-calming zone ends

text: What do you have to watch out for, when crossing a priority road?
explanation: When crossing a priority road, you must keep in mind: 1. the width of the priority road, 2. the distance and speed of oncoming traffic, 3. the weather conditions. These are all the influences that are important for crossing the priority road. The weather influences the condition of the road and the visibility. Along with the road width, it determines how long you need to cross the priority road. By estimating the distance and the speed of oncoming traffic you can assess how much time you have available.
options: - the width of the priority road
- the speed and the distance of the cross traffic
- the weather conditions

text: You want to use an autobahn. To allow you to do so, what type-specific maximum speed must be entered in Part I of the registration certificate or in the operating licence?
explanation: According to the German Road Traffic Regulations (Straßenverkehrsordnung - StVO), motorways may only be used by vehicles with a maximum design speed of more than 60 km / h.

text: You are driving in a built-up area on a cycle path on which mopeds are permitted. What should you anticipate?
explanation: If you ride on a bike path in town, you should expect everything. Doors of parked cars can be opened suddenly, turning vehicles can overlook you and pedestrians can use the bike path.
options: - the doors of parked vehicles will be suddenly opened
- vehicles turning into another street may not be able to see me
- pedestrians will walk on the cycle path

text: Which factors lengthen your braking distance?
explanation: The braking distance of a vehicle is extended: 1. on a steep hill, 2. on a wet or slippery road surface, 3. if the vehicle has to carry an additional load. The reasons for the extended braking distances are: On a steep hill, acceleration force is caused by gravity. On wet or slippery roads, the static friction between tires and road surface is reduced. Additional load increases the mass that needs to come to a stop.
options: Towing a trailer not fitted with brakes
A wet or slippery roadway
Driving down slopes

text: What does the braking distance depend on?
explanation: The braking distance of your vehicle depends on the tires, the brake system and the condition of the road. Braking forces are generated powerfully and quickly by a functioning brake system and are optimally transmitted to the roadway only if there is sufficient tread. The static friction of the tires depends on the road condition.
options: - tyres
- braking system
- road surface

text: What is the permissible top speed generally in built-up areas?
explanation:
50 km/h is the legally prescribed maximum speed limit within cities.
If this speed is exceeded, you will no longer be able to process information in time to react.

text: You double the speed at which you are travelling. How does this affect the braking distance?
explanation: It also depends on your speed: At twice the speed, the braking distance will be four times as long - from 9m at 30 km/h to 36m at 60 km/h.

text: What must you take into consideration when selecting your speed?
explanation: You are only allowed to drive your vehicle at maximum legal speed. The actual permissible speed is usually lower. It depends on the visibility and weather conditions, the road conditions, the current traffic conditions and your personal driving skills.
options: Visibility and weather conditions
The condition of the road and traffic conditions
Personal driving ability

text: By which rule of thumb can you determine from the speed the distance in metres a motor vehicle travels in one second?
explanation: With the following rule of thumb and the help of speed, you can calculate the distance in meters that a vehicle travels in a second: Divide the speed by ten and multiply the result by three. If you drive your vehicle at 100 km/h, you can travel 30 meters in one second.
options: {Speed in km/h}/{10} x 3
{Speed in km/h}/{10} x 5
{Speed in km/h}/{10} x {Speed in km/h}/{10}

text: By which rule of thumb can you determine the braking distance in metres from speed when braking normally?
explanation: The braking distance is the distance you travel from the start of braking until your vehicle stands. It can be calculated from a simple rule of thumb during normal braking: the speed traveled divided by ten times the speed traveled divided by ten.
options: {Speed in km/h}/{10} x {Speed in km/h}/{10}
{Speed in km/h}/{10} x 5
{Speed in km/h}/{10} x 3

text: You are travelling at 30 km/h. According to the rule of thumb, the braking distance is 9 metres when braking normally. How long is the braking distance under the same conditions when travelling at 60 km/h?
explanation: If you double your speed to 60 km/h, the braking distance will quadruple. Just proceed from the braking distance for 30 km/h and accordingly calculate 9 m times 4 = 36 m.

text: You are driving on a wide road on which oncoming traffic can pass by you, unobstructed. Within what distance must you be able to stop in any event?
explanation: You must be able to stop within the distance you can see in case obstacles such as animals or people suddenly enter the carriageway.
options: - the distance readily visible to me
- half the distance readily visible to me
- twice the distance readily visible to me

text: What does the distance to be maintained from the vehicle ahead depend on?
explanation: The distance to the vehicle in front depends on the speed as well as the visibility and road conditions. As a rule of thumb, you should keep at least a distance of half of your speed in meters. In poor visibility or road conditions, the distance should be increased.
options: Visibility conditions
Speed
State of the road surface

text: What is the right course of action?
explanation: If a driver in front of you suddenly intervenes and reduces the safety distance between him and your vehicle, you must brake until the distance is guaranteed again.
options: I brake
I increase my distance to the vehicle in front moving into my lane
I maintain my speed

text: What is the right course of action?
explanation: If you are overtaken by a car, you must not increase your pace. On the contrary, you should slow down to let the overtaking car recoil as fast as possible.
options: I reduce my speed
I maintain my speed
I accelerate

text: What benefit can be obtained by maintaining an adequate distance between you and the vehicle ahead?
explanation: You should always maintain a sufficiently large safety distance to the car in front of you. Through anticipatory driving, you maintain optimal visibility and reduce the risk of accidents.
options: It aids far-sighted driving
It helps reduce the risk of accidents
It restricts visibility

text: When driving outside of a built-up area, you want to overtake cyclists or pedestrians. What is the minimum space to the side that you must maintain?
explanation: Outside built-up areas, the minimum distance to be maintained for pedestrians, cyclists and personal transporters is 2 metres.

text: Driving within a built-up area, you want to overtake a cyclist. What is the minimum space to the side that you must maintain?
explanation: When overtaking, you must keep a sufficient distance to the side so as not to endanger other road users. In built-up areas, the minimum distance for pedestrians, cyclists and personal transporters is 1.5 metres.

text: Driving within a built-up area, you want to overtake an electric scooter. What is the minimum space to the side that you must maintain?
explanation: When overtaking, you must keep a sufficient distance to the side so as not to endanger other road users. In built-up areas, the minimum distance for pedestrians, cyclists and personal transporters is 1.5 metres.

text: Where is overtaking prohibited?
explanation: Overtaking is prohibited in the following cases: 1. in the event of an unclear traffic situation; 2. in the event of violation of traffic regulations. In one-way streets, however, there is no general rule of no overtaking. Before you start the overtaking process, look back in the mirror and over your shoulder to make sure you are not hindering or jeopardizing other road users.
options: When the traffic situation is not clear
Where oncoming traffic could be obstructed
In all one-way streets

text: What is the correct procedure for pulling out to overtake?
explanation: For pulling out when overtaking the following rules apply: You need to convince yourself with a look in the mirror and a glance over the shoulder that your overtaking maneuver will neither jeopardize nor hinder subsequent traffic. Only then you are allowed to indicate and pull out. During the overtaking process you must take care not to hinder oncoming traffic. If the driver in front of you is flashing to the right, you should not be tempted to overtake.
options: There is no danger to the traffic behind
Oncoming traffic is not endangered
The vehicle in front indicates right

text: What must you do to end an overtaking manoeuvre?
explanation: As an overtaking driver, you must merge right as soon as possible. However, do not go back into the lane as long as you're still too close to the driver you just overtook, as you may obstruct or even endanger him. Use the turn signal in good time before starting to pull out and merging back into the lane again.
options: Move over to the right as soon as possible without inconveniencing the vehicle you have overtaken
Signal your intention to draw in clearly and in good time
Move over to the right-hand side of the roadway right in front of the vehicle you have overtaken

text: What are the regulations governing speed when overtaking?
explanation: You may only overtake a vehicle in front of you if you are significantly (at least 20 km/h) faster. Also, when overtaking: Do not exceed the maximum speed limit. The one who is being overtaken must not increase its initial speed during the maneuver.
options: The speed of the overtaking vehicle must be appreciably higher
The permissible top speed must not be exceeded
The person being overtaken must not increase his speed

text: What must you do when you are being overtaken?
explanation: Drive as far to the right as possible so as not to jeopardize the oncoming traffic and overtaking vehicle. During the entire overtaking process, you, as the one who is being overtaken, must not increase the speed, as otherwise safe overtaking would not be possible.
options: If possible, drive on the far right
Not increase your speed
Increase your speed

text: On which side must you overtake a tram which is travelling in the middle of the roadway (not a one-way street)?
explanation: Trams must in general be overtaken on the right. If vehicles are parked here, you have to drive behind the tram. If the rails are too far to the right, trams may also be overtaken on the left.
options: On the right
On the left
On the left only if other vehicles are blocking the roadway on the right

text: When may a tram be overtaken on the left?
explanation: Rail vehicles such as trams may basically only be overtaken on the right. For once, you can overtake on the left when the rails are too far to the right or when the rail vehicle is traveling in a one-way street. The right-hand traffic obstructing vehicles are not a sufficient reason to overtake rail vehicles on the left.
options: In one-way streets
When the rails run too far to the right
When the roadway (not a one-way street) to the right of the tram is blocked by other vehicles

text: Which vehicles may be overtaken only by maintaining a specially great lateral distance?
explanation: When overtaking you must always keep sufficient distance to the road users next to you. This must be particularly large with motorcycle and bicycle riders. Single lane vehicles are more unstable and can sway. The lateral minimum distance to two-wheeled vehicles is 1.5 meters.
options: Bicycles
Motorcycles
Trams

text: When must you signal?
explanation: Whenever you want to make a lane change or turn, you need to indicate. This also applies when following a turning priority road, but not when you leave the priority road straight ahead. Even if the direction indicator is set: always make sure that you do not endanger anyone when pulling out or going back into a lane.
options: Before pulling out to overtake or to pass
Before pulling in again after overtaking
When proceeding straight ahead as you leave a priority road which bends sharply

text: Where is it forbidden to overtake?
explanation: When overtaking, you must exclude dangerous situations for other road users. It is generally forbidden to overtake on pedestrian crossings and on roads that are difficult to observe. You might see oncoming vehicles too late. You may overtake the bus on the bus lane.
options: At pedestrian crossings
At points in the road where visibility is poor
At special bus lanes

text: You are driving a slow-moving vehicle on a main road. How can you facilitate faster-moving vehicles in overtaking?
explanation: To allow faster vehicles to overtake you on a country road, you can dodge on a suitable side stripe, a lay by or in a rest stop. It is also possible to slow down or even stop at a suitable location.
options: - onto the hard shoulder
- onto the parking area
- into a lay-by

text: When overtaking, what do you have to observe regarding spacing?
explanation: When overtaking, you must ensure that you have sufficient lateral distance to other road users: at least 1 meter to cars, trucks, buses, trams. For pedestrians and cyclists, the minimum distance is 1.5 meters. When we go back into lane you must not cut in on the driver you just overtook. (Check: Is he visible in the rearview mirror?)
options: Maintain an adequate space to the side, particularly between the vehicle and persons
To maintain an adequate space to the side between the vehicle and other road users
To maintain a greater side spacing towards multi-lane vehicles than towards single-lane vehicles

text: How can you tell if a horse-drawn carriage wants to change direction?
explanation: When a horse-drawn carriage wants to change its driving direction, it can be recognized by one of the following signs: The horse-drawn carriage indicates; the coachman beckons with his arm or with a signaling disk.
options: The driver extends his arm
A traffic paddle is displayed
A flashing indicator

text: You want to overtake a horse-drawn carriage on a rural road. What should you do?
explanation: Drive past the horses at an appropriate speed and with as much distance as possible. The animals may be frightened by sudden and loud noises such as a car horn or high engine speed, and may bolt. Therefore, avoid noise and proximity.
options: - as little noise as possible
- the most space to the side as possible
- a high engine speed

text: You want to overtake a horse-drawn carriage on a rural road. What should you do?
explanation: If you want to overtake a horse-drawn carriage on a country road, you must do the following: Avoid unnecessary noise such as honking or driving at high engine speeds so as not to scare the horses. Pay attention to the hand gestures of the coachman, as he can assess the behavior of his horses. Keep a safe distance.
options: I maintain the most space to the side possible
I pay attention to the driver's hand signals
I overtake with a high engine speed

text: You are driving a slow-moving vehicle on a rural road. A line of vehicles is forming behind you. What should you do?
explanation: A long queue behind a slow-moving vehicle leads to dangerous overtaking maneuvers. To make overtaking easier for the vehicles jamming behind you, reduce your speed. If the queue still does not disappear, you may need to stop on a side strip. This does not apply to highways! You must not use the hazard lights.
options: I allow the vehicles behind me to overtake
I come to a stop at a suitable place, if this is the only way the vehicles behind me can overtake
I switch on my hazard lights and drive as far to the right as possible

text: You want to overtake a horse-drawn carriage on a rural road. What is the right course of action?
explanation: When overtaking a carriage, you must pay attention to hand signals from the coachman, who may give you separate instructions. Carriages should always be overtaken at a safe distance so as not to frighten the horse.
options: I look for hand signals from the driver indicating he wants to turn off
I maintain a sufficient amount of distance when pulling in again
I maintain the smallest possible side clearance

text: What amount of side clearance must you maintain when overtaking pedestrians and cyclists?
explanation: To protect cyclists and pedestrians, you must keep a distance of at least 1.5 metres to the side in built-up areas and at least 2 metres outside built-up areas.
options: - maintain a minimum side clearance of 1.5 m within a built-up area
- maintain a minimum side clearance of 2.0 m outside of a built-up area
- maintain a minimum side clearance of 1.0 m within a built-up area

text: What must you note when overtaking the cyclists in this situation?
explanation:
When overtaking in built-up areas, you must maintain a distance of at least 1.5 metres to the side of the cyclist. 
Due to the commuting of cyclists, a larger minimum distance is recommended.
options: The incline causes the cyclists to sway
I must overtake with at least 1.5 m of side clearance
I must overtake with at least 1.0 m of side clearance

text: What is the correct course of action in this situation?
explanation: The driving lane line is solid. Therefore, overtaking is forbidden here.
options: I remain behind [the cyclist]
I overtake [the cyclist] with a sufficient amount of side clearance
I have to allow [the pedestrian] to cross the road

text: Which vehicle must wait when half the roadway is closed because of roadworks?
explanation: If you want to drive past a parked car or a barrier on your side of the street, you must give priority to oncoming traffic, no matter how large the vehicle.
options: The vehicle on the side of the roadway where the roadworks are
The vehicle on the unobstructed side of the roadway
Always the smaller vehicle

text: Who must wait?
explanation: If you want to drive past a parked car or a barrier on the left side of the road, you must give priority to vehicles that meet you.
options: I must wait
The oncoming vehicle must wait

text: Why should you drive especially slowly here?
explanation: In front of you, a standing truck narrows the road. The view of traffic is limited. In front of the truck, pedestrians cross the street, which you may perceive too late, as their view is also blocked. Therefore, avoid the obstacle very slowly and carefully.
options: - the truck is narrowing the lane
- people are proceeding onto the road
- I am approaching a traffic light junction

text: What is the right course of action?
explanation: You want to drive around the vehicles parked on the right side of the road. But that is only possible when the oncoming cyclist has passed you by. Otherwise you would not be able to maintain the necessary lateral distance and therefore have to wait.
options: Wait, because otherwise there would not be enough space between the cyclist and the car
Continue driving at a moderate speed, because there is very little space between the cyclist and the car
Continue driving as before, because there is sufficient space between the cyclist and the car

text: What should you do now?
explanation: Your visibility is limited by the van and you cannot tell if vehicles are coming towards you. Before driving on, make sure that there is no oncoming traffic approaching. You have to wait, because the construction site is on your lane.
options: - if it is clear that there is no oncoming traffic
- so as not to impede the way of possible oncoming traffic
- because any possible oncoming traffic must already be waiting

text: What is the correct course of action in this situation?
explanation: You wait until the oncoming motorcyclist has passed, as the obstacle is on your half of the lane.
options: I wait until the oncoming road user has driven past me
I take priority before the oncoming road user
The oncoming road user and I agree on who takes priority

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: What must you remember when you want to change lanes?
explanation: Turn the turn signal on and make sure that you do not endanger other road users before you start to change lanes. Do not brake abruptly. If there are vehicles on the roadway that you want to change to, you have to wait for a sufficiently large gap in the traffic.
options: You must signal your intention to change lanes in time
You must pay attention to the traffic following behind
You must always brake heavily before changing lanes

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: On a road with several lanes in one direction, one of the lanes ends ahead. You are driving on the lane which is coming to an end. What should you do?
explanation: If there is an obstacle on a road or if a multi-lane road narrows, then zip merging applies to all vehicles traveling in the same direction. Drive to the end of your lane. Do not change lanes earlier to prevent tailback. Wait here until a vehicle on the adjacent lane lets you enter.
options: Only move over just before the road starts to narrow by following the zipper feed-in method
Move into the through lane immediately after you see the first sign indicating that the road will narrow
Always be the first to move over into the through lane

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: What do you do in a tunnel with oncoming traffic?
explanation: In a tunnel with oncoming traffic, you must behave as follows: Orient yourself on the right side of the road and avoid looking directly into the light of oncoming traffic. You must not drive over or turn on the road edge marking. If necessary, increase the safety distance, drive anticipatory and pay attention to restriction on overtaking.
options: Do not drive over the lane boundary markings
Do not make a U-turn
Drive over the lane boundary markings when overtaking

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: What is the correct course of action in this situation?
explanation: You drive as close as possible to the barrier and only change to the right-hand lane after about 200 m. You may overtake all vehicles in the right-hand lane.
options: I move over to the right-hand lane after around 200 m
I may overtake the vehicles driving in the right-hand lane
I move into the right-hand lane now

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: In what situations is the alternate merging procedure to be used?
explanation: If the road narrows or if there is an obstacle on it so that a lane ends, zipper merging applies. It does not apply to acceleration lanes of slip roads. Here you have to wait.
options: When lanes come to an end
If lanes are not continuously free to traffic due to an obstacle
Where merging lanes join

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: A lane terminates on a road with several lanes heading in the same direction. What should you do when driving on the through-lane?
explanation: You must allow the driver, who is prevented from continuing to drive on the terminating lane, to safely change to the adjacent lane. It is mandatory that the vehicles of the ending lane and the vehicles on the continuous lane alternately merge into the lane immediately before the beginning of the lane narrowing. This is called zipper merging.
options: - allow traffic on the terminating lane to merge in accordance with the alternate merging procedure
- drive past the vehicles on the terminating lane
- make eye-contact and then decide according to the situation

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: You want to continue driving straight ahead. What should you do?
explanation: If a lane ends, vehicles should only merge into the lane right before the beginning of the constriction. This should be done alternately: Each vehicle from the continuing lane lets a vehicle from the ending lane go into the lane. This is called zipper merging. Practically, vehicles often go into the lane themselves too early out of fear of not being let in, thus narrowing the lane earlier than necessary.
options: I change lanes just before the narrowing of the road
I move into the right-hand lane now

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: You want to turn right at the junction. What should you do?
explanation: You would have to switch to the right lane, that is blocked by the waiting vehicles. Thus, you would hinder other road users on their lane while waiting. Therefore, you better avoid turning here.
options: I refrain from turning right, and remain in my lane
I steer clearly to the right, in order to create a space in the right-hand lane
I wait until all the vehicles have passed by, and then I move into the right-hand lane

text: You want to turn left. When must you check for traffic behind?
explanation: If you want to turn left, you must indicate this in a first step by pressing the direction-indictor control in order to make it clear for the follow-up traffic. Both before merge into the lane and immediately before the turn, you should make sure that the follow-up traffic has registered your intention by looking into the rearview mirror and looking over the shoulder.
options: Before getting into lane and again immediately before turning
Only once before turning

text: Two vehicles are approaching each other. Both want to turn left. What must they do as a rule?
explanation: Oncoming vehicles, each of which want to turn left from their direction of travel, have to turn in front of each other. This traffic situation is called tangent turns. This is the required rule. There are exceptional situations at narrow intersections or intersections with safety islands, which allow a turn in a wider arc.
options: They turn in front of each other
They pass each other in a wide arc and turn behind each other

text: Two vehicles are approaching each other. Both want to turn left. In which cases are you not allowed to turn left in front of each other?
explanation: As a rule, you have to turn left before the oncoming vehicle (tangent turning). However, drive in a wide arc behind the other vehicle if this is prescribed by lane markings on the lane. If the driving style of the other vehicle driver indicates that he wants to turn behind you, you also have to do without a turn in front of each other.
options: When you notice that the approaching vehicle wanting to turn left wishes to turn behind your vehicle
When this is forbidden by lane markings
When the approaching vehicle wanting to turn left stops just before the middle of the crossroads

text: What is the right course of action?
explanation: If you want to turn left, you have to give the oncoming vehicles right of way. The oncoming vehicles have right of way, even cyclists.
options: I have to allow [the yellow vehicle] to pass through
I may make the turn before the [yellow vehicle]

text: What driving line should you maintain up to the left turn?
explanation: Left-turning drivers get themselves up to the middle of the roadway. The vehicle must not protrude into the lane of oncoming traffic and thereby hinder the flow of traffic. In one-way streets driving on the left lane side is allowed.
options: The right
The left

text: You want to turn left. When must you pay attention to the traffic following behind you?
explanation: When turning left, you should be aware of following traffic before turning and before merging.
options: Before selecting the appropriate lane
Before taking the turn
After taking the turn

text: Two vehicles approach one another at an intersection. Both vehicles want to turn left. In what exceptional case do they have to turn one after the other?
explanation: Always turn in front of each other. If the traffic situation or the design of the intersection, e.g. lane markings, requires it, you must turn one behind the other.
options: If the road traffic situation demands it
If the layout of the intersection demands it
If the vehicles are crossing over an equal priority intersection

text: Two vehicles approach one another at an intersection. Both vehicles want to turn left. What must both drivers do in the normal case?
explanation: If two left-turning vehicles come towards each other, they turn in front of each other (tangentially).
options: - turn in front of one another
- turn behind one another
- communicate with one another to agree the mode of turning

text: You want to turn left. What driving line should you maintain?
explanation: Use the right-hand driving line. The left-hand driving line is intended for oncoming traffic.
options: The right driving line
The left driving line
Both driving lines are possible

text: To which road user must you give way here?
explanation:
When turning, you must give priority to oncoming traffic and cross traffic - in this case cyclists and pedestrians.
Although your traffic lights are green, you must wait until the pedestrian has crossed the road. Pedestrians have priority over turning vehicles.
options: [The pedestrian]
[The cyclist]
The bus

text: You want to leave the roundabout at this exit. What is the right thing to do?
explanation:
When leaving the roundabout, crossing walkers and cyclists have priority.
You must therefore allow cyclists and walkers to cross the carriageway.
options: I must allow [the pedestrian] to cross the road
I must allow [the cyclist] to cross the road
I have priority over the road users crossing the road

text: You want to turn right here. What is correct?
explanation: You must let both pedestrians cross the road. They do not change their direction of movement and therefore have priority over you.
options: I have to let both [pedestrians] cross the road
I only have to let [the oncoming pedestrian] cross the road
I have right of way over both [pedestrians]

text: What can give rise to particularly dangerous situations where several lanes turn off?
explanation: Drive at moderate speed into multi-lane turns. At too fast a pace you could get out of your lane and get into the lane of parallel driving vehicles. Avoid a lane change within this turning situation. There is a risk that a vehicle is directly behind you in your blind spot.
options: Driving too fast
Changing lanes while performing the turn
Keeping exactly to your lane

text: All three vehicles want to turn left. Which is in the correct lane?
explanation: Only the yellow car merged into the lane correctly. He passed right, as it says on the road sign on the safety island, in order to then get in proper lane as left as possible to prepare his turn to the left. The green car is completely wrong on the rails; In this situation, the truck may only drive straight ahead or turn right.
options: The yellow car
The truck
The green car

text: After turning left, you want to turn immediately right. How should you position your vehicle?
explanation: If you want to turn right again immediately after turning left, you get in proper lane on the right, if there are two lanes for turning left. Otherwise, keep as far to the right as possible. This is the only way you can turn right after a left turn without hindering other road users.
options: - the red car
- the green car
- the blue car

text: Who must signal a change of direction here?
explanation: The change of direction must indicate who changes it. This is true regardless of the importance of the road. So, the motorcyclist who follows the course of the turning priority road has to indicate. You continue straight ahead and do not indicate.
options: The motorcycle
I myself
No one

text: You are on a roundabout. What should you remember?
explanation: In a roundabout you may only stop if this is unavoidable due to traffic, for example due to a traffic jam. Indicate when leaving the roundabout. You can only drive over paved or asphalted central islands if it is unavoidable due to the size of the vehicle. Always give priority to cyclists traveling on your right side and remaining in the roundabout.
options: You can only drive over a central island if this is unavoidable because of your vehicle's size
You are not allowed to stop on the roadway in a roundabout
You must indicate to leave the roundabout

text: In what situation is it especially dangerous to perform a turn?
explanation: When turning in poor visibility (fog), dangerous situations can arise. The same applies when turning in curves and before crests.
options: Before the crest of a hill
Before bends in the road
In foggy conditions

text: Who is required to indicate?
explanation: Changing the direction of travel must always be indicated by pressing the indicator. If you stay on a turning priority road you should also indicate that. Therefore, the blue truck must indicate. You, who's turning left, must also indicate.
options: Me
[The blue truck]
[The red car]

text: Who is required to indicate a change of driving direction here?
explanation: The change of the direction of travel must always be indicated early enough. All three drivers intend to turn. Therefore, all three vehicles must indicate.
options: Me
[The red car]
[The motorbike]

text: Who is required to indicate a change of driving direction here?
explanation: The intention to change the direction of travel must be announced at an early stage by indicating. You follow the turning priority road; this change of direction needs to be indicated.
options: Me
The oncoming [car]

text: When do have you to indicate a change in direction?
explanation: If you want to turn into a T-junction or a property, you have to indicate. The same applies if you follow a turning priority road - here, too, the change of the direction of travel must be indicated.
options: Before turning into a junction or a property lot
If I want to continue following a priority road that changes direction
If I want to continue straight on, thereby leaving a priority road that changes direction

text: Why are you required to stop now?
explanation: Drivers who turn need to wait for vehicles from the opposite direction, even for cyclists. The red car has to wait until the green car and the cyclist are gone.
options: - cyclist
- green vehicle
- red vehicle

text: You want to turn left. In what sequence do you prepare to take the left turn?
explanation: If you want to turn left, prepare the turn in the following order: 1. look, 2. indicate, 3. arrange. Looking means that you are observing follow-up traffic in the mirror and over your shoulder. Then press the indicator to the left side. Only if you can rule out danger for other road users, you may merge left in order to turn.
options: Observe traffic behind you, indicate the direction of turn, enter the lane
Indicate the direction of turn, enter the lane, observe traffic behind you
Enter the lane, indicate the direction of turn, observe traffic behind you

text: What is the right course of action?
explanation: In front of the traffic sign "Stop! Give way!", colloquially also called stop sign, you must always stop. Mostly there is a stop line. The wheels must be stationary for at least a short amount of time. The cross traffic has right of way - then the cyclists on the opposite side. As a driver turning left, you have to grant him the right of way.
options: I have to wait at the stop line
I have to allow the cyclist to pass through
I may make the turn in front of the cyclist

text: How should you behave?
explanation: Turning drivers generally have to wait for oncoming vehicles. These include cyclists. Cyclists who drive in their own direction on or next to the lane you also need to let pass.
options: Give way to both cyclists
Only give way to the cyclist travelling in the same direction
Sound your horn and take the turn before the two cyclists

text: You want to turn left. To whom must you give priority?
explanation: The oncoming traffic when turning left, has always right of way. This also applies to cyclists; they are granted priority. If pedestrians cross the street you want to turn into, the pedestrians have priority too.
options: Oncoming cyclists
Oncoming vehicles
Pedestrians seeking to cross the road into which I am turning

text: You want to turn left. What difficulties could arise here?
explanation: When turning left, vehicles approaching each other have to turn in front of each other (tangent turning). This can lead to poor visibility of the straight-ahead traffic. Especially left-turning trucks can lead to massive obstructions and make it safer to turn in a wide arc (turning behind each other). There may be misunderstandings between drivers when one wants to turn behind and the other in front.
options: Visibility restrictions caused by oncoming vehicles
Misunderstandings with oncoming traffic turning left
Traffic turning left can come dangerously close

text: Why are you required to stop now?
explanation: You are on a priority road and therefore you're allowed to drive before the white car coming from the right. However, as a driver who wants to turn, you have a subordinate position to traffic driving straight-ahead, in this case the tram. You have to stop.
options: Because of the tram
Because of the cyclist
Because of the white car

text: What is the right course of action here?
explanation: You must not overtake the moped before the level crossing. In general, no vehicles may be overtaken at level crossings from signs 151, 156 to the rails.
options: - not overtake the moped before the rail crossing
- overtake the moped, while allowing sufficient space to the side
- overtake the moped before the rail crossing once the cyclist is out of the way

text: Why are you required to brake now?
explanation: The motorcyclist comes from the left at high speed. He probably did not see you because of the oncoming vehicle. Although you have the right of way, you have to slow down, as otherwise an accident will occur.
options: Because of the motorbike
Because of the van
Because of the cyclist

text: Why do you have to wait before turning right?
explanation: If you want to turn, you must give priority to road users traveling straight ahead. In this case, you have lower priority to the pedestrian and the cyclist and must allow them a safe crossing.
options: Because of [the pedestrian]
Because of [the cyclist]
Because of [the black car]
