The traffic sign means “Entry prohibited”. Driving into the signposted area is therefore prohibited.

text: What do you do when you see this traffic sign?
explanation: The road is too narrow for two lanes. The traffic sign regulates the right of way. The oncoming traffic is granted priority. If you are met by vehicles, you must stop early and allow oncoming traffic to pass.
options: You must give precedence to oncoming traffic
You are not allowed to turn
You take precedence over oncoming traffic

text: In which directions are you allowed to continue?
explanation: The traffic sign "You" only allows turning to the right or left" only allows you to turn left or right. The desired direction of travel needs to be indicated. You are not allowed to drive straight ahead.
options: To the left
To the right
Straight ahead

text: A school bus is stopping on the roadway approximately 80 m in front of you. Can this be dangerous?
explanation: If a school bus stops in front of you on the road about 80 m away, you have to expect the following: Children could suddenly run on/off the road to reach the bus, for example, by the shortest route. This danger exists even if school crossing guards secure the traffic. You have to be ready to brake and you are only allowed to drive past the school bus at walking speed.
options: Yes, because children frequently run across the road to catch the bus
Yes, because children do not always take the shortest route to cross the roadway
No, because school crossing patrols regulate traffic at every school bus stop

text: Who is allowed to drive a motor vehicle on this road?
explanation: The street is a declared sidewalk, with the additional sign "delivery vehicles only". Therefore, this road may only be used by a distributor with a motor vehicle. The distributor must be able to prove that he has to deliver something in this street. He has to drive at walking speed, regardless of whether or not pedestrians pass the street. He has to take care of pedestrians.
options: Persons delivering goods
Shoppers
Visitors

text: Which vehicles are allowed to use the special lane marked like this?
explanation: The lane shown here is intended for public buses. Only they are allowed to use this lane. For all other drivers the use of this lane is prohibited.
options: Regular buses
Trucks
Cars

text: Who is allowed to enter a street sign-posted like this?
explanation: The additional sign indicates that drivers who have to go on errands in this street privately, or for business reasons may enter. Residents and visitors are customers of shops, patients of medical practices as well as people who live in this street and their visitors. Through traffic is prohibited in this street.
options: Residents
People visiting residents
Through-traffic

text: Which vehicles are not allowed to use a road sign-posted like this?
explanation: Cars, but also other multi-lane motor vehicles, may not drive on a road with this sign. These include cars, trucks and buses. The ban does not apply to motorcycles, including side cars, and non-motorized vehicles.
options: Trucks
Cars
Motorcycles

text: Which vehicles are not allowed to use a road sign-posted like this?
explanation: This round road sign with the red border prohibits the passage for cyclists. It usually can be found on roads where you are allowed to drive fast and where a cyclist can get into dangerous situations due to his or her low speed. Motorized vehicles such as motorcycles and cars may continue here.
options: Bicycles
Motorcycles
Cars

text: Which vehicles are not allowed to use a road sign-posted like this?
explanation: A round traffic sign with a red border indicates a general traffic ban for vehicles. If the circle contains a symbol, the types of vehicles to which the traffic ban applies are specified more precisely. Here the road may not be used by motorcyclists.
options: Motorcycles
Cars
Trucks

text: What do these traffic signs indicate?
explanation: The traffic sign "Do not enter" forbids car drivers to enter this road with vehicles of all kinds. The additional sign makes it clear that this prohibition applies only in 100 meters. It does not explicitly state for how long. Always expect that vehicles can come out of this road.
options: No entry 100 m ahead
A one-way street 100 m long
A customs post 100 m ahead

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: The traffic sign indicates the beginning of a zone with a maximum speed of 30 km/h. It is often set up in residential areas and only once at the beginning. You are not allowed to drive faster than 30 km / h in the entire area. This speed limit is canceled with the "End of the 30 km/h zone" sign.
options: - a permitted maximum speed of 30 km/h
- an obligatory minimum speed of 30 km/h
- a recommended speed of 30 km/h

text: A traffic calmed commercial zone (verkehrsberuhigter Bereich) starts here. What must you do?
explanation: In a traffic calming zone with shops, road users are often distracted by the displays in the shop windows. You must therefore pay attention to rain and inattentive foot traffic. Your maximum speed is 20 km/h. This is a no parking, but waiting allowed zone and you're obliged to use your parking disc. To offer parking to many customers, the maximum parking time is two hours.
options: You must specifically watch out for busy pedestrian traffic
You must pay attention to the allowed maximum parking time
You must observe a minimum speed of 20 km/h

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign indicates the end of an area in which the permitted speed was set to 30 km/h and thus cancels the maximum speed of 30 km/h.
options: - a permitted maximum speed of 30 km/h
- an obligatory minimum speed of 30 km/h
- a recommended speed of 30 km/h

text: Are you allowed to drive at a speed faster than 60 km/h here?
explanation: Due to the additional sign, the maximum permissible speed of 60 km/h applies only in wet conditions. Decrease the speed of your vehicle accordingly, if the entire roadway is covered with a thin film of water and therefore counts as wet. If the road is dry or only damp, you are also allowed to drive faster than 60 km/h as a car driver.
options: Yes, if the roadway is dry
Yes, if the roadway is wet

text: What do you do when you see this traffic sign?
explanation: This traffic sign dictates that you have to drive here at least at a speed of 60 km/h. Driving slower is only allowed if traffic safety requires it. A car driver may not use this road if he/she cannot or is not allowed to drive that fast due to the vehicle or its load or due to lack of personal abilities.
options: You must drive at least at a speed of 60 km/h, weather and traffic conditions permitting
You may not use this road if you cannot or are not allowed to drive at least 60 km/h
You are not allowed to drive faster than 60 km/h

text: Which vehicles are you allowed to overtake where you see this traffic sign?
explanation: The restriction on overtaking prohibits a car driver from overtaking multi-lane vehicles such as cars, trucks or tractors and motorcycles with side cars. Motorcycles without a side car and bicycles are allowed to be overtaken, as these are single-lane vehicles.
options: Motorcycle without sidecar
Motorcycle with sidecar
Car

text: What do these traffic signs indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign signals a restriction on overtaking on multi-lane motor vehicles or motorcycles with side car. The black arrows with the km indication indicate that the restriction on overtaking applies for 3 km. The restriction on overtaking comes into force starting from the traffic sign.
options: No overtaking for 3 km
Start of a no-overtaking area 3 km ahead
Roadway with two lanes in one direction for 3 km

text: What do these traffic signs indicate?
explanation: With this traffic sign the car driver is prohibited to overtake multi-lane vehicles and motorcycles with side car. The additional sign prohibits overtaking in 200 meters. Since it contains no black arrows, it does not mean that you are not allowed to overtake in the next 200 meters.
options: Start of a no-overtaking area 200 m ahead
No overtaking for 200 m
End of a no-overtaking area 200 m ahead

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign indicates the end of the speed limit of 60 km/h. The car driver may drive at the usual speed again.
options: End of speed restriction
A prohibition to drive faster than 60 km/h
Start of speed restriction

text: Which prohibitions cease to apply when you see this sign?
explanation: This traffic sign cancels all road restrictions. For example, road restrictions include restrictions on overtaking and speed limits. Stopping restrictions such as a parking ban are not covered by road restrictions.
options: No overtaking
Speed restrictions
No parking

text: What do these traffic signs indicate?
explanation: The traffic sign signals the car driver that it is forbidden to come to a stop on the road. The additional sign extends the stopping restriction and also prohibits stopping on the side strip for all vehicles, not just for trucks.
options: - on the roadway and the hard shoulder
- on the hard shoulder only
- for trucks only

text: What is allowed in the zone which starts here?
explanation: With the traffic sign "No parking. Waiting is allowed.", there is a restricted stopping ban in an entire area without stopping signs being placed here in certain streets. As a car driver, you are allowed to wait up to three minutes throughout the entire zone. Situations of loading and unloading or getting in and out of the car may also take longer.
options: Stopping for up to 3 minutes
Stopping for loading or unloading as well as boarding or alighting
Parking, provided a parking disc is used

text: What ends here?
explanation: Here the no parking zone ends. Note that this traffic sign is often only on placed on the left side of the road and does not suspend the stopping restriction.
options: A no-waiting area
A no-stopping area
All previous zonal prohibitions

text: When must you indicate?
explanation: If you enter the roundabout, you do not need to indicate this because the entrance to the circle is always to the right. On the other hand, if you leave the roundabout, you will need to indicate this to make it easier for other drivers to enter the circle.
options: When you leave the roundabout
When you enter the roundabout

text: You are approaching this combination of traffic signs. What must you remember?
explanation: Vehicles driving in the roundabout have right of way. Indicating when entering the roundabout is not necessary, as a roundabout is always entered from the right. Therefore, the answer "Entering the roundabout must be indicated" is wrong. You only indicate when you leave a roundabout. This makes sense because this makes it easier for vehicles to enter the roundabout.
options: Vehicles in the roundabout have priority
You must indicate to leave the roundabout
You must indicate when entering the roundabout

text: What does this traffic sign mean?
explanation: You have to give priority to the vehicles driving in the roundabout. In the roundabout there is always an absolute stopping restriction. You only indicate when you leave a roundabout. This helps other cars to enter the roundabout. A general driving with walking speed in the roundabout is not required.
options: Stopping on the roundabout is forbidden
You must indicate when entering the roundabout
You are only allowed to drive at walking speed

text: What does this traffic sign mean?
explanation: The traffic signs indicate that the drivers in the roundabout have priority. They also show that you do not need to indicate when entering the roundabout, as motorists can only enter the circle to the right. As soon as you leave the roundabout, you will need to indicate that to make it easier for other road users to enter the roundabout.
options: You must give way to vehicles in the roundabout
You must indicate when leaving the roundabout
You must indicate when entering the roundabout

text: What must you do when you see this combination of traffic signs?
explanation: When driving in, you must give priority to the vehicles in that are already in the roundabout. The circle may only be entered through the right. You only indicate when leaving the roundabout. This regulation makes it easier for drivers to enter the roundabout. When recognizing the turn signal, they can decide whether they can already enter the circle with due regard for due diligence.
options: You must indicate right to leave the roundabout
When entering the roundabout, you must give way
You must enter to the left

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign identifies a cycle path that cyclists must use but is prohibited for other road users. Cyclists crossing the road have their own warning sign.
options: A mandatory cycle path
A "cyclists prohibited" zone
Cyclists crossing the carriageway

text: What does this traffic sign combination indicate?
explanation: The traffic sign announces that after a hundred meters you will find a priority road where you will find the traffic sign "Give way". In any case, you must stop there at the stop line or line of sight.
options: - "Stop. Give way."
- "Give way."
- "Give way to oncoming traffic"

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: The traffic sign "Footway" marks paths which may be used exclusively by pedestrians and cyclists up to 10 years. Car drivers, cyclists and other road users may not be traveling on these routes. However, exceptions may be regulated by additional signs.
options: A footpath
A prohibition on cycles and mopeds
The start of a traffic-calming zone

text: What vehicles are permitted to use this road?
explanation: The traffic sign "No vehicles of any kind permitted" includes all vehicles. Only motor bicycles such as motorcycles and scooters and bicycles may be pushed here.
options: Cycles and motorcycles that are pushed
Motor vehicles
Electric-powered vehicles

text: How must you act when driving a vehicle during permitted delivery times?
explanation: Since the traffic sign "Footway" is combined here with the additional sign "Delivery vehicles only", a distributor may drive on a road that is marked this way. You have to drive at walking speed, regardless of whether pedestrians are visible or not. Pedestrians have priority, you should be especially considerate of them.
options: I may only drive at walking speed
I must keep a close look out for pedestrians
If there are no pedestrians in my vicinity, I may drive faster than walking speed

text: What must you do upon seeing this traffic sign?
explanation: This traffic sign indicates the prohibition to turn in order to drive in the opposite direction. Turning left, however, is allowed. This traffic sign does not only apply to dead ends.
options: I may not perform a U-turn here
I am in a cul-de-sac and have to turn around
I may not turn left here

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: Starting from these traffic signs a maximum of 60 km/h may be driven, regardless of the weather conditions. In bad weather conditions, the speed must be reduced further. However, the traffic sign does not say that 60 km/h must always be driven in order to stay safe. There is no traffic sign for a recommended minimum speed.
options: I may not drive faster than 60 km/h
There is absolutely no problem in driving at 60 km/h
The recommended minimum speed is 60 km/h

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign means "You must go straight ahead". You can only drive straight ahead and are not allowed to turn. The one-way street sign has the same colors but is rectangular.
options: I may only drive straight ahead
I have priority over oncoming traffic
I am on a one-way road

text: What do you do upon seeing this traffic sign?
explanation: The traffic signal "Give way" signals that you are driving on a subordinate road and the cross traffic has priority. Drive slowly and stay ready to brake so that you do not miss a vehicle that is entitled to drive.
options: I approach at a moderate speed ready to brake
I allow the cross-wise moving traffic the right of way
If I am turning right, I am not obliged to wait

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign shows you a riding path. Here riders move with their horses. Other road users are not allowed to use this path.
options: A bridle-path, which riders are required to use
A bridle-path, which may not be used by other road users
A path, which may not be used by riders

text: What must you do upon seeing this traffic sign?
explanation: The sign "Stop! Yield to cross traffic" requires you to stop and thereby slow down the vehicle to a complete stop. It doesn't matter if there is a stop line or if cross traffic is coming.
options: - stop and give way
- stop only if there is a stop line
- stop only if there is cross-wise moving traffic

text: What do you have to do in this traffic situation?
explanation: At the traffic sign "Stop! Yield to cross traffic" you have to stop and give way. You always have to stop, even if there is no cross traffic. Since there is no stop line, stop at the line of sight. From the line of sight, you can see the street you want to enter.
options: - stop at the line of sight and give way
- not stop, because there is no stop line
- stop only if there is cross-wise moving traffic

text: What do you have to do in this traffic situation?
explanation: The traffic sign "Stop! Yield to cross traffic!" requires that you stop and give way. Since there is a stop line, you must stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, you must stop at the line of sight and your wheels have to stop completely. You always have to stop, even if there is no cross traffic.
options: - stop at the stop line and give way
- stop only at the stop sign
- stop only if there is cross-wise moving traffic

text: You are driving along a priority road. Which traffic sign ends your right of way?
explanation: Example 1 means "Yield", you must give priority to other road users. Sign 2 grants you right of way at the next intersection. Sign 3 only warns of a danger zone.

text: What do you have to be aware of with this traffic sign?
explanation: This traffic sign regulates the direction of travel. You may only turn left here. The change of the direction of travel must be indicated.
options: I have to signal a left-turn
I may only continue driving by taking a left turn
I may not signal

text: What applies with this traffic sign?
explanation: This traffic sign prescribes from which side you have to circuit the obstacle. You can find the regulation sign at central, stop islands or construction sites. If you meet the sign at an intersection or T-junction, you may turn in the appropriate direction.
options: I have to drive past obstructions on the left
I am obliged to turn left
I may not turn right before the sign

text: What applies in the area 15 m in front of and behind this traffic sign?
explanation: At the traffic sign you can see that there is a tram or bus stop here. 15 meters before and after the traffic sign, drivers are not allowed to park their vehicles. Unless public transport is impeded or passengers are endangered, waiting is allowed for up to three minutes.
options: - stop
- not obstruct passengers boarding or alighting
- park

text: What applies with this traffic sign?
explanation: The given direction of travel is binding. The car driver must turn right before the traffic sign and indicate this process to other road users.
options: I have to signal a right-turn
I may only continue driving by taking a right turn
I may also continue driving by taking a left turn

text: What applies with this traffic sign?
explanation: The traffic sign indicates a taxi stand. There is basically a stopping restriction for all other vehicles. The car driver must always expect departing and arriving taxis and passengers in this area.
options: I have to anticipate taxi moving off and coming to a stop
I may stop
I may park

text: What does this traffic sign combination indicate?
explanation: This sign means "Danger zone" and the additional sign stands for "Winter sports allowed". The combination indicates that winter sportspersons may use the road and road users must pay particular attention to it.
options: - may be used by winter sports enthusiasts
- may not be used by traffic in winter
- may only be used with snow chains

text: What do you have to be aware of in this traffic situation?
explanation: You must not drive over the lane boundary (solid line) to the left, which is located at the middle of the lane. Driving on it is also prohibited.
options: - not cross the lane marking
- cross the lane marking in order to overtake
- cross the lane marking if oncoming traffic permits this

text: What must you be aware of on this priority road?
explanation: The solid line in the middle between the two lanes prohibits crossing or crossing this line. It also prohibits parking on priority roads outside of built-up areas.
options: Parking is prohibited
You may not cross the lane marking
Parking is permitted if there is a clear space of at least 3 m between a parked car and the lane marking

text: You want to overtake. What is the right thing to do?
explanation: You may overtake if other road users are not endangered. The one-sided lane boundary allows you to cross the two lines from the side where the broken line is located.
options: - overtake
- not overtake
- only overtake, if I remain in the right-hand lane while doing so

text: As a resident, you want to drive into a cycle highway that has this sign. What must you be aware of when doing so?
explanation: A maximum speed of 30 km/h applies to traffic. Cycling traffic must not be endangered or obstructed. If necessary, motor vehicle traffic must reduce speed further. Side-by-side cycling is permitted.
options: Vehicles may not be driven faster than 30 km/h
Cycles may travel alongside one another
Cycle traffic may not be impeded

text: Who may enter a street that has this sign?
explanation: Vehicular traffic other than cyclists may not use cycle lanes unless permitted by additional sign. The additional sign allows residents to enter the bicycle lane.
options: All cyclists
All persons visiting residents
All moped riders

text: This road traffic sign is displayed for your lane. What must you be aware of?
explanation: This traffic sign indicates the prescribed minimum speed. You must therefore drive at least 60 km/h, provided that the road and traffic conditions allow it.
options: I must drive at a minimum speed of 60 km/h, if permitted by the road and traffic conditions
I may only use this lane if my vehicle can and is allowed to drive at a speed of least 60 km/h
I may not drive faster than 60 km/h

text: What is the maximum speed a vehicle may drive in a zone with this sign?
explanation: Cyclists, light electric vehicles and other authorized vehicles may not drive more than 30 km/h in bicycle zones.

text: What situation applies according to this traffic sign?
explanation: The additional sign limits the speed limit between 10 pm and 6 am.
options: - applies between 10 pm and 6 am
- applies between 6 am and 10 pm
- does not apply to electric vehicles

text: What should you do when you see this road sign?
explanation:
The arrow on this traffic sign always shows the direction of travel. If it is a straight arrow, you have to turn in front of the sign. If it is a curved arrow, you must turn according to the sign. 
You have to flash to indicate the change in driving direction.
options: - indicate left
- turn left before the traffic sign
- turn left behind the traffic sign

text: Which road sign indicates that turning around is not allowed?
explanation:
All traffic signs show you that turning is prohibited.

The traffic sign tells you that a tunnel begins here. Turning is strictly prohibited in the tunnel.

The traffic sign “Turning Prohibited” shows you that turning is prohibited here.

This traffic sign tells you that you are on a highway. U-turns are strictly prohibited on the highway.

text: From which road sign onwards may you not exceed a permissible maximum speed of 60 km/h?
explanation:
Traffic signs with a red border generally indicate a ban.
On a road with such a traffic sign you are not allowed to exceed the maximum permitted speed of 60 km/h.

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign grants you priority in a specific place. Thus, the right of way for the driver is limited and has no general validity.
options: - only at the next crossroads or junction
- at all crossroads and junctions on this road
- as far as the urban limit

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: The traffic sign indicates that the motorway starts here. This also gives effect to all the rules that apply to this particular type of road.
options: The start of an autobahn
The end of an autobahn
The start of a clearway for motor vehicles only

text: What do the white markings on the road mean in this situation?
explanation: At intersections and junctions with “right before left” regulation, especially in confusing places, are also used by waiting lines. Wartelinia are often used that look as similar to many small way to go-along.
options: - highlight a duty to give-way due to the right-before-left rule
- indicate a traffic-calming zone
- are a warning about the poor state of the road surface

text: What is the rule created by the road markings in this situation?
explanation:
You have to nourish yourself this intersection carefully, as it applies right to the left.
At intersections and junctions with “right before left” regulation, especially in confusing places, are also used by waiting lines. Wartelinia are often used that look as similar to many small way to go-along.
options: - approach the junction cautiously
- give way to the [red vehicle]
- come to a stop in front of the road markings

text: From which road sign onwards are you only allowed to drive at walking speed?
explanation: In a traffic-calmed area, you may only drive your vehicle at walking speed, as you must expect pedestrians or children playing at any time.

text: At which traffic sign at the next junction do you generally have right of way?
explanation: The traffic sign “One-time right of way” signals to you that you have the right of way at the next intersection or junction. However, this sign has no effect on the intersection after that.

text: Which traffic sign gives right of way at the next crossroads?
explanation: Only the first traffic sign gives you right of way at the next intersection. The second traffic sign, however, indicates the end of the priority road and traffic sign number three regulates the right of way at a bottleneck.
options: Traffic sign 1
Traffic sign 2
Traffic sign 3

text: Which traffic sign gives right of way?
explanation: The correct traffic sign to observe the right of way is number two. Number one indicates that a dangerous turn is in front of the driver while number three indicates the number of a national highway.
options: Traffic sign 2
Traffic sign 1
Traffic sign 3

text: What is allowed on priority roads outside built-up areas?
explanation: On priority roads outside of built-up areas, you may: 1. wait at the right side of the road; 2. park on a hard shoulder. On the other hand, parking on the road is prohibited. Parking vehicles constitute a hindrance and/or danger to flowing traffic, since vehicles are traveling much faster here than within the closed local area. Since a hard shoulder is not considered a lane, you may use it for parking. If there is a possibility to dodge on a hard shoulder, you should also use this for waiting shortly.
options: Stopping on the right edge of the roadway
Parking on the hard shoulder
Parking on the roadway

text: What ends here?
explanation: This traffic sign announces the change of a priority rule. It marks the end of the previous priority route. The signs "Give way" and "Stop! Give way!" that you can find on intersections and T-junctions, have a similar meaning.
options: A priority road
A controlled parking zone
All previous zonal prohibitions

text: What do you do when you see this traffic sign?
explanation: The traffic sign gives you priority over oncoming traffic. The oncoming traffic is obliged to wait in front of the obstacle. Nevertheless, you must prepare for stopping when oncoming traffic is already in the bottleneck. You have to let those drivers drive out. You may proceed with right of way if the bottleneck is free.
options: You may only take precedence when the narrowing is clear
You must be ready to stop despite taking precedence
You must give precedence to the oncoming traffic

text: What do these traffic signs allow?
explanation: This traffic sign indicates a parking lot that may only be used by residents with a correspondingly numbered parking pass. Other road users are not allowed to park there and have to switch to other parking places.
options: Residents holding a parking licence with corresponding number may park here
All residents may use any of these parking spaces
Everybody may use this parking space as long as other parking spaces are still free

text: Are you allowed to park here?
explanation: There are special parking spaces for people with impaired mobility or the blind. An official parking permit identifies the vehicles of these persons or their escorts. Even short parking on these areas is forbidden to other drivers.
options: Yes, as a seriously disabled person with an official parking permit
Yes, as a person accompanying blind persons with an official parking permit
Yes, briefly for shopping

text: What must you observe when parking here?
explanation: In this parking lot you are only allowed to park with a valid ticket. Attach the parking ticket legibly behind the front or rear window of your car. Be sure not to exceed the parking time stated on the ticket. The parking disc does not replace the parking ticket: the parking disc is only valid if the parking meter is out of operation.
options: The parking time indicated on the parking ticket may not be exceeded
The parking ticket must be put in a place so it can be easily read when controlled
Parking ticket and parking disc rank equal

text: Which vehicles are allowed to park here?
explanation: The traffic sign regulates the parking situation for the road user. The sign allows parking partly on the sidewalk, the side strip and on the green verge for vehicles up to a total weight of 2.8 tons.
options: Vehicles with a permissible total mass of up to 2.8 t
Motorcycles
Vehicles with a permissible total mass of more than 3.5 t

text: What must a motor vehicle's maximum speed, determined by its construction, be at least if you want to use this road?
explanation: You must be able to achieve at least a maximum speed of 60 km/h on a motor road with your vehicle. The beginning of a motor road is always marked by a traffic sign.
options: 61 km/h
51 km/h
81 km/h

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This is a dead end. You can drive normally in a dead end, but the road ends so you might have trouble to turn your car around to leave the street again.
options: A cul-de-sac
An underpass
A road closed to vehicle traffic

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign shows that a first aid station such as "Red Cross" or "Samaritan" is present at this point. However, it does not indicate any danger zone.
options: A first aid station
A crossroads
A danger spot

text: What must you remember when you see this traffic sign?
explanation: If you see this sign at lanterns, then you have to secure your vehicle with your parking light. Since these lanterns are not lit up all night, it's very unsafe to leave an unlit car here.
options: Street lighting does not stay on all night
Vehicles may be parked here all night without lights
Vehicles may not be parked here

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign refers to a main road. The number stands for the number of the respective federal highway and not for example for a speed limit.
options: A federal road (Bundesstraße)
Vehicles may not drive faster than 35 km/h
Vehicles must drive at least 35 km/h

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: The diversion arrow points out to you as a car driver that you are on a traffic jam-prone section of the motorway and points out an alternative route. But you are not obliged to follow this.
options: An autobahn section which is normally not used very much
The place where the autobahn must be exited
An obligatory diversion for vehicles with dangerous goods

text: During daylight, you enter a lit tunnel marked like this. What do you do?
explanation: As the car driver, you must turn on the low beam. The daytime lights are not enough, because the light conditions in the tunnel cannot be compared to daylight. You are obliged to make your vehicle seen.
options: I switch on the dipped headlights
I do not have to switch on the lights
I switch on the side lights

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign shows you an emergency lay-by. There you can and should wait if you have a breakdown. It's possible that there's already a vehicle there. For breaks an emergency lay-by may not be used.
options: There may be a vehicle in the next emergency bay
In case of breakdown, you should stop in the emergency bay indicated
You may stop here to have a break

text: What do you have to do when you see this traffic sign?
explanation: This traffic sign is located in front of the entrance to a tunnel. Turn on the low beam and remove sunglasses for unrestricted visibility.
options: Take off your sunglasses
Switch on dipped headlights
Switch on the hazard warning lights

text: You drive into a brightly lit tunnel which is indicated like this. What do you do?
explanation: Even a brightly lit tunnel cannot reach daylight conditions, so you need to drive in with low beam to make your vehicle recognizable. The daytime running light is simply not enough in this case.
options: Drive with dipped headlights
Drive without lights
Drive with daytime running lights

text: What does this traffic sign combination indicate?
explanation: The traffic sign points to the end of the traffic-calming zone. Now higher speed rules apply again. As a car driver, you have no right of way when you leave and must be careful when entering.
options: - a traffic-calming zone
- a pedestrian zone
- a children's playground

text: What does this traffic road sign mean?
explanation: You drive on a priority road. The traffic sign is repeated at each intersection or T-junction where you have priority. Outside built-up areas, parking on priority roads is prohibited. On these roads people drive relatively fast and parking vehicles would be a hindrance or a threat.
options: Priority road
No parking on the carriageway outside of settlements
Expressway

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign indicates a numbered detour. Since there are several detours, they are numbered. So, you know exactly where to drive.
options: A numbered diversion
Tram line no. 3
A numbered underground car park

text: What do you have to be aware of when you see this traffic sign combination?
explanation: The priority road is turning due to the additional sign. It's a turning priority road. If you stay on the priority road, you will need to indicate that. You have to take care of pedestrians crossing the street, if necessary, you have to stop. The answer: "Driving to the left is mandatory" is wrong, since this traffic sign does not dictate a direction of travel.
options: If I am following the priority road, I have to signal a left-turn
If I continue driving straight ahead, I have to signal a right-turn
The direction of traffic to the left is prescribed

text: What is the correct action on roads with these types of protective cycle lanes?
explanation: The directional sign indicates the safe area for cyclists. As the vehicle driver, you may only drive on the designated bicycle lane if a risk to cyclists is ruled out. Parking is strictly prohibited here.
options: - drive on the protective lanes when necessary, if there is no risk to cyclists
- in no event drive on the protective lanes
- use the protective lanes to assist parking

text: What must you do upon seeing this traffic sign?
explanation: On pedestrian crossings pedestrians have precedence, so vehicles should always drive at moderate speed and be ready to brake at any time. There's a strict restriction on overtaking at pedestrian crossings and with halting traffic it is forbidden to come to a stop at the crossing.
options: I must approach at a moderate speed if it is clear that pedestrians want to cross the road
I must allow the pedestrians to cross the road
I may not remain stationary on the pedestrian crossing if the traffic backs up

text: What must you be prepared for here?
explanation: The traffic sign 'crossing guard', formerly school crossing guards, means that traffic assistance regulates traffic. They are allowed to stop traffic to allow children to cross the road. You need to be prepared for the flow of traffic to stop and for children to walk on the road more often than usual.
options: That the flowing traffic will come to a stop
That children will cross the road more frequently than usual
That children will be playing on the road under supervision

text: What applies according to this traffic sign?
explanation: Within traffic calming zones you are allowed to travel at a maximum walking speed of 4 to 7 km/h, which means first gear, without giving gas. The street may be used completely by pedestrians. Children are allowed to play in the street. Be especially attentive and ready to brake. Pedestrians must not be impeded or endangered, you may have to wait. Since playing on the street is allowed here, you have to pay more attention to children. You are only allowed to park on marked areas.
options: I have to drive at walking speed
I may not impede pedestrians
I may only park on designated places

text: What does this traffic sign combination mean to you?
explanation: The traffic sign indicates the course of the priority road. The additional sign indicates the bend to the left; if you follow this direction, you will still be on the priority road.
options: I am on a priority road that bends left
I am not permitted to turn right or drive straight ahead
If I continue driving straight ahead, I have to allow right of way to vehicles arriving from the right

text: What do you have to be aware of when you see this traffic sign?
explanation: For this question, all three answers are correct. In a "traffic calming zone", pedestrians may use the entire width of the street, children can play on the street and you may only drive at walking speed.
options: Children may play across the entire road
Motor vehicles have to drive at walking speed
Pedestrians are entitled to use the entire breadth of the road

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: When you see this traffic sign, you approach a customs office. This means that you may encounter a traffic jam and therefore have to reduce your speed. You may also be controlled, so have all the papers at hand. Follow the instructions of the customs officers.
options: A customs point
A toll road
A prohibition on through-traffic

text: What is correct in this situation?
explanation: The village sign indicates the end of a closed village in the lower part. The upper part indicates the next town. You are standing on the left side of the road.
options: - a built-up area ends
- a built-up area starts
- a deviation ends

text: What do you have to observe in a traffic situation like this one?
explanation: Guidelines have the task of separating the lanes. Therefore, you may only drive over them if you avoid obstacles or overtake vehicles. This is only allowed if no road user is endangered.
options: - cross the centre line in order to pass by the obstruction
- cross the centre line in order to overtake
- not cross the centre line if this would endanger other traffic

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: If you are driving a vehicle, you may only stop in an emergency stop and breakdown bay in the event of an emergency or breakdown.
options: An emergency stop and breakdown bay
A temporary additional carriageway
A stop for breaks and changing drivers

text: You are driving on a road that has a protective lane for cyclists. How may you use the protective lane?
explanation: You may use the cycle lane if necessary, provided you do not endanger or obstruct cyclists.
options: - drive on the protective lane when necessary
- park on the protective lane
- stop on the protective lane

text: What can red-white warning plates on vehicles indicate?
explanation: Red and white warning signs point to vehicles with excess width (e.g., abnormal wide agricultural vehicles). Trailers parked inside a built-up area must either be illuminated or marked with reflective warning signs. So, warning signs do not refer to hazmat trucks.
options: A trailer parked on the roadway within a built-up area
A vehicle with excessive width
A vehicle transporting dangerous goods

text: What must you remember in the interests of environmental protection?
explanation: In the interests of environmental protection, you as a car driver must pay attention to the following: 1. Avoid driving unnecessarily; 2. Operate the engine evenly at medium speed; 3. Shut off the engine during extended periods of idling - after about a minute. In general, running the engine at idle will result in faster engine wear and wastes energy. You should therefore warm the engine in medium speed range and possibly stay in this area. High engine speeds lead to increased fuel consumption and therefore pollute the environment.
options: To avoid running the engine unnecessarily when you are stationary
To avoid driving back and forth unnecessarily
To drive with high revolutions per minute too often

text: What must be regularly serviced to prevent high fuel consumption and excessive pollutant emission?
explanation: The fuel consumption of a vehicle should be as low as possible. As a car driver, you should therefore regularly check and maintain all the components of your vehicle that are important for fuel consumption. These are, for example, the ignition and injection system and the engine air filter and the carburetor.
options: Engine air filter
Carburettor or fuel-injection system
Ignition system

text: What happens as a result of tyre pressures being well below the recommended levels?
explanation: Too low air pressure in the tire as well leads to increased fuel consumption. The effort required to keep the tire running is significantly higher than when the tire pressure has been set correctly. This leads to higher wear on the tire, increased fuel consumption and harms the environment.
options: Fuel consumption increases
Tyre wear increases
Pollutant emission decreases

text: When should you switch off the engine to save fuel and reduce pollution?
explanation: In order to avoid unnecessary consumption of gasoline, the engine should be switched off in certain situations. These include, for example, moments in traffic jams or in front of level crossings. Although there is an increased consumption during starting, it is compensated again starting from a downtime of one minute. You should not turn off the engine at a stop sign.
options: When you have to wait in a traffic jam for a long time
When you have to wait at level crossings or building sites
When you stop at a "STOP" sign

text: Your vehicle loses oil. How much drinking water can be polluted by a single drop of oil?
explanation: You should urgently avoid oil loss. Because even a single drop of oil can contaminate up to 600 liters of water and make it unfit for consumption.
options: 600 litres
50 litres
1 litre

text: What must you remember when refuelling?
explanation: Inhaling fuel vapors is harmful to your health. Therefore, make sure that the dispenser is being used correctly and pay attention to any defects when refueling. When the tank is full, the automatic system should be switched off. This prevents the overflow of gasoline or diesel. In addition, some air must remain in the tank for the fuel to expand.
options: Do not breath in any fuel fumes
Do not refuel when the tank is full and the nozzle has switched off
Fill up to the brim if possible

text: The engine and exhaust system of a vehicle have been "souped up". What could be the effects?
explanation: A souped-up engine and muffler provide increased noise pollution. In addition, the vehicle consumes more fuel. On top of that, exhaust emissions are increased and pollute the environment. In the worst case, the driver can expect a withdrawal of the operating license.
options: Increased noise pollution
Increased pollutant emission
Considerable reduction in fuel consumption

text: How can you reduce the noise made by a car?
explanation: In the low-speed speed range, the engine runs quieter than in high-revving areas. Deep-tread tires and driving without air filters also cause noise pollution. A driving style predominantly in the low-speed range saves fuel, is environmentally friendly and quiet. The minimum speeds must, however, be met, otherwise the engine runs twitchy, is cogging and sputtering. The lower the speed at which the engine is still running without cogging, the lower the noise.
options: By driving at a low engine speed
By using all-terrain tyres
By removing the air filter

text: Where can used oil, lubricants and car batteries be taken to be disposed of properly?
explanation: Waste oils, lubricants and vehicle batteries can be disposed of properly in the recycling center or via the car repair shop. Never should these substances be disposed of with household waste. It is special waste.
options: To recycling centres
To car workshops
In the household waste

text: How can you drive fuel-efficiently when travelling at a constant speed?
explanation: At constant speed, you can save fuel with the following measures: 1. by driving evenly in the low speed range; 2. by using the cruise control. The low speed range is just above the minimum speed that the engine needs for its optimal performance. If you drive below that, the engine is cogging; if you drive over it the fuel consumption increases in the high-speed range due to the engine performance. With steady driving in the low-speed speed range, the engine runs smoothly and with low fuel consumption. Cruise control allows a uniform driving style and relieves the / the car driver.
options: By using cruise control
By driving at a low engine speed
By driving at a high engine speed

text: At which engine speed range will fuel consumption be lower?
explanation: An engine consumes the least fuel in the speed range just above the minimum speed. This is the so-called low-speed speed range. When driving in the low-speed range, the speed should always be above the idle speed. An engine below the minimum speed runs twitchy, is cogging, sputtering or turns off. As a rule of thumb, the lower the speed at which the engine runs without cogging, the more fuel can be saved.
options: At low engine speed
At high engine speed

text: You have to wait because of a closed rail-crossing barrier. How can you now help protect the environment and save fuel?
explanation: When waiting in front of closed gates it is recommended to switch off the engine. On the one hand you save fuel and thus money, on the other hand, a switched-off engine is environmentally friendly. A pure gearshift to idle is not recommended, as even at idle the engine does not turn off and continues to use fuel.
options: By switching off the engine
By switching off the automatic start-stop
By letting the engine idle

text: What measures help protect the environment?
explanation: Turning the air conditioning off saves fuel as well. Low rolling resistance tires are designed for lower rolling resistance and can save fuel. Low-friction oils are synthetic oils with improved flow behavior, the so-called viscosity. This lubricates the engine faster and better and reduces friction. This also leads to a noticeable saving of fuel. Only oils approved by the engine/vehicle manufacturer should be used to prevent engine damage.
options: - low-resistance tyres
- low viscosity engine oil
- air-conditioning systems

text: What should you do to protect the environment?
explanation: You should avoid driving at high speeds. If the vehicle develops smoke, have it checked and repaired in a workshop.
options: - a lot of smoke is coming from the exhaust, I should arrange for the motor vehicle to be checked
- waiting for prolonged periods, I should switch off the engine
- driving, I should use the upper engine speed range

text: What can regular vehicle maintenance help achieve?
explanation: Regular vehicle maintenance helps to ensure road safety, low fuel consumption and low emissions.
options: Keeping fuel consumption low
Keeping emission levels low
Ensuring road safety

text: In which situations should you switch off the engine to save fuel and reduce environmental pollution?
explanation: You should turn off the engine before a gated railway crossing or if you are in a traffic jam, as you cannot accurately estimate the length of the waiting time. This way you can reduce your environmental impact and save fuel at the same time.
options: - it is foreseeable that I will have to wait longer in a traffic jam
- I have to wait at a gated level crossing
- I have to stop at a “Stop” sign

text: What can cause unnecessary noise pollution when driving?
explanation: If you drive at high speed or your muffler is defective, the noise level is increased. Low-speed driving also reduces fuel consumption. A defective muffler should be repaired in a workshop.
options: Unnecessarily fast acceleration
A defective exhaust
Driving at low revolutions per minute

text: How should you change gears in order to drive with particular consideration to the environment and fuel saving?
explanation: Changing gears environmentally friendly means to upshift early and shift down late. Do not drive the gears into the upper speeds, because this leads to the highest fuel consumption. You should start in first gear and then switch directly to second gear if possible. However, in some traffic situations, such as on the highway acceleration lane or while overtaking, it is necessary to drive with high speed. Of course you should do this in such a situation.
options: Change to a higher gear as early as possible
Change to a lower gear as late as possible
Change gears only when reaching the upper revolution limit

text: What is important to avoid pollution and to save energy when driving?
explanation: Low fuel consumption defines environmentally friendly and energy-saving driving. This requires the regular examination of consumption values ​​in order to optimize engine timing and to detect errors in good time.
options: Check the fuel consumption regularly
Have the engine tuning checked regularly
Wash the engine regularly, at least four times a year

text: How is fuel wasted and the environment polluted?
explanation: If you drive hectically, switching constantly between braking and accelerating and "playing with the gas", your vehicle consumes too much unnecessary fuel. Especially when accelerating a lot of energy is needed. When driving downhill in high gear, vehicle drivers burden the brakes unnecessarily. However, this does not result in increased fuel consumption.
options: By driving in a hectic manner
By "playing with the accelerator" while waiting at traffic lights
Using a high gear driving downhill

text: What indicates excessive petrol consumption due to high wear or wrong tuning of the engine?
explanation: Dark smoke indicates increased fuel consumption. It may be causally related to a fault of the engine control. You should definitely visit a workshop. Condensation, which drips from the exhaust, or white water vapor in cold weather, however, are normal.
options: A lot of dark exhaust smoke
Condensation water from the exhaust

text: What kind of driving results in high fuel consumption?
explanation: High speeds require more power due to the increased air resistance. As a result, the fuel consumption increases. If the driver drives rapidly or accelerates unnecessarily, this driving style also leads to an increased consumption. The same applies if gears are driven at full speed.
options: Fast starts and unnecessary acceleration
Revving up all gears
Driving at high speed

text: How do you drive with consideration to the environment?
explanation: Avoid constant acceleration and braking. Accelerating consumes unnecessary fuel and can be avoided, for example, in front of red lights by laying off the gas pedal. Maximum acceleration leads to high pollutant emissions and high noise as well as environmental pollution.
options: Decelerate in good time and use the momentum of the car when the next traffic light is on red
Avoid unnecessary acceleration and unnecessary braking
Always accelerate to the maximum when the traffic light changes to green

text: How can you cover more kilometres on less fuel?
explanation: The least fuel is consumed in the low-speed range. Timely upshifting avoids high-speed, fuel-intensive driving. Anticipatory driving saves fuel, as you can lay off the gas pedal early and let the vehicle roll out with its existing momentum.
options: Accelerate in such a way that the highest possible gear is quickly reached
Think ahead when driving in order to avoid unnecessary acceleration and braking
By pushing all gears to the highest possible revolutions

text: What can help save fuel and reduce pollution?
explanation: Before buying a car, the driver can check which model consumes little fuel. In addition, economical driving also contributes to savings.
options: Paying attention to the fuel consumption of a motor vehicle when buying it
Contributing to a constant flow of traffic by thinking ahead and driving correspondingly
Using public transport, a bicycle or walking, wherever possible

text: What can you do to help protect the environment?
explanation: The best way to protect the environment is to drive less. All journeys that are not absolutely necessary should be avoided. Certain driving styles consume extra fuel: Short-distance driving, especially when the engine is still cold, stop-and-go traffic, for example in crowded inner cities and searching for a parking space. On top of that, in areas with heavy traffic, the risk of smog from the exhaust emissions of vehicles increases. Driving at full throttle will not only cause noise, but your fuel consumption will increase disproportionately. However, once you are only 20% below the maximum speed, you reduce your fuel consumption by about 40%. Carpooling is also good for the environment.
options: - driving short distances
- driving at flat-out speed
- driving in crowded city centres

text: How can you achieve efficient fuel consumption and low pollutant emissions?
explanation: Before you drive off, you should make sure that the correct tire pressure is set. All important information about this topic can be found in the operating instructions of your vehicle. If the tire internal pressure is too high or too low, there will be an increase in pollutant emissions. Even unbalanced driving can lead to high fuel consumption. Therefore, instead of accelerating to the upper rotational speed limit and only change gears then, you should shift up in the lower or middle rotational speed limit range. This means you consume less fuel and at the same time reduce the exhaust emissions of your car.
options: By having the proper tyre pressure
By maintaining an even driving style at low engine speeds
By using the total capacity of every gear

text: Other road users draw your attention to the persistent thick smoke coming from your exhaust. What do you have to do?
explanation: You should visit a workshop that checks the damage. Because the strong smoke is a sign that the engine or the fuel system has a defect. In addition, the escaping gases are harmful to the environment and the smoke can obstruct the view of other road users.
options: Have the vehicle promptly checked
Change down gears early
Change up gears early

text: Why is it beneficial to use low viscosity engine oil?
explanation: Low-friction oils are characterized by a better flow behavior. These are synthetic oils that reduce friction in the engine through their improved viscosity and optimize oiling. This saves fuel. When using low-friction oils, attention must be paid to the approval of the manufacturer of the engine or vehicle.
options: - generate less friction in the engine
- reduce fuel consumption
- can be disposed of as household waste

text: What should you do after starting the vehicle?
explanation: After starting the car, you should drive off directly in the low-speed range. Warming up the engine while standing is prohibited and wastes fuel. In the low-speed range, the engine can be warmed up gently. Driving at high-revving directly is not good for the engine. Generally, the engine consumes more fuel at high speed. At too low speeds, the engine is cogging and sputtering. The consumption of an engine is the lowest just above the minimum speed.
options: - drive off as promptly as possible
- drive at low engine speeds where possible
- if possible, allow the engine of the stationary vehicle to warm up

text: How can you save fuel?
explanation: You can save fuel by: 1. driving smoothly and anticipatory while avoiding high engine speeds; 2. remove unused roof structures, as they increase fuel consumption with air resistance; 3. swap winter tires for summer tires in the warm season. Driving smoothly means avoiding unnecessary acceleration and deceleration. For example, by slowly rolling toward a red light, you can use the rest of the momentum to drive on if it is already green when you reach the traffic light. Only having to give gas, saves fuel compared to starting from standing completely still.
options: - removing any non-essential roof boxes etc
- driving in a foresighted manner
- driving with winter tyres the whole year round

text: How can you minimise tyre wear?
explanation: Driving with winter tires in non-winter weather leads to increased tire wear. Strong acceleration is associated with increased abrasion. The tire pressure recommended by the vehicle manufacturer must be observed. Too little tire pressure increases the tire wear considerably. If the air pressure is too low, the tire will deform more with each rotation than with correct tire pressure. Thereby the fabric layers of the tires rub against each other. Heat can be generated that irreparably damages the tire.
options: I refrain as much as possible from rapid acceleration
I regularly check the tyre inflation pressure
I use winter tyres all year round

text: What vehicles are generally exempt from the ban on road traffic in "environmental zones"?
explanation: A traffic ban for "environmental zones" does not apply to ambulances that are on duty. Also not affected are tractors from agriculture and forestry.
options: Agricultural and forestry tractors
Ambulances on duty
All motor vehicles belonging to the environmental zone inhabitants

text: When is it sensible to switch off a combustion engine?
explanation: Longer waiting times before a closed level crossing as well as loading and unloading a vehicle justify turning of an internal combustion engine. This saves fuel and reduces noise. The waiting time at a stop sign is usually short and you can usually drive on quickly after letting cross traffic pass. Therefore, in this situation, the internal-combustion engine is not turned off.
options: During lengthy waits at rail crossings
When loading and unloading the vehicle
When stopping at intersections with a stop sign

text: You are driving through city traffic in rush hour. What are the effects of stop-and-go driving?
explanation: The fuel consumption in stop-and-go traffic is greater, because drivers have to brake and accelerate more often. This leads to more exhaust fumes and other road users may be disturbed.
options: - consumes more fuel
- creates more exhaust gases
- creates more nuisances for others

text: What is a pre-condition for environmentally-friendly and energy-saving driving?
explanation: Tyre pressure has a major impact on fuel consumption as it affects rolling resistance. Regular vehicle maintenance contributes to low fuel consumption and emissions.
options: Checking the tyre inflation pressure regularly
Performing vehicle maintenance regularly
Washing the engine regularly

text: You are driving a motor vehicle with a manual gearbox. What style of driving results in higher fuel consumption within a built-up area?
explanation: When accelerating hard, you consume more fuel than when accelerating normally. The higher the speed, the more fuel is consumed.
options: Accelerating heavily
Driving at high engine speed
Driving in a high gear

text: You are driving a motor vehicle with a manual gearbox. How can you reduce the fuel consumption of your vehicle?
explanation: The higher the engine speed, the more fuel is consumed. If you ride with foresight, you can avoid unnecessary acceleration and braking.
options: By switching early up to the next gear
By employing an anticipatory driving style, to avoid frequent changes of speed
By driving at a high engine speed

text: How can you reduce the noise generated by your motor vehicle?
explanation: The higher the engine speed, the louder the engine will be. Tyres have differences in quality. When buying tyres, pay attention to the rolling noise.
options: By driving at a low engine speed
By using tyres that have a low rolling noise
By removing the air filter insert

text: What should you do to help protect the environment?
explanation: The engine also burns fuel when stationary, you should switch off the engine if you stop for a longer period of time. If there are atypical signs, such as smoke, you should have your vehicle checked.
options: - have the motor vehicle inspected if the exhaust is emitting an excessive amount of smoke
- switch off the engine if waiting for longer periods
- avoid unnecessary driving back and forth

text: You are driving a motor vehicle with a manual gearbox. When driving, what can cause avoidable noise pollution?
explanation: The higher the engine speed, the louder the engine. Tuned exhaust systems are usually louder than the standard exhaust system. You will consume more fuel when accelerating hard than when accelerating normally.
options: Heavily accelerating unnecessarily
Defective silencer
Driving fast in low gears

text: You are driving a motor vehicle with a manual gearbox on a level carriageway. How should you change gears so as to drive in a particularly environmentally conscious and economical way?
explanation: When accelerating, always try to keep the engine speed as low as possible. When coasting, shift gears as late as possible to take advantage of the engine braking effect and use the brakes as little as possible.
options: Changing up gears as early as possible
Changing down again as late as possible
Drive until the upper engine speed range is reached in one gear, before changing up

text: You are driving a motor vehicle with a manual gearbox. What type of behaviour pollutes the environment?
explanation: Constant speed consumes less fuel than constant deceleration and acceleration. Unnecessary acceleration at red lights burns fuel unnecessarily.
options: An uneven driving style
Frequently pressing the accelerator while waiting at traffic lights
Driving downhill in a high gear

text: You are driving a motor vehicle with a manual gearbox. How can you achieve efficient fuel consumption?
explanation: At constant speed, less is consumed than when constantly decelerating and accelerating. Tyre pressure has a major impact on fuel consumption as it affects rolling resistance.
options: By having the proper tyre inflation pressure
By adopting an even driving style with low engine speeds
When accelerating, changing the gears upwards as late as possible

text: What should you consider after starting your vehicle?
explanation: Unnecessary standing with the engine running unnecessarily pollutes the environment. Start the engine only when you want to drive off. The lower the engine speed, the less fuel is burnt.
options: - drive off as promptly as possible
- drive at low engine speeds
- if possible, allow the engine of the stationary vehicle to warm up

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What influences the degree of centrifugal force on bends?
explanation: The centrifugal force can throw your vehicle out of the curve. When doubling the speed, the centrifugal force quadruples. In addition, the curve radius influences this force as well. The tighter the curve, the more the centrifugal force increases. Therefore, you must brake early in tight corners.
options: The radius of the bend
Speed
Headwind

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Wet conditions can impair the effectiveness of drum brakes. What should you do?
explanation: The drum brake can run dry. For that you as the car driver brake cautiously. The drum brake heats up and the water can evaporate. Of course, you brake only when the traffic flow allows it. A rear-end collision must be avoided at all costs. Keep an eye on the traffic behind you.
options: I carefully drive to dry the brakes
I apply the brakes repeatedly while stationary
I refill the brake fluid

text: When will offences carrying two points be deleted from the Central Register of Road Traffic Offenders?
explanation: Registered misdemeanors, which have been scored and entered in Register of Driver Fitness with two points, become statute-barred after five years. Serious violations are always punished with two points.
options: - 5 years
- 3 years
- 2 years

text: What can cause skidding on bends?
explanation: Defective shock absorbers can be the cause of a vehicle skidding or swinging off the curve when turning. The correct tire pressure specified by the manufacturer is important for a stable vehicle position in curves. It is tailored to the overall design of the vehicle. Too low or too different tire pressure reduces driving stability and increases the risk of skidding on turns. Too high a load has an influence on the driving stability. There is not too little loading.
options: Faulty shock-absorbers
Insufficient or uneven tyre pressure
Load is too small

text: What can cause skidding on bends?
explanation: In curves, the following factors can lead to skidding: 1. excessive speed; 2. wet or icy roads; 3. strong braking. In turns, much of the stiction forces are needed for the cornering forces that hold the vehicle in the lane. If you brake too much, the stiction is instead used largely for the transmission of the braking force. As a result, the cornering forces are too low to counteract the centrifugal force, the same applies to excessive speed. On wet roads, a film of water between the road surface and the tire reduces grip and promotes skidding.
options: Heavy braking
Driving fast on a wet roadway
Slight acceleration when leaving the bend

text: What can cause a dangerous situation?
explanation: When cutting a corner, the vehicle in the curve is directed inward and the opposite lane is used as well in order to progress faster. This represents a serious threat to oncoming traffic and can lead to serious accidents. Dimming too late can also jeopardize oncoming drivers as they are dazzled and drive almost blindly.
options: Cutting corners
Dipping your headlights too late
Driving too far behind the vehicle in front

text: What do you do if the white car does not stop?
explanation: Even if you are in the right of way: Do not take risks in case of bad traffic behavior of other participants. Draw attention to the error with horn signal, but do not insist on your right and renounce your right of way. Lower your speed as well.
options: Reduce speed, waive your priority
Sound your horn and try to pass in front of the car

text: What results in specific risks to motorcyclists?
explanation: If you ride with the visor open, an insect can fly into it at any time. This can be very painful and distracting. If the road surface changes, there is a risk of falling down because the grip level is different. In heavy rain, motorbikes are more likely to aquaplane than cars.
options: Riding with the visor open
Riding in heavy rain
Changes in the road surfacing

text: What should you do now?
explanation: The overtaking vehicle will probably not be able to complete its overtaking manoeuvre as planned. To prevent an accident, you should let the overtaking vehicle get into the lane.
options: I reduce my speed so that the overtaking vehicle can pull in ahead of me
I accelerate so that the overtaking vehicle can pull in behind me
I maintain my speed because there is sufficient safety distance

text: Why should you allow the truck to change lane?
explanation: If you are in the dead corner of the truck and the truck suddenly exhaust yourself, a dangerous situation can occur and you would have to slow down. Since there is enough space between the vehicle in front, you should take the truck into account and enable it to change lanes.
options: Because the driver of the truck may fail to see me
Because I should show due consideration to the truck
Because the alternate merging procedure applies here

text: As a motorcyclist , why is it important that you adopt an anticipatory driving style especially on very winding stretches of road?
explanation: By riding with foresight, you can recognise the behaviour of oncoming traffic and potentially dangerous situations, such as dirt on the road or a change in cornering radius, in good time and adapt your riding behaviour accordingly.
options: Because the turning radius can reduce as the road continues
Because otherwise I will not be able to see dirt on the roadway in time
Because it means I am able to adjust myself in good time to the actions of oncoming traffic

text: As a motorcyclist, you can easily go unnoticed by other vehicle drivers. How can you reduce this risk?
explanation:
Try to put yourself in the shoes of the drivers involved so that you can better understand what they might do next. This way, you may be able to recognise a potential hazard and react to it in good time.
If you are driving in a vehicle's side blind spot, the driver will not be able to see you. If possible, drive in such a way that you are not in the blind spot for an unnecessarily long time. You should also try to make eye contact with the drivers involved before turning to ensure that they can see you.
options: I avoid remaining for too long in the blind spot to the side of other vehicles
I try to see the road situation from the perspective of other vehicle drivers
Before taking a turn, I try to establish eye-contact with other drivers in my vicinity

text: What can cause a dangerous situation?
explanation: If a foot brake has a strong one-sided effect, the vehicle may swing off laterally during braking. The car may skid and overturn. Therefore, unequal braking forces are extremely dangerous. Excessive steering can also lead to skidding at high speeds because you can no longer keep the lane properly. A disturbed traffic radio is not a technically dangerous defect.
options: Brakes which engage heavily on one side
Too much steering-wheel play
Disturbed reception of traffic information on the radio

text: What are the effects of listening to loud music - especially with an extremely loud bass volume - in the car?
explanation: Loud music in the car leads to two negative effects: The driver is distracted by the music and he cannot concentrate on the road. Deep basses in particular lead to strong uncertainty in blind road users. These can lose their orientation, especially with low-frequency music.
options: Blind people lose their orientation when they are near the car
The driver’s attention is significantly impaired
It makes it easier for blind people to recognise where the road is

text: What can create a hazard when driving?
explanation: If the dipped headlights are not working, you will see poorly on the one hand and you will be seen worse on the other. If the service brake is too one-sided, the vehicle could swerve or have a longer braking distance. If there is too much play in the steering, the steering command will not be carried out.
options: A service brake that responds heavily on one side
An excessive amount of play in the steering
A faulty dipped headlight

text: You are driving on a narrow road. About 20 m ahead of you a child suddenly runs onto the roadway. When is a collision unavoidable despite emergency braking?
explanation: For this question, you must first calculate the thinking distance and the hazard braking distance. At 50 km/h, the thinking distance is 50/10 x 3 = 15. So, there are 15 meters of thinking distance. The hazard braking distance is determined by the following calculation: [(50/10 x 50/10) / 2] = 12.5. 50 km/h is the right answer.
options: 50 km/h
30 km/h
20 km/h

text: Why do you have to brake?
explanation: You have to expect the person standing in front of the stationary truck to move to the left. Braking serves to protect the person.
options: Because someone is walking onto the road
Because passengers are exiting the tram
Because the truck is switching into my lane

text: What is the right course of action now?
explanation: When turning right, you must always be aware of pedestrians and cyclists approaching. They may cross the road in front of you.
options: I stop
I continue driving as before
I accelerate

text: What must you anticipate in this situation?
explanation:
The road sign signals increased caution against children who could walk across the road between the vehicles.
In addition, you have to expect that people get off to the side of the road.
options: Children walking out onto the road
People exiting their vehicles via the side nearest the road
There is a pedestrian crossing up ahead

text: What is the right course of action now?
explanation: Since a person wants to cross the intersection, you have to stop and have the person crossed the traffic light.
options: I stop
I continue driving as before
I accelerate

text: What must you reckon with when you are driving in the left-hand lane of an autobahn at high speed?
explanation: At high speed, motorcycles are very sensitive to wind from the side. Small fast motorcycles are hard to see, other vehicles might therefore not see you.
options: Motorists in front of you may suddenly pull out to overtake
Even a slight, unexpected side wind can effect road stability
If you have full beam switched on, vehicles travelling in front of you will not pull out to overtake

text: When is there a danger of a motorcycle veering sideways at high speed?
explanation: Sudden side wind increases the risk of a motorcycle to veer sideways. Sudden side wind can occur when exiting under a bridge, out of a tunnel, or when overtaking a truck.
options: When you overtake a truck
When driving under a bridge at high speed in a strong side wind
When the braking effect is different on both sides of the front disc brake

text: What must you reckon with when it starts raining after a longer period of dry weather?
explanation: Rain clean up part of the dirt on the road. If the weather was dry for a long period of time, the road will accumulate a lot of dirt. With the addition of water, it will create a film on the road that will make the surface more slippery and increase the braking distance. You can also expect poor visibility on your helmet or goggles.
options: A dangerous greasy film on the surface of the road
Bad visibility through helmet visor or goggles
Shorter braking distance

text: You come unexpectedly upon a stretch of road with loose chippings. What do you do?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Avoid braking if possible
Hold your course if possible
Brake hard using the handbrake

text: What can happen if you drive around a left-hand bend near the marked central line?
explanation: When turning left, being near the central line is dangerous. Due to the inclination left, you could be hit by a vehicle going in the opposite direction. Road markings such as the central line are slippery, if your motorcycle run on it, it could slip resulting in a fall
options: Because of the inclined position, the upper part of your body could be hit by oncoming traffic
The motorcycle could catch the central line and slip from under you
There is no danger as long as the tyres are new

text: What are the dangers on wet cobblestones?
explanation: Cobblestones are slippery and will therefore increase the risk of falling or tires to lose adhesion to the road and spin when accelerating as well as a tendency of breaks to lock
options: Increased tendency for the brakes to lock
Increased danger of falling
Spinning and skidding of the rear wheel when accelerating

text: What should you particularly remember when it is raining?
explanation: Rain reduces visibility. The road surface is less visible when wet. The visibility can also be lowered by water particles coming from other vehicles. Your visor will also accumulate water droplets and further diminish your visibility.
options: Visibility through goggles or helmet visor gets considerably worse
Road surface damage is less noticeable when the road is wet
Visibility is further reduced by water sprayed up by other vehicles

text: What should you remember when there are tramlines in your lane?
explanation: Tramlines are made of metal which is slippery. A motorcycle therefore has a higher risk of sliding and falling on them. When crossing you should try to be as perpendicular to them as possible to avoid slipping
options: Tramlines should always be crossed at the widest angle possible
There is always greater danger of falling on tramlines
Tramlines should always be crossed at the narrowest angle possible

text: What can cause the danger of falling on bends?
explanation: When turning on bends, slippery surfaces such as lane markings, oil on the road, dirt, manholes, sand or leaves can lead to a fall
options: Oil on the roadway
Lane markings
The outside edge of the bend is higher than the inside

text: What can cause the danger of falling on bends?
explanation: When turning on bends or braking, slippery surfaces such as lane markings, oil on the road, dirt, manholes, sand, dust, gravel, wet surfaces, cobblestones or leaves will increase the risk of falling
options: Manhole covers on the roadway
Leaves on the roadway
Sand on the roadway

text: When must you apply the brakes with particular care?
explanation: Braking is less effective on slippery surfaces (wet road, cobblestones, dirt road) and needs to be applied with care
options: When travelling on cobblestones
When it starts raining
On a concrete roadway with good grip

text: What can cause in aquaplaning (sliding on wet roads) on wet road surfaces?
explanation: Aquaplaning - also known as hydroplaning - occurs when the tread depth of the tires is too low to displace the accumulated amount of water or when the amount of water to be discharged is too large due to a high speed (from 60 km/h). In addition, wheel ruts in the road, in which water accumulates, favor this effect.
options: High speed
Worn tyres
Grooves in the roadway

text: Why could overtaking be dangerous here?
