You also create more space on the road if the motorcycle behind you tries to overtake and hasn't seen the truck yet.
options: I reduce my speed
I drive as far to the right as possible
I signal to the motorcyclist that he can overtake me

text: What should you do?
explanation: A car driving in front of you parks. You must reduce your speed and then change the lane to avoid the parked car when the motorcycle has passed you.
options: Reduce speed, be ready to brake
Move to the left-hand lane
Continue driving, flash lights to signal

text: What should you know about using the rear-view mirror?
explanation: Using the rear-view mirrors requires you to know the following: 1. Rear-view mirrors must be adjusted to the driver before starting to drive. 2. There are blind spots on all types of rear-view mirrors. These indicate areas hidden from view in which pedestrians, small vehicles or obstacles can be overlooked. By optimally adjusting the outer rearview mirror and the inner mirror, you keep the blind spot as low as possible.
options: I am unable to see vehicles and pedestrians in the blind spot
Rear-view mirrors must be adjusted to the particular driver
The interior mirror has no blind spot to the right-side

text: You are driving into a right-hand bend. A motorcyclist approaches you at high speed. What risks should you take into account?
explanation: As you enter a right-hand turn, the oncoming motorcyclist makes a left turn. His upper body is tilted towards you. Bear in mind that the motorcyclist is almost as wide as a car while doing that. If the rider is riding too far at the center line to increase the radius of curvature and lower centrifugal forces, his upper body could be caught by your vehicle.
options: - will intrude into my lane because of the heavily tilted position
- will cut the corner and intrude into my lane
- will brake in good time and avoid intruding into my lane

text: On a narrow road you want to overtake cyclists on an incline. What should you do?
explanation: Cyclists tend to sway more on inclines. So, the required minimum distance to the cyclist of 1.5 m should therefore be increased. Oncoming traffic must be allowed to pass before overtaking. Do not drive close to the cyclists while passing them.
options: - maintain a large distance to the side
- allow the oncoming traffic to pass before overtaking
- drive carefully close past the cyclists

text: You are driving on a rural road. A line of approximately 15 slow-moving vehicles is travelling in front of you. What should you do?
explanation: In such a convoy, it is important to stay calm and to maintain the necessary safety distance. So-called queue, that is the overtaking of individual vehicles, brings no time gain and leads to a high accident risk.
options: I remain behind the line of vehicles for the moment
I flash my lights and sound my horn to urge vehicles ahead to overtake
I overtake the line of vehicles as quickly as possible

text: You stop to allow passengers to exit your vehicle on the right-side. A cycle path runs along there. What should you do?
explanation: You as a car driver have a special duty of care. So, if you're stopping at a bike path with a co-driver, you should warn him/her about the cyclist before he/she gets off.
options: I should make sure that no cyclists are approaching
I should point out the cycle path to the persons exiting
I should observe the traffic using my rear-view mirror only

text: You increase your speed from 50 km/h to 100 km/h. How does the reaction distance change in accordance with the rule of thumb?
explanation: If the car driver doubles the speed of the vehicle, the braking distance doubles from 15 to 30 meters.
options: It is doubled from 15 m to 30 m
It is quadrupled from 25 m to 100 m
It is halved from 50 m to 25 m

text: What can cause a faster-moving vehicle to suddenly swerve on a dry, straight road?
explanation: By gusts of wind and tire blow your vehicle can break out and distract you from your direction of travel.
options: Gusts of wind
A tyre blow-out
Continuous head wind

text: What should you anticipate?
explanation: The danger sign warns of a sharp left turn. The crest blocks the view forward on the road. The curve is not visible. You have to expect a broken-down vehicle or another obstacle. Because of the road, there can be no cross traffic in front of the crest.
options: A dangerous left-hand bend
An obstacle situated around the corner
Cross-wise moving traffic before the summit

text: What is the right course of action now?
explanation: As you can see in the rearview mirror, there is a vehicle behind you in the left lane. So stay in the middle lane and let the truck change lanes to overtake.
options: I stay in the middle lane
I move into the left-hand lane
I move into the right-hand lane

text: What must you reckon with here?
explanation: The sign announces the end of the left lane. The traffic flow will condense from two lanes to a single lane. Halting traffic might occur. The vehicle in the left lane will change the lane. You have to allow the vehicles on the left side of the lane to change over to your lane according to the zip merging principle.
options: The vehicle in front changing lanes
Denser traffic beyond the underpass
The right-hand lane coming to an end

text: What must you do here?
explanation: If the car driver drives at high speed on the highway for a long time, the senses get used to the fast pace. There is a risk of underestimating the pace. In particular, if you want to drive out, check your speed on the speedometer. Use the deceleration lane of the freeway to reduce your speed. Braking there doesn't hinder anybody. Then you can enter the sharp bend of the exit at a reasonable speed.
options: Check your speed again and, if necessary, brake
Brake only on the bend so as not to obstruct traffic following behind

text: A traffic jam is building up here. What is the correct procedure?
explanation: If you drive towards a traffic jam, turn on your hazard lights to alert other road users. It is important to build a rescue lane for any approaching rescue vehicles. In this case, drive as far to the right as possible.
options: If possible, switch on hazard warning lights to warn vehicles following behind
Drive as far as possible to the right in order to leave room for a channel on the left
Drive as far as possible to the left in order to leave room for a channel on the right

text: What must you anticipate with inclines on motorways?
explanation: When driving uphill on motorways, you should expect slow-moving trucks in the right lane, sudden overtaking manoeuvres by other road users and large speed differences between vehicles. All 3 answers are correct.
options: Slow-moving trucks on the right-hand lane
Sudden overtaking manoeuvres by other road users
Large differences in speed between vehicles

text: What must you do?
explanation: Since you are currently being overtaken by a car on the left-hand side, you must maintain the lane and reduce the speed until the truck in front of you has completed its overtaking maneuver and changes to the right-hand lane.
options: Slow down and stay in lane
Move to the left-hand lane
Maintain speed and stay in lane

text: What must you be aware of when joining the motorway?
explanation: On the freeway, the continuous traffic always has the right of way and does not have to allow entrance. On the acceleration lane the driver may drive faster than the rest of the vehicles.
options: On the merging lane, I may drive faster than the through-driving traffic
The through-driving traffic has priority
The through-driving traffic on the right-hand lane must allow incoming traffic to merge

text: You are driving at the recommended speed on the motorway and want to leave it at the next exit. What should you do?
explanation: Finish overtaking in good time and get on the right lane. Before changing to the deceleration lane look around and indicate. On the deceleration lane, check your speed on the speedometer in order to assess it right. Only on the deceleration lane you should reduce the speed significantly, so as not to hinder subsequent traffic on the continuous lane.
options: I cease overtaking manoeuvres in good time
I significantly reduce my speed on the exit lane
I significantly reduce my speed while still on the right-hand lane of the motorway

text: After a longer journey travelling at about 120 km/h, you want to exit the motorway. What must you be aware of when doing so?
explanation: If you, as a car driver, leave the motorway at a speed of about 120 km/h, you must observe the following: 1. complete all overtaking maneuvers in good time; 2. merge right; 3. reduce the speed while checking it on the speedometer; 4. indicate. In order not to hinder the traffic on the continuous road, you should reduce the speed only when you change to the deceleration lane.
options: I signal in good time and then brake while on the exit lane, so as not to impede the traffic behind me
I check the speedometer to make sure I do not underestimate my speed
I maintain my speed while on the exit lane, so as not to impede the traffic behind me

text: What should you do now?
explanation: When approaching a jam end on the highway, you must reduce your speed and warn the road users behind you by switching on the hazard lights. A rescue lane is to be formed.
options: I slow my vehicle down
I switch on my hazard lights
I continue driving in the clear lane

text: What should you anticipate with this bend?
explanation: The course of the curve is not assessable. You always have to expect obstacles such as broken-down vehicles or traffic jams. Be prepared for a stop within sight. The curve may narrow in its course. Thereby you'll only notice in the curve that your speed is too high. It is important to reduce the speed on time.
options: With an obstacle situated around the corner
That the bend will become tighter as it progresses
With oncoming traffic on my lane

text: What is correct in this situation?
explanation: The curve is difficult to assess for the car driver. There may be other road users or even obstacles on the route. Therefore, it makes sense to slow down the pace even before the turn and mentally adjust to a possible danger situation. Because even for oncoming drivers this is a difficult spot and caution is required.
options: I have to reduce my speed
The truck has right of way
The truck has to wait

text: Why do you have to slow here?
explanation: The moveable road barrier with flashing arrow in the right-hand lane forces the truck driver to change to your lane on the left. That's why you have to delay now. The white car behind you is no danger.
options: Because of the truck
Because of the speed limit
Because of the white car

text: Why do you have to reduce your speed now?
explanation: In this situation, the blue car is likely to change to the right lane. You should therefore reduce your speed and keep a safe distance from it
options: Because of the blue car
Because of the speed limit
Because of the red van

text: You are driving at least 20 km/h faster than the green truck. What should you do?
explanation: You are on an acceleration lane to the freeway. On the acceleration lane it is permissible to drive faster than the vehicles on the continuous lane. Therefore, you can drive onto the highway at a faster pace in front of the green truck.
options: I move onto the motorway ahead of the green truck
I brake and move onto the motorway behind the green truck
I stop at the end of the merging lane, and move onto the motorway behind the blue truck

text: You are approaching these vehicles. What should you do in this situation?
explanation: The white car on the left lane must not be overtaken on the right. To go behind it on the left lane and to make him/her change with flash light is also prohibited. You have to slow down and drive on the middle lane just as fast as the car. Allow him/her as much distance as it takes in order for him/her to be able to change to the middle lane at any time.
options: I remain on the middle lane but without overtaking the white car
I remain on the middle lane and cautiously overtake the white car
I move into the left-hand lane and flash my headlights until the person in front vacates the lane

text: You are driving a truck. What is the right course of action now?
explanation: Please magnify the distance to the vehicle ahead and therefore hold a required safety distance.
options: I increase the distance to the vehicle ahead
I maintain my speed
I overtake the truck in front of me

text: What should you do now?
explanation: Next to you is a red car that changes into the middle lane. Therefore, you cannot change the lane, otherwise you would endanger other road users.
options: - do not switch lanes, because [the red car] is already moving across
- move into the middle lane, because my overtaking manoeuvre is complete
- switch lanes so that I do not obstruct [the yellow car]

text: You want to join the motorway. What driving line should you follow?
explanation: While driving onto the freeway you should continue to follow the third driving line, so stay true to the lane and do not cut the boundary line.

text: What should you be prepared for now?
explanation: No traffic jam can be seen in this situation. Since the motorcycle is driving on the left, it will not leave the motorway. On the other hand, the car driving on your left flashes to the right. You can be prepared for the driver to leave the motorway.
options: [The yellow car] exits the motorway
The motorbike exits the motorway
The [blue bus] in front of me brakes due to a traffic jam

text: You want to exit the motorway. What is creating a dangerous situation here?
explanation: The motorbike behind you (see right wing mirror) creates a dangerous situation for you. Take this into account when leaving the motorway.
options: The motorbike
[The yellow truck]
[The green vehicle]

text: What is the right course of action now?
explanation: There is an object on the roadway in the right lane in front of the truck. Truck will avoid the object by using the left lane. You should therefore stay in the left lane. If you continue to drive unchanged, you could collide with the truck. You should therefore reduce your speed.
options: I reduce my speed
I remain in the left-hand lane
I continue driving as before

text: Why must you reduce your speed now?
explanation: The right lane is blocked in front of the truck. He has to change to the left lane. To allow him to do this, you should reduce your speed. The car driving behind you is no reason for you to slow down. The maximum permissible speed here is 120 km/h. Keep this in mind.
options: Because of the truck
Because of the speed limit
Because of the [blue] car

text: You want to leave the motorway. What is the right course of action?
explanation: As soon as you have entered the deceleration lane, you should brake. If you brake before entering the deceleration lane, you will unnecessarily interfere with traffic on the motorway. You should check your speedometer more often to make sure you are not entering the bend too fast. On motorways, there is a danger that you will get too used to the high speed and therefore enter an exit too fast. If you were to slow down at the turn, you would not be able to reduce your speed in time. In general, you should always brake before a bend and not only in the bend.
options: I use the speedometer to check my speed at short intervals
I reduce my speed now
I reduce my speed only once I am at the turn

text: When driving on motorways, why should you maintain the recommended speed of 130 km/h?
explanation: The higher the speed, the longer the reaction distance, braking distance, etc. If all vehicles travel at a similar speed, the traffic flow becomes more even.
options: - can prevent accidents occurring
- can reduce the severity of possible accidents
- achieves an even flow of traffic

text: What must you anticipate here?
explanation: Due to the sudden traffic jam, the driver of the truck sees the end of the traffic jam too late. Due to the traffic jam, the motorcycle will try to go through the rows of vehicles.
options: The driver of the [yellow truck] does not notice the start of the tailback in time
The motorbike drives between the lines of vehicles
[The blue car] pulls into my lane in front of me

text: What should you anticipate when driving out the exit slip road?
explanation: A warning triangle indicates a nearby obstacle, e.g. people, a defective vehicle or a fallen load, in the exit lane. Therefore, enter the exit at a very reduced speed.
options: A broken-down vehicle
People on the carriageway
A fallen load

text: Why should you avoid overtaking alongside the roadworks site?
explanation:
When overtaking in the construction site area, the risk of accidents is significantly increased, because there is a risk that the vehicles that you want to overtake run over the yellow lane marking. The lanes are mostly narrower and the distractions on the edge of the road can lead to inattentiveness.
Overtaking in the construction site area often saves almost no time, since most drivers in the construction site area only drive the maximum speed.
options: The time saved is frequently insignificant
Vehicles in the right-hand lane may cross over the yellow road markings
The risk of an accident increases significantly

text: How can you reduce the risk of driving onto a motorway against the stipulated direction?
explanation: To avoid driving against the direction of travel on the motorway, you should always pay attention to the relevant traffic signs. It is very important to pay attention to the exact signs, especially when the traffic routing has changed.
options: I deliberately look for traffic signs showing the right direction of travel at motorway slip roads
I pay close attention to the signage when the traffic routing changes
When encountering roadworks, I only follow the information provided by my navigation system

text: What must you remember as bus driver on duty?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: - not have any beverages containing alcohol while on duty and while on stand-by duty
- not start to drive while under the effect of alcohol
- have beverages containing alcohol while on duty, as long as a blood alcohol standard of 0.3 per mille is not exceeded

text: What must you remember as bus driver on duty?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: You may not take any drugs or medicaments which impair your ability to drive while on duty or stand-by duty
You may not start to drive when your ability to drive is impaired by drugs or medicaments
You may take any drug for which no prescription is required, without having to fear that your ability to drive is impaired

text: What must you do if you notice signs of fatigue when driving on open stretches of road at night (heavy eyelids, feeling chilly, sudden frights etc.)?
explanation: You can only avoid signs of fatigue if you take sufficiently long breaks in time. Do not turn on the radio to stay awake, as there is a risk it will distract you further. If you already feel the first symptoms of fatigue, find a place where you can take a longer break as soon as possible.
options: Interrupt your journey for an adequate break
Switch on the radio and proceed

text: How can fatigue be prevented on a long journey?
explanation: Timely breaks prevent overfatigue. Gymnastic exercises during the break pep up the circulation and are good for the joints. Coffee has only a short-term mobilizing effect, which can then quickly turn into the opposite. That means you could fall asleep without warning.
options: By well-timed and sufficient stops for rests
Gymnastic exercises during stops
Drink coffee and make no stops

text: What is the potential risk when using driver assistance systems?
explanation: The car driver may have too high expectations of the advanced driver-assistance system. This may result in the car driver neglecting his or her own responsibility and paying too little attention to the traffic. Even when using advanced driver-assistance systems, the responsibility for safe driving remains with the driver.
options: - have false expectations of the systems
- pay too little attention to the traffic around him
- neglect his own personal responsibility

text: What is the risk if you become distracted while using electronic devices when driving?
explanation: Using electronic devices while driving can cause you to miss traffic signs and wander off your lane (concentration distracted).
options: I may deviate from my lane
I may fail to notice road traffic signs
My stopping distance may be reduced

text: What frequently causes younger drivers to have “disco accidents”?
explanation: All three are correct. The so-called disco accidents are caused by overtiredness, by physical exhaustion and by being unfit to drive.
options: - are over-tired
- are physically exhausted
- are not fit to drive

text: What is the right thing to do if you sense signs of fatigue during a night-time journey?
explanation: As soon as you feel tired, you should take a break immediately. The risk of falling asleep increases with every second. If possible, you can let your passenger drive if they have the driving licence.
options: I interrupt the journey to take an adequate break
I allow a co-driver to drive, if possible
I decide against taking a break, and fight the tiredness

text: What can diminish alertness in road traffic?
explanation: All external stimuli such as joy, anger, interesting things on the radio and lively conversations can negatively affect the attention while driving, as they can be distracting.
options: Strong emotions (e.g. delight, annoyance, impatience)
Animated conversation
Engrossing programs on the car radio

text: What strongly distracts you while you are driving?
explanation: Telephoning while driving is only allowed via a hands-free system. Even then it is still a distraction. The lighting of a cigarette is considered a strong distraction, as it directs the view from the roadway to the cigarette. Whining children and passengers can be very distracting, if necessary, take a pause.
options: Telephoning
Lighting a cigarette
Nagging children on the backseats

text: When should you interrupt your journey?
explanation:
Especially on longer trips, it can always happen that concentration subsides. If you notice that your concentration wanes noticeably, you should definitely take a break.
You should also stop if you want to cancel an object that has fallen into the vehicle. By searching and lifting an object, you can distract yourself very much. Therefore, you can endanger yourself and other road users.
options: - want to pick an item that has fallen down in my vehicle
- notice that the concentration is decreasing
- want to activate the cruise control system

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: A slow driver prevents you from proceeding quickly. What is right?
explanation: Never start a risky overtaking maneuver or force your frontman to speed up with your flash light. Keep the necessary safety distance and wait for a convenient opportunity for safe overtaking.
options: You follow him until there is a possibility to overtake
You flash your headlights to make him drive faster
You close up to him in order to shorten the overtaking distance

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: What makes a good driver?
explanation: A good driver adheres to the traffic regulations and is characterized by a cooperative behavior in dealing with other road users. He/she refrains from risky driving styles and careless overtaking maneuvers. A good driver does not have to prove his/her skills to others.
options: He treats others like partners, drives calmly and cooly and refrains from showing that he is superior
He uses every possibility to overtake, give the slip to others and show his superiority even if his manner of driving involves risks
He drives fast in order to show his abilities

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: Travelling on a main road after a lengthy period of time of following behind, you are finally able to overtake a very slow-moving car. What should you do?
explanation: You should stay calm in this situation and overtake with a sufficient safety distance without endangering other road users. Harassing others by tightly cutting them should be avoided. Otherwise an accident could occur.
options: - I pull back in after an adequate distance in order not to impede the other driver
- I brake briefly in order to call the attention of the other driver to his slow speed
- I drive especially slowly in order to emphasise to the other driver the effects of his driving style

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: The vehicle ahead has prevented you from overtaking for some time now. What is the right course of action?
explanation: The car driver has to wait until overtaking is possible without danger and always maintain the necessary safety distance to the vehicle in front. Stay calm, because tailgating, turning the headlights on full beam for a long time or honking is considered coercion and will be punished with fines or even a withdrawal of your driving license.
options: I wait until I am able to overtake
I close the gap
I sound my horn and flash my headlights persistently

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: Right before you want to drive off, you got annoyed about something and have become very angry. What should you do?
explanation: Getting into the car angrily can negatively affect your driving style. If you are angry, your driving style is also aggressive and limited. Therefore, only get into your vehicle when you're abreacted.
options: I only drive off, once I have calmed down again
I drive off, in order to distract myself from my anger
I try to reach my destination quickly, so that I can calm down there

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: You have just avoided a road traffic accident by performing an emergency braking manoeuvre. Your hands and knees are shaking. You are still far from your destination. What should you do?
explanation: You should calm down first. Because your restlessness can have a negative effect on your driving style. Find a place to stop and relax. Afterwards you may continue the journey.
options: - to the next stopping place, in order to calm myself down
- to my destination, so that I can recover my composure

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: What should you be aware of when driving a car after a long day's work?
explanation: After a long day at work, you are usually not fully productive and get tired faster. That's why mistakes while driving can increase and your concentration decreases.
options: I drive with a lower level of concentration
I will become tired more quickly
I make fewer driving errors

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: How can you recognise a good driver?
explanation: A good driver always takes care to act in partnership and also knows that people can make mistakes.
options: - exhibits a calm and relaxed driving style
- refrains from responding to provocations on the road
- always informs other traffic participants of their driving errors

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: The [red] car in front of you has been driving slowly for some time now. What is the correct course of action in this situation?
explanation:
You maintain your speed so as not to tailgate and keep the required safe distance. It is forbidden to tailgate, tailgate too closely or honk your horn in traffic.
The road is clear, but you can only see as far as the next bend. The visible distance is too short for an overtaking manoeuvre.
options: I maintain my speed
I overtake, because the road is clear
I close the distance and sound my horn

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: What frequently causes young people to have “disco accidents”?
explanation:
Young drivers in particular have less driving experience and a higher willingness to take risks through showing off. Dangerous situations are assessed more poorly and accidents occur more frequently.
A defensive driving style can prevent accidents.
options: A lack of awareness of the road traffic
A high readiness to take risks
A defensive driving style

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: Why can driving under pressure of time be dangerous?
explanation: When you are under time pressure, you may underestimate dangers because your willingness to take risks increases and people often drive too fast. You should still drive defensively and stick to the speed limits to avoid endangering yourself and others.
options: - risks are frequently underestimated
- the driver frequently goes too fast
- a defensive driving style is frequently adopted

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: You are on a road outside of a built-up area, and a car in front of you is driving much slower than is permitted to and has the capacity to. What is the right course of action?
explanation: Even if you don't like it, you must adapt your speed to that of the car and not get too close to it. Only overtake at a suitable place and not in front of it. Do not endanger yourself or others.
options: I adjust my speed to that of the car
I overtake at a suitable place
I flash my headlights, until the car begins to drive faster

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: Why is it not advisable to change lanes frequently?
explanation: Every lane change requires certain activities: observing traffic, flashing, changing the lane yourself. In this case, other road users can be overlooked and endangered. Changing lanes often doesn't save you much time, but the more often you change lanes, the more likely you are to make mistakes.
options: Because this can increase the risk of driving errors
Because the time gained by this is generally very small
Because this can endanger other road users

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: You have narrowly avoided a road traffic accident through emergency braking. Your hands and knees are shaking. What is the right course of action?
explanation:
Stop at the next opportunity and take a break until you have calmed down. Maybe you can get out, walk a few metres and take a deep breath. 
You should also go through the situation again in your head later, as you may realise what didn't go perfectly. That way you can adjust your driving behaviour in the future.
options: I take a break at the soonest possible opportunity, in order to calm myself
Later, I ponder if I could have avoided the situation
I continue driving in order to calm myself

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: While driving, you become very annoyed at the behaviour of another road user. What is the right course of action now?
explanation: It is important that you are not distracted by the traffic if you are annoyed by the behaviour of other drivers, because road safety is paramount. Concentrate on the traffic and continue driving calmly; if you are emotionally agitated while driving, you could overlook dangers. If necessary, take a break and only continue driving when you have calmed down.
options: I continue to concentrate on the road traffic
I continue driving in such a way that my anger does not negatively affect road safety
If necessary, I take a break to calm myself down

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: Why does environment friendly driving in general have a beneficial effect on traffic safety?
explanation: Avoid high speeds and drive anticipatory. This not only has a positive effect on the environment. It also contributes to greater road safety.
options: Because drivers think ahead when travelling, so that possible dangers can be recognized in time and well avoided
Because environment friendly driving avoids high speeds so that dangerous situations occur less frequently
Because you can only drive slowly using alternative fuels

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: The queue you are driving in is overtaken in an inconsiderate manner by a car. Because of oncoming traffic the driver wants to join the queue in front of the car driving in front of you. This driver is annoyed and "closes the gap". What do you do?
explanation: In such a situation, by deliberately giving in, you should reduce the speed and giving the other road user space to go back into lane in order to reduce the risk of an accident. Remember that everyone can misjudge.
options: You give in and let the jostling driver join the queue
You also "close the gap" in order to teach the jostling driver a lesson
Nothing, since you are not concerned

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: A truck indicating to the right is driving in front of you. An impatient car driver is jostling you. What can you do?
explanation: In this situation it is better to cut back and keep a safe distance. Maybe the truck driver would like to signal that the road is clear. However, it may also be that he/she intends to stop or turn right. Only overtake if there is no danger. Increase the distance to the truck so that the pushy driver can overtake.
options: I only overtake when I am completely certain that the traffic situation allows overtaking without danger
I open up the distance to the truck to make overtaking easier for the jostling driver
I overtake because I assume that the truck driver wishes to signal to me that overtaking is possible

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: On a road not within a built-up area, a car is driving in front of you at a speed somewhat slower than that permitted. You are annoyed at the slower-moving car. What should you do?
explanation: You should definitely wait for a safe situation to overtake. Harassing someone by tailgating or flash light, however, represents a threat or even coercion. You should refrain from doing so.
options: I adjust my speed to that of the vehicle ahead
I overtake at a suitable place
I flash my headlights, until the car in front begins to drive faster

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: What can frequently lead to road traffic accidents during night-time recreational drives at the weekend?
explanation: Too little driving experience during the dark and a lack of knowledge about driving behavior in fully occupied vehicles often leads to accidents during nocturnal recreational rides on the weekend.
options: - little experience driving after dark
- little experience with fully occupied vehicles
- little knowledge of road traffic regulations

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: You are under time pressure. What must you ensure?
explanation: Even if you are under time pressure, you must follow the traffic rules. This also means that you comply with the speed limits. After all, excessive speed is THE main cause of accidents.
options: - to exceed the speed
- to drive through the traffic lights even when red
- to reduce the safety

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: Serious accidents frequently occur when young people drive cars during night-time recreational drives at weekends. What causes can be particularly relevant here?
explanation: Unreasonable speed and willingness to take risks often lead to serious accidents among young people during weekend rides at night.
options: Inappropriate speed
High risk readiness
Hesitant driving style

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: After overtaking you, a car pulls back into lane without leaving sufficient space in front of you. What should you do?
explanation: The car driver in the overtaking vehicle shows a misconduct that should not disturb you. Stay calm, do not honk and do not turn on the flash light. Decelerate slightly and restore the required safety distance between the vehicles.
options: I remain calm in order to avoid conflicts
I brake in order to ensure that the safety distance is again established
I flash my headlights in order to call attention to the impediment

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: The risk of causing an accident when driving a vehicle is significantly higher for drivers aged between 18 and 24. What reasons are frequently relevant here?
explanation: Young car drivers often have too little experience to be able to correctly assess road traffic risks. They often drive carelessly and riskily, overestimate their abilities and rely on the safety of the vehicles they control. By testing their car and their own driving skills, they sometimes get into unmanageable situations.
options: Too little driving experience
Over-estimation of own capabilities
Higher levels of risk readiness

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: While you are in a traffic jam, looking in your rear-view mirror you see a motorcyclist "snaking" past the stationary line of vehicles. What should you do?
explanation: Under no circumstances should you act illegally just because another road user violates applicable rules. It is forbidden for you as a car driver to honk in this situation, to stop the motorcyclist or to let him pass.
options: I let him drive past
I sound my horn and note his registration
I take steps to ensure that he too must come to a stop

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: You are driving on a main road and a car following behind is "tailgating" you. How should you react?
explanation: When driving on a highway and being harassed by the car behind you, you should keep calm and control your speed at an appropriate pace. You should avoid slow driving so as not to hinder the flow of traffic. However, you should also not be tempted to drive faster. It's best to let the pushy driver pass at the next opportunity.
options: I maintain my speed and keep to the right to enable the car following behind to overtake
I increase my speed until the car following behind ceases "tailgating" me
I reduce my speed until the car following behind ceases "tailgating" me

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: You overtake on a motorway. Behind you a car approaches at high speed, with headlights and indicators flashing. What should you do?
explanation: The only thing you can do is to keep calm! Stay calm and do not try to score off the pushy driver. It is best to let him pass. If you have sufficient overtaking speed, you can still complete the overtaking process. As soon as the next opportunity arises, you should switch to the right lane and let the pushy driver pass.
options: I continue overtaking swiftly
I pull over into the right-hand lane as soon as possible
I gently decelerate

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: Five young friends are driving in a car to a recreational event. The mood is exuberant. To what risks can this give rise?
explanation: For the car driver, there is a risk of getting carried away by the mood. He/She can be distracted by the others and overlook traffic hazards and make driving mistakes. It is recommended to set up rules of conduct for the passengers before starting the journey. So, the car driver is not a spoilsport or tempted in any way.
options: - be distracted from events on the road
- be induced to drive in a risky manner
- be induced to drive slowly

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: While driving on the motorway you overtake several vehicles. A vehicle approaches you from behind with indicators and headlights flashing. What should you do?
explanation: The dense, aggressive tailgating of the following vehicle endangers all road users. For this reason, you should try to change to the right-hand lane in compliance with the safety distance. Any braking maneuver would only worsen this dangerous situation. Switching on the hazard light is prohibited in this case.
options: I continue driving until I can again pull into the right-hand lane
I turn on my hazard lights briefly to urge the vehicle behind to keep its distance
I brake briefly to prompt the vehicle behind to keep its distance

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: You want to overtake. Why should you not do so?
explanation: A car driver may only overtake if he/she can see that the opposite lane is free. In this situation, the oncoming traffic cannot be seen, so you must not overtake.
options: The oncoming traffic
The bend in the road
The state of the road surface

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: You were in a bad mood prior to commencing your journey. What consequences should you avoid when driving?
explanation: Anything that could negatively affect your safe driving should be avoided. Besides distractions, this also includes aggressiveness. If you're upset, do not get behind the wheel immediately afterwards.
options: Distraction
Aggressiveness
Caution

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: Which is the stamp of a responsible driver?
explanation: A responsible car driver expects mistakes from other road users and does not sit behind the wheel while he/she is very tired or cannot control his/her feelings. Furthermore, he/she does not always insist on his right and cannot be distracted.
options: He anticipates the mistakes of other road users
He avoids driving when tired
He is assertive towards other road traffic

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: What emotions can influence driving behaviour?
explanation: Strong emotions such as anger, fear and sadness as well as joy and exuberance usually influence the driving behavior. They distract the car driver from the road and often lead to risky, aggressive or over-cautious driving. Only when you're calm and balanced you should participate in traffic.
options: Happiness and exuberance
Worry and sorrow
Anger and rage

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: What indications mean you should interrupt your journey?
explanation: Brief microsleep often causes devastating accidents. If you have to yawn frequently, can barely keep your eyes open, or have trouble keeping your lane, you should stop your journey and take a rest.
options: Yawning frequently
Difficulty keeping your eyes open
Difficulties staying in lane

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: Your passenger wants to discuss something with you during the journey. What should you do?
explanation: You should not be distracted while driving. If your passenger wants to discuss with you, you should stop the journey.
options: - my driving
- the discussion

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: During the journey your passenger informs you that you are repeatedly tailgating. What should you do?
explanation: You should take the safety advice of passengers seriously. Keep a larger distance. Within built-up areas, the distance to the vehicle in front should be at least three car lengths or approx. 15 m. Outside built-up areas, you should follow the "two-second rule of thumb".
options: I take the passenger’s comments seriously
I maintain a greater distance
I ignore the passenger’s comments

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: At a red light in a built-up area, another driver apparently wants to provoke you into a street race. What should you do?
explanation: Don't be provoked and stay calm. Since road races are strictly prohibited, you should not pay attention to this behavior.
options: I totally ignore this behaviour
I accept the challenge, but without exceeding 50 km/h
I get out and confront the driver

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: What frequently causes young people to have “disco accidents”?
explanation: Young drivers in particular have less experience driving at night with crowded vehicles. In addition, the risk of accidents increases due to distracting passengers.
options: A lack of experience driving after dark
Little experience with fully occupied vehicles
A distraction caused by passengers

chapterName: Affective Emotional Behaviour In Road Traffic
text: At a red light in a built-up area, another driver apparently wants to provoke you into a street race. What should you do?
explanation: Racing will increase your risk of accidents and put people at risk. You should ignore such behaviors
options: I totally ignore this behaviour
I accept the challenge, but without exceeding 50 km/h
I get out and confront the driver

text: You are driving on a road with one lane in each direction and want to turn left. Where should you position yourself?
explanation: When turning left in this situation, go towards the center of the road (which is the left side of your lane)
options: - towards the centre of the roadway
- on the right-hand edge of the roadway

text: Are you allowed to use your motorized bicycle on the pavement?
explanation: Yes but only if you push it, you cannot ride on the pavement
options: Yes, if the motorized bicycle is cautiously pushed
Yes, if the motorized bicycle is used as a bicycle
Yes, also using the engine when traffic on the roadway is too dense

text: Several cars are waiting in the right-hand lane at a "red" traffic light. Are you allowed to pass the cars cautiously on the right?
explanation: In this case you can behave similarly to a bicycle and can pass the car on the right if there is enough space
options: Yes, provided there is adequate space on the roadway
Yes, provided you use the pavement
No, you must always wait behind the last car

text: You are driving on a road outside a built-up area with three lanes marked in each direction. Individual slower vehicles are travelling well spaced out in the right-hand lane. Which lane may you use continuously?

text: What is the right course of action now?
explanation: The tractor seems to want to turn onto the dirt track on the right. Stay behind the tractor and wait until it has turned off. Overtaking it is dangerous because the implement installed at the rear could swerve.
options: I remain behind the tractor
I anticipate that the tractor may turn off the road
I comply with the tractor driver’s indicator-based prompt to overtake

text: You want to overtake [the blue car]. What is the right course of action?
explanation: Wait for the bike to leave the blind spot. Note that the car driver who is overtaking has to drive at a higher speed than the driver who is being overtaken. Accelerate if necessary and finish your overtaking process before the restriction on overtaking takes effect, such as a solid line.
options: - overtake at a substantially higher speed
- overtake while maintaining the speed driven
- do not overtake, because a motorbike is in moving in the blind spot

text: What could make this situation become hazardous?
explanation: The car driver approaching from behind tries to overtake you before the turn, although he/she cannot see the curve. If traffic is approaching in this situation, it can lead to dangerous evasive maneuvers by the oncoming traffic and the driver who is overtaking. The tractor next to the road is no danger.
options: Oncoming traffic
The [red car]
The tractor

text: You are driving on the motorway in a motor vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating in excess of 7.5 t. The heavy snowfall has reduced visibility to less than 50 m. What must you do?
explanation: With your vehicle that exceeds a maximum permissible gross weight of 7.5 t, you are not allowed on the leftmost lane driving, because this is there for overtaking for faster cars. You can not with your vehicle faster than 50 km / h drive. You can continue to drive on the highway even with snowfall.
options: I may not use the extreme left-hand lane
I may not drive faster than 50 km/h
I must leave the motorway at the next exit

text: You are driving outside built-up areas. Visibility is reduced to just about 50 m due to heavy rain. What applies in this situation?
explanation: Here, too (50 m due to heavy rain) applies in reduced visibility is the speed limit 50 km / h. Motor vehicles above 7.5 t street legal. Total mass is prohibited overtaking. The rear fog light does not have to be switched on.
options: Overtaking is prohibited for motor vehicles with a permissible total mass exceeding 7.5 t
The maximum permissible speed is 50 km/h
The rear fog lamp must be switched on

text: You are driving an agricultural machine. A queue of cars has formed behind you. What is correct?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Reduce speed at an appropriate place or wait in order to let the cars following you overtake
Switch on the hazard warning lights to show that overtaking is not possible
Agricultural machines are not required to let faster vehicles overtake

text: What should you do now?
explanation: In this situation, you should pull into the bus stop and let the car behind overtake you
options: I pull into the bus stop on the right, and stop there
I increase my speed
I maintain my speed and continue driving

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: What is the right course of action now?
explanation: The bottleneck is in your lane. Therefore, you must stop before the bottleneck and wait until the oncoming car has passed.
options: I stop and wait ahead of the constricted point until the oncoming car has passed through
I pass through the constricted point by carefully driving between the oncoming car and the construction site barrier
I signal to the driver of the oncoming car that he should drive closer to the edge of the roadway

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: What is the right course of action here?
explanation: The distance to the bicycle is not enough. Stop and wait until the biker has passed the bottleneck. This is the only way to be sure that you do not endanger the biker.
options: I slow down and wait
I queue behind the vehicles already waiting on the right
I continue driving at a reduced speed

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: You are approaching a "red" traffic light. Several cars are waiting in all lanes. What do you do?
explanation: You should always wait in line behind the last car in your lane and not try to pass over other cars by either side.
options: Wait in your lane behind the last car
Pass the waiting cars on the right-hand side and proceed to the stop line
Pass the waiting cars on the left-hand side and proceed to the stop line

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: Which motor vehicles may freely choose their lane inside built-up areas?
explanation: In Germany, the legal driving requirement applies. Vehicles up to 3.5 tons are excluded from the right-hand drive requirement within built-up areas and can freely choose their lane.

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: What is the right course of action now?
explanation: In Germany, you must drive on the right. As there is no vehicle in front of you that is travelling slower than you, you must move into the right lane. As soon as slower vehicles appear, you may move back into the centre or left lane to overtake them.
options: I move into the right-hand lane
I stay in the centre lane
I move into the left-hand lane

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: How could a dangerous situation arise?
explanation: The fast driving style of the yellow truck suggests that he will overtake the blue truck in front of him as well. Their speed is faster than that of the trucks. You cannot dodge to the left as a car on the left lane is directly behind you. If the yellow truck swings out, you have to brake hard.
options: - yellow truck
- green truck
- the car up ahead

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: What should you do now?
explanation: Since the driver of the car on the right of the acceleration lane increases its speed, you should enable him/her to merge into traffic. Refrain from your right of way and reduce your own speed. You cannot change on the left lane as a vehicle approaches there.
options: I let the blue car merge in front of me
I accelerate
I immediately change from the left lane to the central lane

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: What should you do?
explanation: Stay on the middle lane and delay. The leading car will also delay soon to let the car on the left lane merge into traffic, because this lane ends. You cannot go to the left, changing to the right lane would be too dangerous as well.
options: I stay in the middle lane and slow down
I move to the right-hand lane and slow down
I move into the left-hand lane and overtake the red car in front of me

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: What is the right course of action?
explanation: You drive on the middle lane and in this situation you have to stay on the lane and reduce the speed. The driver on the left lane drives more slowly. You must not overtake him from the right. You cannot change to the right lane, there is a vehicle.
options: I reduce my speed
I continue driving without changing speed
I move into the right-hand lane

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: What must you anticipate in this situation?
explanation: Since the vehicle drives very fast from the right onto the freeway, you have to expect that it will change to the middle lane. This impression is reinforced by the fact that trucks maintain their speed and distance.
options: - grey car will move into the middle lane
- yellow truck will pull out in front of me to overtake
- grey car will remain in the right-hand lane

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: What is the right course of action?
explanation: A car drives in front of you and from the right a car drives onto the main carriageway of the freeway. It is clear that the car driving on the left lane has a slower pace than you. Since it's only allowed to overtake on the left, you must delay and reduce your speed.
options: I reduce my speed and stay in the middle lane
I maintain my speed and stay in the middle lane
I maintain my speed and move into the right-hand lane

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: You are driving on a road that has several marked lanes going in one direction. When should the alternate merging procedure be employed?
explanation: The zipper merge is to be used when a lane cannot be used any further. The exception is on the motorway.
options: When a lane comes to an end
If one lane is not continuously free to traffic due to an obstacle
When a merging lane ends on the motorway

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: What is true about using the hard shoulder in this situation?
explanation: The traffic sign indicates that the hard shoulder is to be used like the right-hand lane.
options: - must be used like a right-hand lane
- may only be used in a breakdown situation
- may only be used by trucks

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: What is true in this situation about using the hard shoulder?
explanation: The hard shoulder may not be used regularly. You can only use it in case of a breakdown.
options: – may only be used in the case of a breakdown
– may only be used by trucks
– must be used in the same way as a right-hand lane

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: What is the right behaviour now?
explanation: If one of the lanes ends on a multi-lane road, vehicles must be allowed to move to the adjacent lane. Here it is important to drive with foresight in order to be able to react to lane changes in a timely manner and to adjust your own speed if necessary.
options: I reduce my speed
I let the [blue] car in front of me move over
I accelerate

chapterName: Use Of Lanes By Motor Vehicles
text: What applies to this road that is outside of a built-up area?
explanation:
This traffic sign draws you aware that you will have to choose a direction shortly. At the same time, you will receive an idea of ​​the intersection, especially the turning traces.
Therefore, you can only use the left lanes outside if you want to turn left.
options: - to perform a left turn
- to overtake
- if there is a traffic jam

text: Where are U-turns prohibited?
explanation: You may not turn your vehicle on freeways or motorways. Reverse driving is strictly prohibited on both types of roads as well.
options: On motorways
On clearways for motor vehicles only
On farm or forest tracks

text: Why do you have to wait before the left turn?
explanation: As a left-turning driver, you generally have to give priority to oncoming traffic. Cyclists also have this right of way. So, in this situation you have to let the motorcyclist pass before turning. He will pass the left-turning driver from the right and continue straight ahead.
options: - motorbike
- car
- bicycle

text: What is the right course of action?
explanation: If you want to turn left and a car wants to overtake you from the left, you have to let it pass first. Only after the car has completed its overtaking maneuver, you may turn yourself.
options: - once the [red] vehicle has overtaken me
- now in order to make the carriageway clear
- now so that following vehicles will not be confused by my slowing down

text: You want to turn left. What is the right course of action?
explanation: Since you are currently being overtaken, it is not possible to turn left. You must wait for the overtaking process to be finished before you can turn left.
options: I stop at the farm track and wait
I accelerate and swiftly take the turn
I continue driving, because I cannot turn off the road here

text: In this situation, why do you have to wait before the left turn?
explanation: In this situation, you need to wait for the motorbike behind the car to pass before turning left
options: - motorbike
- [red car]
- [bicycle]

text: What is the right course of action in this situation?
explanation: In this situation, you should first wait for the motorcycle to overtake you before turning left.
options: - after [the red car] has overtaken me
- now, so as not to impede the truck behind me
- now, so that my hesitation does not create any uncertainty in the minds of those behind me

text: Why are you not allowed to turn off the road now?
explanation: The red car is overtaking and is travelling to your left. To avoid a collision, do not turn off now under any circumstances. Check whether your indicators are dirty and therefore cannot be seen.
options: - [red car]
- bus
- oncoming traffic

text: You want to turn left at the next junction. What is the right course of action now?
explanation:
If you drive past the waiting vehicles, you could obstruct oncoming vehicles and, in the worst case, block the entire road.
Therefore, start to flash left now to signal to other road users that you want to turn into the road. Also, stay behind the waiting vehicles and only turn off when you reach the road.
options: I remain behind the stationary vehicles
I indicate left
I drive carefully to the left past the stationary vehicles

text: You want to turn left. Which line should you steer?
explanation: Keep to the centre line when turning left. This allows you to drive as far to the left as possible without driving in the opposite lane and the motorbike behind you can pass you on the right.
options: The middle driving line
The left driving line
The right driving line

text: You want to turn left. Which line should you follow?
explanation: You should keep as far to the left as possible when turning left. However, you are riding in a one-way street where cycling is permitted in both directions. You are therefore not allowed to ride on the far left because cyclists may be coming towards you. Therefore, follow the centre line.
options: The middle driving line
The left driving line
The right driving line

text: You want to turn left. Which line should you follow?
explanation: If you want to turn left in a one-way street, you should keep as far to the left as possible, so follow the left lane.
options: The left driving line
The middle driving line
The right driving line

text: What is the right course of action when reversing?
explanation: When reversing, look to the rear and additionally secure the traffic area by looking all around, drive attentively and slowly and, for safety reasons, make sure that there are no persons in the blind spot.
options: - ensure the road area is safe by additionally looking all around me
- drive slowly and attentively
- make sure that no-one is located in my blind spot

text: You are driving a motor vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating in excess of 3.5 t. At what speed do you have to turn right within a built-up area?
explanation: Drive at walking speed to avoid danger and accidents.
options: - walking speed
- at 20 km/h maximum
- at 30 km/h maximum

text: Your vehicle is equipped with a rear view camera. You want to reverse into a forecourt from a very busy road. What must you be aware at this time?
options: I should additionally arrange a look-out to help guide me in
I must also observe the traffic directly
I can rely solely on the rear view camera

text: What can reduce the risk of serious accidents when turning right within a built-up area?
options: By equipping vehicles with turn assist systems
By driving at walking speed when turning right
By taking rights turns quickly so as not to impede other road users

text: You want to reverse your vehicle out of a property lot onto a road. What must you do?
explanation: To drive backwards from a property to a road, it is not enough just to use the rear view camera. You should be instructed on the street if necessary and keep in mind that pedestrians have priority.
options: - arrange for someone to direct me, if necessary
- allow pedestrians right of way
- only use the rear view camera

text: When turning right, there is a risk of overlooking cyclists travelling straight ahead in the blind spot. How can you reduce this risk?
explanation:
When a bus or truck turns right, there is a risk of overlooking cyclists driving straight ahead in the blind spot. To minimize the risk, you should observe the following and side traffic at short intervals, make sure that your mirrors are adjusted correctly and ensure that no accessories are obstructing your view.
This way you can recognize cyclists in good time and avoid accidents.
options: I monitor the traffic behind and to the side at short intervals
I make sure the mirrors are adjusted correctly
I make sure that accessories in the cab do not obstruct the view

text: You have mounted a plough which extends far beyond the back of your tractor. What must you remember when you turn right?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Turn only when there is no danger for oncoming traffic caused by the plough moving over
No-one can be endangered when turning if the plough is marked by warning panels

text: You have mounted a plough which extends far beyond the back of your tractor. Who can be endangered when you turn right?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Vehicles travelling behind you wishing to overtake
Vehicles in the lane on your left
Vehicles parking on the right-hand side

text: To your tractor you have attached a hay turning machine that projects a long way to the back. Who could be endangered by this when you take a left turn?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Vehicles that have pulled in alongside me to my right
Pedestrians on the right-hand side of the road
Vehicles that have pulled in behind me

text: You are driving an agricultural tractor with two trailers and you want to take a right turn. What must you look out for?
explanation: Since the room increases your agricultural tractor with two trailers when turning to the right, please make sure that the supporters do not compromise when turning people on the edge of the road or on the sidewalk, and if there are right next to you cyclists that are hidden by the blind spot ,
options: Whether there are any cyclists alongside me to the right
That during the turn the trailers will not endanger any pedestrians on the side of the road or on the footpath
That I remember to switch on my hazard lights if I have to swing out far to the left when taking the turn

text: You are returning on a tractor from working in a field and want to turn onto a road. What should you observe in order to avoid dangerous situations?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Keep windscreen clean
Avoid places where drivers with the right of way cannot be seen from an adequate distance
Be directed onto the road if my vision is restricted

text: Where is stopping prohibited?
explanation: In general, the road traffic act prohibits stopping at the traffic areas when stopping is dangerous for other road users or endangers public safety and order. This is especially true for holding on the lanes of the freeway or on a highway. The same goes for sharp and confusing curves.
options: Outside parking areas on autobahns and clearways for motor vehicles only
Near or on sharp bends
At bus stops

text: Where is parking prohibited?
explanation: A parking ban in accordance with the road traffic act applies in all places where other road users can be obstructed or the public order and safety is no longer guaranteed by parked cars. For example, parking is prohibited at taxi stands, narrow lanes or entrances and exits in front of property as well as on and up to 5 m before pedestrian crossings.
options: On narrow roadways opposite driveway entrances and exits
At taxi ranks
Immediately behind pedestrian crossings

text: Who has priority at this parking space?
explanation: The vehicle that reaches the parking space first always has priority. Priority will also be given in the event that the vehicle drives past the parking space just in order to park backwards or perform other movements that are useful for parking in this gap. Priority is also maintained when the vehicle is waiting at the parking space.
options: The white vehicle, because it has arrived at the parking space first
No one, both drivers should agree
Me, because I am parking by driving in forwards

text: What do you have to consider when parking your motorbike?
explanation: The motorbike must not obstruct or endanger anyone. Make sure that the motorbike is parked safely and in a space-saving manner.
options: - may not obstruct anyone
- may not fall over
- must be positioned on the sidewalk

text: When are you allowed to park your two-wheeler on the footpath?
explanation: Basically, the lane is to be used for parking a vehicle. Motorbikes may be parked anywhere where car parking is permitted. In general, parking on sidewalks for motorcycles is not permitted unless a traffic sign permits it.
options: When a traffic sign indicates this is permitted
If the footpath is at least 2.0 m wide
If there are no other options

text: What should you take into account when parking a two-wheeler?
explanation:
When you park your motorbike or scooter, the same rules and prohibitions apply to you as for car drivers. This means that you are not allowed to simply park your motorbike or scooter on the pavement. You must park your bike on the road, just like car owners. Parking on the pavement is also only permitted for motorbikes or scooters in marked parking spaces or if appropriate traffic signs permit this.
You should also always pay attention to the surface on which you park your motorbike; if the surface is too soft or too uneven, your motorbike can quickly fall over and cause other hazards.
options: I should not park the two-wheeler on soft underground
I may park the two-wheeler on footpaths only if this is appropriately signed
When parking the two-wheeler I am released from the duty to display a parking disc

text: Both cars want to park here. Which car takes precedence?
explanation: In this case, the red car has right of way. He has reached the parking space first. Priority will also be given in the event that the vehicle drives past the parking space just in order to park backwards or perform other movements that are useful for parking in this gap.
options: The red car
The white car

text: Up to which permissible total mass may motor vehicles be parked on specially designated footpaths?
explanation: Vehicles with a maximum permissible gross vehicle weight of up to 2.8 tonnes may be parked on specially marked sidewalks.

text: What is the minimum distance a vehicle must leave clear in front of traffic lights if the traffic lights would be concealed by the vehicle?
explanation: A minimum distance of 10 meters must be maintained so that the view of light signals is not obscured.

text: Where are you allowed to park a trailer with a permissible total mass exceeding 2 t in built-up areas regularly on sundays and public holidays and between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.?
explanation: Parking a trailer with a maximum authorized mass of more than 2 t is permitted in commercial and residential areas with appropriately marked parking spaces. Within closed areas and in special areas for recreational purposes, regular parking is prohibited from 22:00 to 6:00 and on Sundays as well as on public holidays.
options: In industrial areas
In wholly residential areas, on specially designated parking spaces
In special areas reserved for recreation purposes, on sufficiently wide roads

text: What must you remember when parking a trailer without a truck?
explanation: Please note that you may not leave your vehicle trailers on regular parking spaces for more than two weeks if they are not attached to a towing vehicle. Incidentally, the same also applies to hard shoulders. Accordingly marked parking lots are excluded from this regulation.
options: - may not be parked for more than 2 weeks on public roads
- may be parked for more than 2 weeks on specially designated parking spaces
- may be parked for an unlimited period of time on adequate hard shoulders

text: You want to park on the right-hand edge of the road. What should you do in this situation?
explanation: You signalled first and therefore have priority to the parking space. To avoid a conflict, you should still give up the parking space.
options: I forego the parking space, even though I have priority
I park now, because I have priority

text: You want to park on the right-hand edge of the road. Who has priority in this situation?
explanation: The car that stopped in front of you signaled first and therefore had priority in the parking lot. If you park now, there could be a collision.
options: The [blue] car has priority
I have priority
No one has priority. We have to agree

text: You want to reverse park on the right-hand side of the road. What is correct in this situation?
explanation:
When parking, you always have to pay attention to the oncoming and subsequent traffic, as you could leave your lane when you steer and thereby endanger other road users.
Also make sure that no other vehicle wants to leave its parking space to avoid accidents.
options: I closely observe the oncoming traffic before manoeuvring into the space
I anticipate that vehicles may exit their parking spaces
I switch on my hazard lights

text: Where are you allowed to park motor vehicles with a permissible total mass exceeding 7.5 t in built-up areas regularly on sundays and public holidays and between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.?
explanation: In a residential area you would at these times not to win a lot of friends. (Volume) Please parke in industrial areas or designated parking spaces in the spa and clinic areas.
options: In health resorts and hospital areas, on specially designated parking spaces
In industrial areas
In wholly residential areas, on sufficiently wide roads

text: Where are you allowed to park regular buses in built-up areas regularly on sundays and public holidays and between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: In industrial areas
At any bus stop
In wholly residential areas

text: Before which sign must you maintain a distance of at least 10 m, if it would otherwise be concealed by your vehicle?
explanation: In front of signs such as the diagonal crosses, light signals or the sign "Stop! Yield to cross traffic", you at least have to keep a distance of 10 meters. This is especially necessary if they are going to be covered by your vehicle. For example, you are allowed to come to a stop in front of a stop sign. Behind it, however, stopping is prohibited.
options: Diagonal cross
Stop. Give way.
No stopping

text: You want to park on the right-hand side edge of the carriageway. How big is the mandatory minimum distance between your vehicle and the solid lane boundary line?
explanation: If a minimum distance of 3 meters to the lane boundary line is observed when parking, the parked car will not present an obstacle.

text: Where must you use a parking disc for parking?
explanation: Wherever traffic signs dictate, the car driver must use a parking disc. It is also used when a defective parking meter makes the withdrawal of a valid parking ticket impossible. The use of a parking disc for a limited stopping restriction does not entitle you to park here for more than three minutes.
options: At a defective parking meter
Where stipulated by traffic signs
In a no-waiting area

text: The time on a parking meter has not yet run out. What do you do?
explanation: If a parking meter has not yet expired, you may use the rest of the parking time and leave your vehicle for free at the parking lot for the remaining time. You do not need a parking disc for this.
options: - use the time left on the meter without inserting more money
- not use the time left on the meter
- only use the time left on the meter when using a parking disc

text: At 10.40, you enter an area where parking is allowed for 2 hours when using a parking disc. What time must you set on the parking disc?
explanation: The pointer of the disc should be adjusted to the stroke of half an hour following the time of parking. If you arrive at 10.40 hours, the pointer should be at 11.00. Thereby the parking duration does not matter.

text: You want to park in a car park where there is a parking-ticket machine. What must you remember?
explanation: The car driver must put the valid parking ticket from in the vehicle so that it is visible from the outside. Avoid exceeding the parking time printed on the receipt, also referred to as a parking ticket. A parking disc as a replacement for a parking ticket is only valid if the parking meter is defective.
options: Place a valid parking ticket in your vehicle so it is easy to read from outside
Do not exceed the parking time indicated on the parking ticket
A parking ticket is never needed when using a parking disc

text: When may you remain parked at a parking meter without activating it?
explanation: After field work, the lighting and signaling device must be cleaned if necessary. The parking time doesn't need to be monitored while entering or exiting and loading or unloading. When driving slowly up to the priority road, the road must be sufficiently visible.
options: To allow people to get in and out of the vehicle
To load and unload the vehicle
To do some quick shopping

text: How must you safeguard your motorcycle against unauthorized use?
explanation: To avoid other people to use your motorcycle, remove the ignition key and lock the steering.
options: By removing the ignition key
By locking the steering
By engaging top gear

text: You want to park your motorcycle on its prop stand. What do you have to consider?
explanation: To avoid your motorcycle to tip over, make sure the surface is firm and can support the weight of the motorcycle and that you swing the side stand all the way up to the stop.
options: The surface under the prop stand must be firm
You must extend the prop stand to the end position
You should only park your motorcycle on an upward slope

text: You want to park your motorcycle on its main stand. What do you have to consider?
explanation: To avoid your motorcycle to tip over, make sure the surface is firm and can support the weight of the motorcycle. You can park your bike that way for a short or long time.
options: The surface under the main stand must be firm
You may only use the main stand to park your motorcycle for a short time

text: Where should you not park a motorcycle (using main or side stand)?
explanation: To avoid your motorcycle to tip over, make sure the surface is firm and can support the weight of the motorcycle. Also make sure that the surface is not too steep downwards which would make the main or side stand unsafe and at risk of tipping over
options: On soft ground
Where the parking surface is a steep downward slope
On firm ground

text: Which precautionary measures must you take when parking a motorcycle?
explanation: You must make sure that no other people can use your motorcycle by removing the ignition key and locking in the handlebar/steering. Also make sure that the groud is firm to avoid the motorcycle to tip over.
options: Park on firm ground
Remove the ignition key
Lock the handlebar

text: You want to park your motorcycle. What must you consider?
explanation: When parking, to avoid your motorcycle to tip over, make sure the surface is firm and can support the weight of the motorcycle.
options: The parking surface must be firm
You can lean the motorcycle against a lamppost if you put it into gear
You must switch on the dipped headlight

text: How do you secure your motorcycle against being used without permission?
explanation: The steering lock prevents steering in the event of unauthorised access. The engine cannot be started by removing the ignition key.
options: - remove the ignition key
- close the steering lock
- disconnect the battery

text: What must you be aware of when using a prop stand?
explanation: If the side stand is not fully retracted, it can cause a fall when cornering. If the slope is too great, the motorbike can slide forward because the side stand folds in on its own. If the ground is too soft, the motorbike may sink until it falls.
options: The gradient of the parking place
The characteristics of the ground surface
That the prop stand is completely folded away before driving off

text: What should be noted when using the prop stand?
explanation:
If the side stand is still folded out and you engage a gear, the side stand switch will automatically switch off the engine. The side stand switch is a safety measure that prevents you from riding off with the side stand folded out.
The side stand is designed for parking a motorbike. Try to avoid slopes when parking. Always make sure that your motorbike is stable and that the side stand is fully extended to avoid danger and damage.
options: Where possible, the motorbike should not be parked on a slope
The prop stand should be fully extended
The prop stand switch can prevent you driving off with the prop stand extended

text: How must you safeguard your vehicle against theft?
explanation: To secure the car against theft, you must first close all the windows and doors. The ignition key must be removed in any case. Snap the steering wheel lock into place to additionally secure the car.
options: By removing the ignition key, engaging the steering wheel lock and closing the windows
By locking the doors and boot
By activating the differential lock

text: What must you do when leaving your car?
explanation: Before leaving the vehicle, you have to protect it against rolling away uncontrolled, for example on a downhill slope. Before exiting you have to make sure not to endanger other road users. This also applies to your passengers. Opening doors carelessly when getting out is a common cause of accidents.
