The vehicle must also be protected against unauthorized use.
options: Before opening the door, look out for traffic behind
Secure the vehicle against rolling away
Secure the vehicle against unauthorized use

text: Your car is standing on the edge of the roadway. What should you do when getting into the car?
explanation: When entering and exiting, you must take care not to endanger the other road users. The entry from the right - from the sidewalk - is safer, but not without any danger. Before you open the doors, make sure that the traffic situation permits that. Make sure that there are no pedestrians or cyclists on the sidewalk at this time.
options: Let passengers get into the car, if possible, from the pavement
Open the doors on the roadway side only when traffic permits
The doors on the right-hand side can always be opened without danger

text: What is important when children are getting in and out of a car?
explanation: As a car driver, you should make sure that children get on and off directly on the sidewalk. If the situation does not allow this, they should only get in or out on the side of the road under the supervision of an adult. Children are seen worse and are unpredictable in their behavior.
options: Let the children in or out, if possible, on the pavement side
Let the children in or out on the roadway side only under supervision
Children are not allowed to get in or out of a car on public roads

text: What should you call the attention of your passengers to before exiting?
explanation: As a car driver you must take the necessary measures to avoid accidents or traffic disruptions when passengers leave the vehicle. Point that out to passengers when they get off on a bike path. Cyclists are not required to wait on bike paths. Anyone entering or leaving the car may not endanger other road users.
options: - they should heed the traffic flowing on the left-side
- they should heed the pedestrians walking on the right-side
- cyclists are required to wait on cycle paths

text: Why may you not exit now?
explanation: Anyone getting in or out of the car must behave in such a way as to avoid endangering other road users. An approaching cyclist can be seen in your left-hand side mirror, you must let him pass first.
options: Because [of the cyclist]
Because of the motorbike
Because [of the pedestrian]

text: You have stopped in a parking strip and now want to exit your vehicle. What must you do in this situation?
explanation: Before you open the door and leave the vehicle, check in the left-hand mirror that no one is coming from behind. You must also look to your left to make sure that there are no other vehicles in your blind spot.
options: - by looking in my left-hand exterior rear-view mirror before opening the door
- by glancing over my left shoulder before opening the door
- just by looking through the slightly opened door

text: When leaving your car, how do you secure it against unauthorised use?
explanation: You have to make sure that no unauthorised persons use your car. Therefore, remove the key from the starter and make sure that all windows and doors are closed.
options: I lock the doors
I close the windows
I activate the child-safety lock

text: You want to let a child out of your car. What should you be aware of when doing so?
explanation: As a car driver, you should make sure that children get on and off directly on the pavement side. If the situation does not allow this, they should only get in or out of the vehicle on the carriageway side under supervision and with prior warning of possible dangers. Children are harder to see and their behaviour is unpredictable, so you should make sure that they no longer have to cross the road.
options: - exit the car on the same side as the footpath
- not have to cross over the carriageway
- be warned of possible dangers when getting out of the car

text: What is allowed when your motorcycle has broken down with engine damage?
explanation: You cannot tow a broken motorcycle, it will tip over and fall. Instead you should either push it or transport it.
options: Loading the motorcycle on a vehicle and having it transported
Pushing the motorcycle to the nearest garage
Having the motorcycle towed

text: You are outside of a built-up area and have come to a stop due to a fault with your motorcycle. How should it be transported to the garage?
explanation:
The operation of a vehicle that is no longer traffic -proof is a significant and, above all, incalculable danger for you and for other road users. Therefore, you have to pull your vehicle out of traffic in the shortest way. You can have your strength bike removed on a suitable trailer or van.
According to § 15a (4) StVO, motorcycles must not be towed with a tow rope.
options: On a suitable trailer
In a suitable van
By using a suitable towrope

text: You want to tow another vehicle with your car. What must you know?
explanation: You need to know if it is a vehicle with a gearshift, automatic transmission or an electric car. An electric car cannot be towed, it must be loaded. A vehicle with an automatic transmission can only be towed for a few kilometers in level "N" without any damage.
options: You must at least have a driving permit class B
You must at least have a driving permit class BE

text: A car with servo brakes has broken down with engine damage. What is correct when towing the car away?
explanation: If possible, use a tow bar when towing a vehicle with a brake booster. Because a brake booster works only with the engine running. When the engine is off, only a weak braking effect can be achieved in this vehicle even with strong pressure on the foot brake.
options: The car being towed can only achieve slight braking effect even when increased pressure is applied to the pedal
If possible, use a tow-bar
The action of the foot brake is not impaired by the engine not running

text: A car with power steering has broken down with engine damage and must be towed away. What is correct?
explanation: The function of the power steering depends on the engine and only works when the engine is running. If the engine and the assistive function of the power steering fail, steering is considerably more difficult and you need more power. The steering is impaired in its function.
options: - is considerably heavier
- is locked
- is not impaired

text: At what distance must the warning triangle be placed when a car has broken down on a road with fast-moving traffic?
explanation: If you are staying on a road with fast traffic with your vehicle, you must set up the warning triangle at a distance of approx. 100 m. Make the breakdown situation visible to other road users by switching on the hazard lights.
options: At a distance of around 100 m
At a distance of around 50 m
At a distance of around 10 m

text: At night, how must you secure a vehicle which has broken down at a place where it constitutes a danger to other traffic?
explanation: If a vehicle has a breakdown on a multi-lane roadway at a location where it cannot be detected in time as an obstacle, you as a car driver must immediately turn on the hazard lights. Afterwards, a breakdown triangle should be placed clearly visible at a sufficient distance, in fast traffic about 100 m in front of the vehicle. You do not need to switch on the reversing light.
options: Immediately switch on the hazard warning lights
Place a warning triangle at a sufficient distance
Switch on the reversing lights

text: When must you switch on the hazard warning lights?
explanation: If a car breaks down on a multi-lane roadway at a location where it cannot be recognized in time as an obstacle, the hazard light must be switched on immediately. Parking in the second row is generally prohibited. This does not change just by switching on the hazard lights. It is not allowed. When loading and unloading the hazard light must not be switched on.
options: When your vehicle has broken down at a place where it cannot readily be recognized as a stationary obstruction
When double-parking
For all loading or unloading

text: What must you remember when towing?
explanation: When towing, the distance between the towing vehicle and the towed vehicle shall not exceed 5 meters. The tools used such as rod or rope are clearly marked. Motorcycles must not be towed but must be loaded.
options: The distance between the vehicles must not exceed 5 m
Tow-rope/tow-bar must be clearly marked
Motorcycles may only be towed with a fixed connection

text: Your car suffers a flat tyre on the motorway. What should you do?
explanation: If your vehicle breaks down on a multi-lane road due to a flat tire in a place where it cannot be detected in time as a stationary obstacle, immediately turn on the hazard lights. After that, a breakdown triangle is to be placed in a clearly visible position at a sufficient distance. In fast traffic, the distance between the vehicle and the breakdown triangle should be approx. 100 m.
options: - turn on my hazard lights and park as far to the right as possible
- place the warning triangle at a distance of about 100 m
- continue driving to the next exit

text: You car has a fault and can no longer be driven. What must you be aware of during towing?
explanation: Keep in mind that without the engine working, the brake boosters of the engine brake will also fail. This means that the applied braking force is much higher than when the engine is running. If possible, always use a tow bar when towing. The towing bar prevents collision and braking forces can be transmitted.
options: - the force required to operate the brake pedal is significantly greater if the engine has failed
- a towing bar should be used where possible
- the rear fog lights should also be switched on to indicate the towing procedure

text: You car has a fault and can no longer be driven. What must you be aware of during towing?
explanation: When towing, the towing vehicle and the towed vehicle must turn on the hazard lights. The tow rope should be kept as tight as possible. If the breakdown did not occur on the freeway, it is not allowed to drive onto the freeway during towing.
options: - the hazard lights must be switched on on both vehicles
- the towing cable should be kept as taut as possible
- the motorway may only be used to shorten the journey to the next car garage

text: You experience a breakdown outside of a built-up area. Your motor vehicle is located on the carriageway behind a bend in the road. What is the right course of action in this situation?
explanation: To secure the area, the car driver must turn on the hazard lights and set up a sign behind the vehicle to warn other road users. In addition, you should wear a safety vest for improved visibility.
options: I have to turn on my hazard lights
I must at least position a conspicuous warning sign behind the vehicle
I should wear a high-visibility vest

text: Your car has an engine fault and must be towed away with a tow rope. What must you be aware of?
explanation: Observe the manufacturer's specifications when towing. The electronic aids fail, so be prepared for sluggish steering.
options: A malfunctioning car with assisted steering is difficult to steer
When towing an electric vehicle, it is necessary to following the manufacturer’s guidelines
Driving licence class BE is the minimum required in order to tow a car

text: You experience a breakdown outside of a built-up area. Your car is situated on the carriageway, behind a bend in the road. Which is correct in this situation?
explanation: Before you leave the vehicle, you must switch on the hazard warning lights and put on a high-visibility waistcoat. This way, other road users can recognise you and react to you. Out of town, a warning triangle must be placed at a distance of 100 m from the vehicle.
options: I have to switch on my hazard lights
I have to place at least one well-visible warning sign about 100 m behind the vehicle
I should wear a hi-vis vest

text: You have to change a tyre on the hard shoulder of the motorway. What safeguard is necessary?
explanation: Since you is you on the highway, be driven on the very high speeds, you should change a tire, place the warning triangle in about 100 m distance clearly visible on the right edge of the roadway. All activities carry a warning vest and place a warning light at a sufficient distance.
options: I have to set up the warning triangle in a well-visible position at a distance of 100 m on the edge of the right-hand lane
I have to set up the warning light at an adequate distance
I should wear a high-visibility vest at all times

text: Where is it permitted to flash headlights to indicate your intention to overtake?
explanation: Outside built-up areas, you as a car driver may use the flashlight to signal your intention to overtake. This is allowed during the day and in the dark. Within built-up areas the flash light may not be used.
options: In daylight outside built-up areas
In darkness outside built-up areas
In darkness in built-up areas

text: When must you switch on the hazard lights on your vehicle?
explanation: If your car breaks down in a blind spot, you should warn other road users with your hazard warning lights. While your car is being towed away, you must switch on the hazard warning lights.
options: - experiences a breakdown at a place where the view is obscured
- is being towed
- is briefly double-parked by me

text: How can you tell whether the rear fog lamp is switched on?
explanation: A look at the dashboard is enough and the car driver immediately recognizes from the yellow warning light that the rear fog-lamp is in operation. According to the highway traffic act, the warning light must be in direct field of vision.
options: By the amber indicator light
By the blue indicator light
By the red indicator light

text: Your motorcycle is fitted with a fog headlamp. What must you remember about lighting when it is foggy?
explanation: When it is foggy, you are less visible to other people on the road. To increase your visibility you may use your headlamp instead or with dipped headlights
options: The fog headlamp may be used instead of dipped headlight
The fog headlamp may be used with dipped headlight
You may drive with parking lights only

text: It is dark and the main beam fails because the bulb filament has burnt out. What must you do?
explanation: You need to make sure that you are both visible to other people on the road and that you are yourself able to see the road. Make sure to replace the bulb as soon as possible in the meantime immediately switch on dipped headlights.
options: Immediately switch to dipped headlight
Replace the bulb as soon as possible
Proceed slowly to the nearest garage using parking lights

text: Visibility is considerably reduced. When are you allowed to switch on fog headlamps?
explanation: If the visibility during the day is badly affected by fog, snowfall or rain, then you, as a car driver, have to switch on to low beam. Only in weather conditions with strong visual impairment you may also turn on the fog lights.
options: In rain
In falling snow
In fog

text: You are driving at night on an unlit road. There is a motor vehicle travelling a short distance in front of you. Which lights must you have on?
explanation: The car driver must turn on the low beam on his own vehicle in order not to blind vehicles driving in front of you nor oncoming traffic. Using high beam is out of the question, as it would dazzle the other driver.
options: Dipped headlights
Full beam
Only side lights

text: The rear lighting systems of your car are covered. What has to be done?
explanation: You must always attach a light carrier with all the rear lights to your vehicle. Keep in mind that you as a car driver are responsible for the effectiveness of the lighting equipment. A kilometer limit does not exist in this situation.
options: - must be attached in any case
- need only be attached for journeys at dusk or during the hours of darkness
- need only be attached on journeys longer than 5 km

text: Depending on the motor vehicle, how can you tell if the main beam is switched on?
explanation: The blue indicator with the headlight symbol indicates that the high beam is on. In addition, you can recognize the position of the switch by touching it whether the main beam is turned on or not. The green warning light does not represent high beam, but low beam.
options: - position of the control switch
- blue indicator light
- green indicator light

text: As a basic rule, what lights of a motor vehicle must be turned on when driving in darkness?
explanation: In Germany it is compulsory to switch on the dipped headlights in the dark. When the low beam is switched on, you see more and you are also seen better.
options: The dipped headlight
Only the parking light
The driving beam

text: How can you tell that your main beam lights are switched on?
explanation: The blue control light indicates that the high beam is switched on.
options: - blue indicator lamp
- green indicator lamp
- red indicator lamp

text: When are you allowed to use fog headlamps also during the day?
explanation: In the event of heavy weather-related visibility restriction due to fog, snow or rain, fog lights may be switched on during the day. These strong weather-related restrictions of visibility usually only occur in autumn and winter months. You are generally not allowed to drive with ice on the windscreen. You need to remove it before starting your journey.
options: - by fog or falling snow
- by rain
- by ice on the windscreen

text: When are you allowed to switch on rear fog lamps?
explanation: The rear fog-lamps of your vehicle may only be used if the visibility is less than 50 m in heavy fog. Due to the high risk of glare, the lights can otherwise become a security risk for subsequent traffic.
options: When fog reduces visibility to less than 50 m
When fog reduces visibility to 100 m
When visibility is reduced by heavy rain

text: Where is it sufficient to use your parking lights while your car is parked on an unlit roadway?
explanation: Cars may only be parked on unlit roads with parking lights switched on within built-up areas. Because within built-up areas, people drive at lower speeds, so that the parked car can be detected in time. Outside built-up areas this is not permitted.
options: In built-up areas
Outside built-up areas
On the hard shoulder of autobahns

text: When you are driving, how can you tell whether the headlights are switched on full beam?
explanation: Usually there is a blue indicator light in the area of ​​the speedometer which indicates the function of the high beam. If this blue light is turned on, the main beam of your vehicle is switched on as well.
options: By a blue indicator light
By a red indicator light
By a green indicator light

text: Which dangers can arise from a manual light range adjustment being incorrectly set?
explanation: The headlamp beam height control is there to adjust the orientation of the headlamps to the load of the vehicle. If set incorrectly, they are either set too low - the visibility is too low - or too high. If they are set too high, it blinds oncoming traffic. The head lamps themselves are therefore not enough.
options: Oncoming traffic may be dazzled
Visibility may be too low
Headlamps may fail

text: Are you allowed to drive only with side lights (parking lights) in darkness?
explanation: With marker lights alone, you are not allowed to ride as a car driver under any circumstances. A synonymous designation for marker light is parking light. The name says it all: Parking light is intended exclusively for stationary, possibly parked cars.
options: No
Yes, if you are driving in a queue outside built-up areas
Yes, if the roadway is sufficiently lit in built-up areas

text: When must you use dipped headlights also during the day?
explanation: If visibility is severely limited due to weather conditions - rain, fog, snowfall - you must use the prescribed lighting equipment, usually low beam, even during the daytime driving. This is necessary to be seen better by other road users and to help you see the others better.
options: - by fog or falling snow
- by rain
- by a misted windscreen

text: During twilight or the hours of darkness, when must you have your side lights switched on as a minimum requirement?
explanation: At dusk and in the dark always drive with low beam. So, you are clearly visible and you can see well yourself. Vehicles are not allowed to only drive with parking light, because the luminosity of these lights, which are also known as the sidelights, is not sufficient.
options: When the vehicle is parked on the hard shoulder outside built-up areas
When driving on roads with adequate continuous lighting

text: When do you have to switch on your dipped headlights?
explanation: In poor visibility you must always turn on the low beam. This is always the case during dusk, in darkness or in weather-related poor visibility conditions such as rain, fog or snow. Even if you drive through a tunnel, you must always turn on the low beam.
options: During twilight
When it is dark
When driving through a tunnel

text: What can be the consequence of wrongly setting the headlamp levelling control?
explanation:
If the headlights are set too high, you will dazzle oncoming traffic. If the headlights are set too low, they will barely illuminate the road and you will not have sufficient visibility ahead.
If the headlights are set incorrectly, the lights may not turn off completely.
options: The oncoming traffic may be dazzled by my dipped headlights
My car's headlamp range may be too short
The life-cycle of the light bulb for the headlights may be reduced

text: What is the function of your vehicle’s high-beam assist during hours of darkness?
explanation:
The assistant switches the high beam on and off automatically so that other road users are not dazzled.
The high beam is only switched on automatically if the road is not sufficiently lit.
options: - dims the high beam in good time when there is oncoming traffic
- activates the high beam when the ambient conditions are suitable
- cleans the headlamp for the high beam

text: In what situation might your high-beam assist be unable to dim your vehicle’s high beam in good time when encountering oncoming traffic?
explanation: When crossing a crest and driving through a bend, the high beam assist camera may not be able to recognise oncoming traffic in time. Switch off the high beam manually when you notice it so as not to dazzle oncoming traffic and endanger yourself.
options: When driving over a summit
When driving around a bend in the road
When dazzled by an oncoming vehicle

text: The automatic lighting system is activated on your car. What should you anticipate when driving in the lighting conditions shown?
explanation: The light and visibility conditions are poor due to the low sun and foggy air. However, the automatic light system does not recognise poor light conditions. Switch on the low beam manually so that following road users can see you better.
options: The low beam does not turn on automatically
I will only be seen very late by the road users behind me
The automatic lighting system will switch on my fog lights

text: Which vehicles must always be marked by their own lights or parking warning plates when parked on the roadway at dusk or in darkness in built-up areas?
explanation: Trucks and recreational vehicles above 3.5 t permissible gross weight and trailers can be parked in town on the road when you're recognizable with a parking warning board or its own light source. Cars do not need this light source.
options: Trucks and motor caravans with a permissible total mass exceeding 3.5 t
Trailers
Cars

text: Which vehicles must be equipped with amber reflectors on their sides?
explanation: To make the long side more visible, you should on tractors that run on attachment, which are longer than 6 m, attach a yellow reflector. The same applies for trailers have fixed the attached implements.
options: Tractors which are longer than 6 m including any mounted implements
Trailers and attached working equipment
All multiple-track motor vehicles

text: You have finished working in the fields and want to drive home on public roads with your tractor. It is already dusk. What must you do?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Switch on the lights even though you can still see well
Check lights and clean when necessary
Switch on the work lights too so you can be seen more clearly

text: You are driving with main beam lights on in darkness. When do you have to dip your headlights?
explanation: You must not dazzle the oncoming traffic with high beam. So, turn it off immediately if you realize that other vehicles are driving towards you. Pedestrians will not be dazzled by your high beam if they travel in the same direction as you.
options: When a vehicle is oncoming
When a vehicle is driving close in front
If there are pedestrians in front moving in the same direction

text: You are driving with main beam lights on in darkness. When do you have to dip your headlights?
explanation: When driving in the dark with high beam, you need to turn it off when approaching oncoming traffic. You are not allowed to drive with high beam on roads that have sufficient lighting throughout. The head lamps of waiting vehicles should not blind others. That's why you have to dip your lights at railroad crossings. If pedestrians precede in the same direction, they are not dazzled by the high beam.
options: If I am driving on a road with constant, adequate lighting
If I am required to wait at a rail crossing and dazzling others
If there are pedestrians moving in the same direction in front of me

text: Why must you also drive with dipped headlight during the day when visibility is impaired by fog, rain or falling snow?
explanation: If visibility is poor during the day, due to weather conditions such as rain, fog or snow, you as the driver must switch on the low beam. The primary concern here is that your vehicle is better seen by other road users. The traffic signs are not better seen from a greater distance.
options: So that you will be more easily seen by other road users
So that you can drive at a higher speed
So that you can see traffic signs at greater distances

text: When are you required to drive with dipped headlights or daytime running lights?
explanation: For your safety and the safety of other people, you should be visible by always having either the dipped headlights or running lights on
options: For every journey
Only when driving in built-up areas
Only when visibility is poor

text: When must attachments have additional lighting systems?
explanation: That need to cover the lighting equipment of your vehicle attachments are additionally with illuminated. The same applies to the stand out by more than one meter above the reflectors out. And when the implement laterally by more than 40 cm above the Begenzungs- or tail lights of the vehicle protruding.
options: - blocks the vehicle's lighting system
- projects more than 40 cm laterally beyond the vehicle's front and rear position lamps
- projects by more than 1 m beyond the vehicle's retro-reflectors

text: You are driving on the autobahn and there is a traffic jam. What is correct?
explanation: During a traffic jam, a motorcycle has to behave like a regular car. It cannot drive in between other vehicles or use the hard shoulder.
options: Drive up to the queue carefully, maintaining the required safety distance
Proceed between the other vehicles
Proceed on the hard shoulder

text: What is allowed on autobahns?
explanation: On the freeway/autobahn, a motorcycle has to behave like a regular car. It can stop on the hard shoulder in case of breakdown. It cannot share a line with another vehicle and cannot leave on a farm track
options: Stopping on the hard shoulder in case of a breakdown
Driving beside another vehicle in the same lane
Leaving the autobahn on a farm track

text: What is the recommended speed that applies to cars and motorcycles on autobahns?
explanation: On motorways cars and motorcycles have to keep an advisory speed limit of 130 km/h. In addition, driving on a freeway is only permitted to vehicles exceeding 60 km/h.

text: You are driving in the left of two lanes and approaching a vehicle that has just started to overtake. What do you do?
explanation: You allow this vehicle to overtake by maintaining a safety distance. As the vehicle changes from the right, be prepared that its speed is lower than yours despite acceleration. Slow your pace down, if necessary. Never tailgate, honk or flash.
options: Keep an adequate distance behind the vehicle in front
Allow the vehicle in front to overtake
Close up to the vehicle in front, sound your horn and flash your lights

text: You are driving on the autobahn in light traffic. How long are you allowed to stay in the left-hand lane?
explanation: The left lane may generally only be used for the purpose of overtaking. If the preceding vehicle overtakes, it can be assumed that the following car driver will also overtake. Therefore, it is allowed here to use the left lane. In all other cases, you have to drive on the right.
options: As long as is necessary to overtake other vehicles
As long as you are driving behind a vehicle which is overtaking in the left-hand lane
All the time, provided no other vehicle wants to overtake you

text: What applies on clearways for motor vehicles only?
explanation: You may only enter at intersections or T-junctions on motorways. Turning on motorways is prohibited. The regulations regarding speed differ from those that apply on the freeway. On highways you must not drive faster than the range of the low beam allows.
options: No U-turns
Join the clearway only at crossroads and junctions
In darkness, you may drive faster than the range of visibility allowed by dipped headlights

text: What top speed must be entered in the vehicle documents to allow the vehicle's use on autobahns?
explanation: A highway or freeway was built for high-speed traffic. That's why only vehicles that can reach a speed of more than 60 km/h are allowed to drive here. If you’re not entirely sure if own vehicle can drive that fast, it is noted in the car documents.

text: A traffic jam has formed on a three-lane autobahn. Where must the channel for emergency vehicles be formed?
explanation: When traffic stops on freeways or on roads outside of built-up areas with at least two lanes in one direction, vehicles must form a free lane for the passage of police and support vehicles. If a road has three lanes into one direction, then the middle is considered to be between the left and the middle lane.
options: Between the left-hand and the middle lanes
Between the middle and right-hand lanes
On the hard shoulder

text: You are driving in a merging lane. What should you do?
explanation: On an acceleration lane it is allowed to drive faster on the right than on the continuous lane. In order to merge, you as a car driver must accelerate adequately and observe the right of way and the safety distance.
options: Drive past to the right of slower-moving vehicles driving on the through-lane and merge in before them
Accelerate appropriately, do not pull up if possible, merge while observing the right of way
Always drive to the end of the merging lane, pull up there and then enter lane

text: What must you do now?
explanation: You approach the end of a traffic jam on the freeway. Turn on the hazard light. Form an alley in the middle of the lane for the passage of police and helping vehicles: on roads with three lanes for one direction, form an alley between the left and middle lane. Therefore, you have to drive far to the right. This rule applies outside built-up areas and on freeways.
options: - as far to the right as possible
- as far to the left as possible
- in the centre

text: What should you do?
explanation: They want to leave the freeway. You can see that traffic is stalling in your intended exit. Since you are not allowed to drive on the hard shoulder and wait on the lane, you behave correctly if you continue driving and use the next exit in order to exit the freeway.
options: I continue driving
I get in line on the hard shoulder
I stop on my lane and wait for a gap

text: What must you do when a traffic jam forms on this road?
explanation: Any car driver must cooperate in forming an alley in the middle of the road for the passage of police and support vehicles in case of congestion on freeways and on out-of-town roads with more than one lane. Do not drive on the side strip, this is prohibited.
options: - drive as far to the left as possible
- drive as far to the right as possible
- continuing driving in the centre

text: What is the right course of action now?
explanation: You meet a wrong-way driver on the freeway exit. By driving as far to the right as possible, you can best counteract a collision with the wrong-way driver. Now other road users must be warned of this acute danger. For this reason, you must inform the police.
options: I warn the driver by sounding my horn and flashing my lights
I drive over to the right-side as far as possible
I notify the police

text: What should you do now?
explanation: They have already passed the truck on the acceleration lane on the right-hand side of the freeway. If you continue to accelerate, you can drive onto the main lane before the end of the lane. You should do that.
options: I accelerate and merge in front of the [truck]
I slow down and merge between the [red car] and the [truck]
I slow down and merge after the [yellow vehicle]

text: You want to exit the motorway. What is the right course of action in this situation?
explanation: You flash and leave the freeway at the exit. The route to the turn of the exit is used to decelerate. Drive quickly off the highway, then reduce your pace. Drive into the corner at a moderately reduced speed.
options: I move into the left-hand lane
I watch out for oncoming vehicles
I continue by driving on the hard shoulder

text: What must you do if you find yourself in a traffic jam on motorways and on highways with two lanes travelling in the same direction?
explanation: If vehicles stand or drive at walking speed on freeways or on roads outside of built-up areas with at least two lanes for one direction, the following applies: You, as a car driver, must participate in forming a free lane between the leftmost and rightmost lane for the passage of police and support vehicles.
options: - drive as far to the right as possible in the right-hand lane
- drive as far to the left as possible in the left-hand lane
- drive as far to the left as possible in the right-hand lane

text: You are approaching a traffic jam on the motorway. What is the right course of action?
explanation: Warn following traffic by switching on the hazard warning lights and close up carefully.
options: I pull carefully up behind the last car in the traffic jam
I drive carefully through the emergency corridor
I continue driving carefully along the hard shoulder

text: What is the right course of action now?
explanation:
You must stay in the middle lane because there are vehicles in the left and right lanes that you would obstruct.
In the right lane, a motorbike is coming onto the motorway from the slip road. In the left lane is the car that just overtook you.
options: I stay in the middle lane
I move into the left-hand lane
I move into the right-hand lane

text: You want to leave the motorway at the next exit. What is the correct course of action in this situation?
explanation:
When leaving the motorway, you should set the indicator at least 300 m before the exit.
Always keep a close eye on the traffic behind you when driving on the motorway. Especially when exiting the motorway, make sure that nobody tries to overtake you on the right.
options: I observe the traffic behind me
I turn on my right-side indicators now
I begin now to smoothly brake down to 60 km/h

text: What should you do now?
explanation: Reduce your speed and allow the blue car to join the motorway while keeping a safe distance.
options: I reduce my speed
I accelerate
I move into the middle lane

text: What can you expect now?
explanation:
You should expect the truck in front of you to slow down because the other truck in the right lane is already slowing down and has its hazard lights on. You also have to expect that the truck will stay in the middle lane because it doesn't have enough space to get into the right lane. 
If a dangerous situation is identified on the motorway, the hazard warning lights may be switched on in order to warn all following vehicles in good time. Dangerous situations usually include accidents, traffic jams or slow traffic.
options: - brake
- stay in the middle lane
- accelerate

text: Your vehicle has broken down on the autobahn. What must you remember when having it towed away?
explanation: When towing on the freeway, the towing vehicle and the towed vehicle must have their hazard lights switched on. It's only allowed to tow on the freeway until the next exit. Then, the freeway must be left.
options: You must leave the autobahn at the next exit
During towing, both vehicles must have their hazard warning lights switched on
You may continue along the autobahn to the exit nearest a suitable garage

text: What applies on autobahns?
explanation: On the freeway you are only allowed to drive forward and only in one given direction. Reversing, turning and stopping is strictly prohibited on the roadway as well as on the side strip.
options: No stopping on the roadway and hard shoulder
No reversing
In darkness, under no circumstances drive faster than the range of visibility allowed by dipped headlights

text: You are driving on the motorway and have missed the exit. What is the right course of action?
explanation: Continue until the next exit and leave the freeway there. Now you can drive back to the missed exit on the other side of the freeway. You must not stop or drive backwards.
options: I continue driving and leave the motorway at one of the next exits
I reverse back on the hard shoulder, because the exit is less than 100 m behind me
I stop on the hard shoulder to plan my subsequent route

text: How can lane changing assist help you in this situation without steering override?
explanation: Lane Change Assist recognises the vehicle in the middle lane as a hazard and warns you not to change to that lane. To change lanes on your own would require steering intervention. Lane Change Assist does not interfere with your speed.
options: - warns of a possible collision with a vehicle in the middle lane
- performs a lane change independently
- brakes the speed of my vehicle

text: What is prohibited when using motorways?
explanation:
According to the StVO § 18 motorways and motor drivers:
(7) Turning and reversing are prohibited.
(8) hold, also on the side stripes, is forbidden.
options: Stopping on the hard shoulder
Reversing
Performing U-turns

text: What vehicles are subject to the toll on motorways and certain federal highways?
explanation: is correct: motor vehicles with at least 7.5 t permissible total mass, which are intended solely for the carriage of goods. Combinations of vehicles with at least 7.5 t permissible total mass.
options: Motor vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating of at least 7.5 t, intended exclusively for the carriage of goods by road
Combination vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating of at least 7.5 t, intended exclusively for the carriage of goods by road
Buses with a gross vehicle weight rating of at least 7.5 t

text: Who can be held responsible if the toll charge is not paid?
explanation: Not only the driver but also the holder are responsible. The shipper is not responsible.
options: The driver
The holder
The shipping agent

text: The gross vehicle weight rating of your towing vehicle amounts to 6.5 t; the gross vehicle weight rating of your trailer is 5.5 t. Is this combination vehicle liable to the toll if used on a motorway?
explanation: If your tractor t a maximum authorized mass of 6.5 and your trailer has 5.5 t, you may distribute the highway only sail if you entrichtest the toll for your vehicle combination is intended exclusively for freight. These are Toll Roads.
options: Yes, if the combination vehicle is intended exclusively for the carriage of goods by road
Always, because the combination vehicle exceeds the gross combination weight rating of 7.5 t
No, because the towing vehicle does not exceed the gross vehicle weight rating of 7.5 t

text: The gross vehicle weight rating of your truck amounts to 5.5 t; the gross vehicle weight rating of your trailer is 2.0 t. Is this combination vehicle liable to the toll if used for road haulage on a motorway?
explanation: Since your total mass of a total of 7.5 is your truck (freight) t, including trailer (vehicle combination) is payable on the highway a toll.
options: Yes
No

text: A user charge must be paid on motorways for motor vehicles or combination vehicles intended or used exclusively for the carriage of goods by road. From what gross vehicle weight rating does this apply?
explanation: The toll is t from a maximum mass of 7.5 to be paid.

text: Your truck has a gross vehicle weight rating of 6.5 t, and you would like to use it on the motorway for road haulage. What is true regarding the toll terminal registration?
explanation: Your trucks with a gross vehicle weight of 6.5 t for freight has no log-on to make, since the total mass is less than 7.5 t.
options: - do not have to register
- have to enter the number of axles
- have to enter the pollutant class (emissions class)

text: Your truck is equipped with an on-board unit (OBU). What information must be reviewed, and adapted as necessary, prior to travelling on a toll route?
explanation: Before you befährst a Toll route your OBU (toll collection device), you should enter the number of axles and adapt if necessary.
options: The number of axles
The emissions class
The gross vehicle weight rating

text: You want to drive a toll-chargeable motor vehicle on the motorway. How can the requisite toll entry be performed?
explanation: 3 answers are right here. With a toll station terminal in the www and also by means of on-board unit, short (OBU) so manually and digitally.
options: - via the internet
- at a toll terminal
- using the on-board unit (OBU)

text: Why should you have the traffic information switched on, when driving on the motorway?
explanation: Drivers are not required to listen to traffic news, but traffic news are indispensable for a smooth journey. Traffic news inform about traffic jams, traffic accidents and construction sites. Warnings about wrong-way drivers have already prevented a lot of serious accidents.
options: - gives warnings about motorists heading in the wrong direction
- provides reports about traffic jams
- is a prescribed requirement for travelling on the motorway

text: Who is responsible for enforcing the road toll?
explanation: The toll-control is carried out by the operator of the automatic control bridges and by the Federal Office for freight transport. Taxes have nothing to do with toll.
options: The operator of the automatic control bridges
The Federal Office for Goods Transport
The Federal Central Tax Office

text: Your truck is equipped with a toll collection device (OBU). What information must be checked and, if necessary, adjusted before driving along a toll section?
explanation: The toll rates are based on the weight classes, so you must account are rolling the perm. Total weight and adjust if necessary.
options: - gross vehicle weight rating
- emissions class
- number of axles

text: In which case are motor vehicles or combination vehicles used in road haulage, subject to a toll charge?
What applies to the payment of tolls in commercial road haulage?
explanation: Both the driver and the owner of a vehicle are responsible for paying the toll properly. If no toll fee is paid, both people are considered to be debtors of the toll and can therefore be held accountable accordingly.
options: The driver can be held responsible for non-payment of the toll
The vehicle owner can be held responsible for non-payment of the toll
No toll has to be paid for empty runs

text: A toll must be paid for motor vehicles or vehicle combinations used for commercial freight transport on motorways. From what technically permissible maximum laden mass does this apply?
explanation: Motor vehicles or vehicle combinations with a technically permissible total mass of more than 3.5 tonnes must pay a toll.

text: Your truck is equipped with a toll collection device (OBU). What information must be checked and, if necessary, adjusted before driving along a toll section?
explanation: The toll rates are based on the weight classes, so you must account are rolling the perm. Total weight and adjust if necessary. For vehicles and vehicle combinations with a gross vehicle weight of over 18 tons in the declaration of weight class one step further must be done. The driver must here also specify the number of axles.
options: - number of axles
- gross vehicle weight rating
- emissions class

text: What effects does a pillion passenger have on driving a motorcycle?
explanation: Having a passenger sitting behind you will increase your weight which makes starting to drive and gaining speed more difficult, it will also increase your breaking distance to stop. Given that it creates more side surface, it increases your sensitivity to side winds
options: Driving off is more difficult because a motorcycle only becomes stable at higher speeds
The motorcycle becomes more susceptible to side wind
The motorcycle's braking behaviour can change

text: You want to take a passenger on your motorcycle. What should you pay attention to before you drive off?
explanation: When taking an inexperienced passenger with you, make sure that he wears a helmet, agrees on how to behave during the ride and gradually get used to the new environment
options: Your passenger has to wear a prescribed helmet
Agree on the conduct during the journey
Carefully and cautiously familiarize inexperienced passengers with riding on a motorbike

text: What must you remember if you want to take a pillion passenger?
explanation: When taking another passenger ensure that he wears a helmet and that the motorcycle is licensed to have him on board
options: The motorcycle must be licensed to carry 2 persons
There must be a safety helmet for the pillion passenger
No safety helmet is required for the pillion passenger when driving in built-up areas

text: What must you point out to your pillion passenger before setting off?
explanation: Make sure that your passenger wears a helmet, keeps his feet on the footrests (otherwise it increases the risk of accident and injury). Your passenger does not have to lean to the outside of the bend to compensate when turning
options: - must put his feet on the footrests
- must wear a safety helmet
- must always lean to the outside on bends

text: You want to take a five-year old child on your motorized bicycle. Which seats are permissible for this?
explanation: In order to carry a child as a passenger, you need a special child seat with footrests
options: A special child's seat with footrests
Luggage rack with a cushion
Tank with attached padding

text: Why is it dangerous if passengers sitting in the rear do not wear their seatbelts?
explanation: In the event of a collision, people on the rear seats can be thrown forward or sideways. If they are thrown forward, the front backrests do not provide adequate protection. As a result, the driver and co-driver are at risk. Even at low speeds, injuries can occur.
options: - could result in injuries even at low speeds
- could result in injuries to persons in the front seats
- could propel these persons from the vehicle

text: To what should you pay attention if you want to take a passenger on the motorbike?
explanation: When increasing the load on your motorcycle, make sure to increase the tire pressure, adjust the chassis/suspension. Your passenger should also wear a helmet and protective gear
options: The passenger should also be wearing protective motorcycling clothing
The chassis should be adjusted accordingly
The tyre inflation pressure should be adjusted

text: What must you be aware of if you want to take a pillion rider with you?
explanation: The passenger(s) must be physically and mentally able to ride, and the motorbike must be adequately equipped.
options: The motorbike must be licensed to carry 2 people
The pillion rider must be capable of riding with you
A child pillion rider over 7 years of age, must be able to use the existing footrests and hand grips

text: How does riding with a pillion rider affect the handling of a motorbike?
explanation: The pillion rider's own movement destabilises the motorbike. Riding with a passenger should be practised.
options: It is more difficult to keep the motorbike stable
Its behaviour changes when braking
There is a reduction in its sensitivity to side winds

text: You want to transport a pillion passenger and luggage on your motorbike. What must you be aware of?
explanation: You must not exceed the permissible total weight for the motorbike. This is made up of the unladen weight and the maximum permitted load. To prevent luggage from flying around, it must be securely fastened. The lighting equipment must be visible at all times and must not be obscured by the loaded luggage.
options: The maximum authorised mass may not be exceeded
Pieces of luggage must be securely fastened
Lighting systems may not be obscured

text: You want to transport a pillion passenger. What must you ensure before commencing your journey?
explanation: In principle, when a pillion passenger is carried, the passenger seat, footrests and a holding device must be available on the motorbike. Both rider and pillion passenger must wear a suitable safety helmet while riding. To ensure a safe ride, you must instruct the pillion passenger on the correct behaviour before the ride.
options: - that my pillion passenger is wearing a suitable helmet
- I have instructed my pillion passenger on how to behave while we are driving on the road
- the bike's technical adjustment settings for carrying a pillion passenger are used

text: What should you anticipate if you want to take a pillion passenger with you?
explanation:
Be aware that the additional weight of the passenger will make your motorbike more slow and shift the centre of gravity backwards. You will therefore no longer be able to corner quite as dynamically as without a passenger.
You should also be aware that the additional weight can make your overtaking distance noticeably longer.
options: The vehicle's handling will be different when cornering
The overtaking distance may be longer
The braking distance will be reduced

text: What conditions must you fulfil to be allowed to carry a five-year-old child on your moped?
explanation:
It is required by law that you must be at least 16 years old if you want to take a child under 7 years old with you on the moped. 
Since the child is under 7 years old, you must be able to attach a special child seat to the moped. The child's height and body control are not yet sufficient to hold on to the moped safely and independently. You also need to make sure that the child's feet cannot get caught in the wheels. There are special protective devices for this, such as: B. Footrests.
options: - be at least 16 years old
- fit the moped with a special child seat
- make sure that the child’s feet cannot get caught in the wheels

text: You are driving a truck with a trailer and wish to give someone a lift as a favour. Where are you allowed to carry such a passenger?
explanation: For safety reasons, you may only carry people inside the cab of a truck. Taking somebody with you on the load platform is not permitted. Only certain persons may exceptionally ride on the loading platform, if, for example, they are responsible for escorting the load.
options: In the driver's cab
On the floor of the truck
On the floor of the trailer

text: What must you ensure before setting off on a journey in your car?
explanation: The car driver is responsible for the safety of the passengers and the cargo. He/she must take all necessary measures to prevent or minimize damage. The loading must be carried out in accordance with regulations and must be carefully secured.
options: That the passengers can put on the existing safety belts
That you have an adequate view to the rear
That no objects (e.g. first-aid kit, road atlas, camera) are lying loose on the rear parcel shelf

text: How are you allowed to transport a small child in your car?
explanation: Toddlers must be specially secured. This is only possible with an age-appropriate restraining device. This is to be mounted on the back seat. Infants are at risk to be suffocated by the airbag in the event of an impact. A baby seat is not secure enough.
options: In an approved child restraint with test mark
On the lap of an adult
In a baby carrycot on one of the back seats

text: How are you allowed to transport a five-year-old child in your car?
explanation: If you want to bring a five-year-old child with you in your car, you must use a child seat that has been tested and adapted to the size of the child. This is mandatory for all children under 12 years.
options: In a suitable and approved child seat with test mark
In a back seat with standard three-point safety belt
On a back seat with waist belt fastened

text: How are you allowed to transport an eleven-year-old child of 140 cm (4'11") in your car?
explanation: An eleven-year-old child that is 140 cm tall needs a children's seat or a booster seat. The child is to be fastened with the belt. Children under the age of twelve or under 150 cm tall must be carried. If the strap rests on the neck, there is a risk of strangulation.
options: On an approved raised seat with test mark and with three-point safety belt fastened
With three-point safety belt fastened
On a back seat with waist belt fastened

text: What should be borne in mind when using an approved child seat with test mark?
explanation: Child seats are made for different age groups. They are safety-tested for the specified weight and size groups. You should pay attention to this when using it. The child seat may only be used on those car seats for which it is suitable and approved.
options: The child seat must be appropriate for the height and weight of the child
The child seat must be capable of attachment to the seat of the vehicle for which it is intended
Nothing apart from the test mark

text: Why is it dangerous not to wear safety belts?
explanation: In an accident, a person may be easily thrown out of the vehicle by the impact energy, or injured in the vehicle by a collision. Already at 20 km/h the impact energy is so high that injuries can occur.
options: Because you cannot adequately protect yourself in case of an impact at a speed of about 20 km/h
Because in case of an accident you can be projected out of the vehicle
Because of the low speed there is no danger in urban traffic

text: At which impact speed must you reckon with serious or deadly injuries when no safety belt is worn?
explanation: Without a seat belt, serious injuries can occur in a collision just over 20 km/h. This also applies to rear-end collisions which are often wrongly considered harmless. That's why you should always fasten your seat belt, even on short distances.
options: From 30 km/h onward
From 50 km/h onward
From 80 km/h onward

text: A car is equipped with two front air bags. On which seats must safety belts be worn?
explanation: The front airbags protect the car driver and the co-driver in the front seat in the event of a strong impact, for example a rear-end collision. However, they are not sufficient for comprehensive protection. All passengers must fasten their seat belts each time they drive.
options: On all seats
Not on the front seats
On the front seats only

text: What does this warning sign mean?
explanation: The note warns against the wrong installation of the children's seat. If the children's seat is mounted so that the child sits in the opposite direction of travel, the child may be seriously injured in the event of a collision and the impact of the airbag. The children's seat must be installed in the direction of travel.
options: - you are not allowed to install a child seat opposite to the direction in which the vehicle is travelling
- you may only install a child seat facing the direction in which the vehicle is travelling
- you must install the child seat as illustrated

text: You wish to take several small children home after a children's birthday party. What must you observe when using your car?
explanation: If you want to bring several small children home with your car, you must ensure that your passengers are secured in all places with the legally required restraining devices.
options: The children must be secured with the prescribed child restraints
Child restraints need not be used within built-up areas
It is sufficient to secure the children with the existing safety belts

text: What must you observe if you wish to drive a vehicle with front passenger air bag?
explanation: The children's seat must be facing forward. If it is placed in the opposite direction, the children's seat must not be used as the airbag poses a risk to the child in the event of an accident.
options: You may not install a child restraint on the front passenger seat facing backwards
You may install a child restraint on the front passenger seat facing forwards
You may install a child restraint on the front passenger seat facing backwards

text: What is important to consider about headrests?
explanation: Head restraints must always be adjusted to suit the height of the occupants. Only then, can they best absorb the impact energy and protect the driver and other passengers in the event of a collision. However, the headrests do not serve as a substitute for safety belts.
options: Adjust them to head height according to the operating manual
They are optimally adjusted by the factory
For the rear seats they replace the safety belts

text: While you are driving, the airbag control light stays on constantly. What must you do?
explanation: If the airbag control lamp is lit up, it signals a defect in the airbag system. An error of this sensory and electronic system can usually only be fixed in a car workshop. This should be done as soon as possible. For this reason, you as a car driver do not have to immediately pull the vehicle out of circulation.
options: Go to a garage workshop
Take the vehicle off the road immediately
Nothing because it is an indication for the garage workshop

text: Are you allowed to transport persons on the loading platform of your truck?
explanation: It is forbidden to carry persons on the load platform or in the shipping space of motor vehicles. A derogation applies, provided that these people have to do necessary work there. The ban also does not apply to the transport of construction site personnel within construction sites.
options: Yes, if they must carry out necessary work
Yes, if they have to accompany the load
Yes, to secure the load

text: How can you prevent a child from opening a door while the vehicle is moving?
explanation: With the central locking, and child safety you can close all doors at the push of a button at the same time. This way you can prevent a child from opening the door while driving and thus being injured.
options: - the child safety locks on the rear doors
- the central locking system

text: You want to carry a child in your car. When must you use a child seat for this purpose?
explanation: You need a child seat if the child is younger than 12 years and smaller than 150 cm. If you do not have it with you, you risk a fine.
options: If the child is younger than 12 years old and is under 150 cm in height
If the child is older than 12 years old and is taller than 150 cm
If the child is older than 12 years old and is under 150 cm in height

text: You want to drive with a baby in the passenger seat. What do you have to be aware of when using an infant carrier?
explanation: The baby carrier must be placed against the direction of travel and the passenger airbag must be switched off to protect the baby. The muscles are not yet strong enough to absorb such a collision.
options: The infant carrier must be positioned reversed to the direction of travel
If installed, the passenger airbag must be deactivated
The baby must be strapped into the infant carrier

text: What should be noted when using a seatbelt?
explanation:
The seat belt is the most important protective device of a vehicle occupant in the event of an accident. Therefore, when creating the seat belt, care must be taken that it is not twisted or damaged.
After putting on the belt, you should pull the belt once again to ensure that the seat belt sits properly.
If you determine damage to the seat belt, it must be repaired immediately.
options: The seatbelt should not be twisted
Once you have put it on, the seatbelt should be pulled tight
A damaged seatbelt should be replaced

text: What inhibits the operation of a three-point seatbelt?
explanation: In order to ensure the maximum protective effect of the seat belt, it must be really cried out into the belt lock and run over the shoulder and hip. Performing the belt under both arms can lead to injuries. Furthermore, the function of the seat belt can be impaired by wearing a thick winter jacket, since there is a lot of air between body and seat belt.
options: Wearing a thick winter coat
Passing the belt under both arms
Not fully locking the belt into the harness buckle

text: What should you check before starting your journey?
explanation:
You should check some points before every start.
You should make sure that all mirrors are set correctly so that you can ensure sufficient traffic observation.
You should also make sure that all those traveling have created the seat belt, since the seat belt is the most important protective device in the event of an accident.
In the best case, you should keep the registration certificate Part II in a safe place and not carry it in the car. While you always have to carry the registration certificate part I (also called vehicle license) in the original in the car. The vehicle registration document documents the official approval for the participation of the vehicle in road traffic.
options: - every passenger has put on their seatbelt
- I can ensure that I can properly observe other road traffic
- I have the registration certificate Part II with me

text: What should be noted regarding the desired protective effect of airbags?
explanation:
The prerequisite for the protective effect of the airbag is that it can develop properly. While the airbag unfolds, it is important that no objects or obstacles hinder the development.
The desired protective effect of airbags is only guaranteed if the passengers are upright and sitting on the back with their backs.
options: Airbags can only achieve their full effect if the vehicle’s passengers are in the right seating position
The airbag deployment zone may not be encroached
Airbags can replace car seatbelts when driving in town

text: You want to transport a person in a vehicle, and that person must remain seated in a wheelchair during the drive. What must you be aware of?
explanation:
Some points should be considered for the safe transportation of a wheelchair. Special passenger and wheelchair retention systems are used for this. Furthermore, there should be a special wheelchair parking space, at which, for example, anchoring points on the vehicle are attached to ensure the wheelchair.

§ 21a StVO
(1) prescribed seat belts must be created while driving; This also applies to prescribed wheelchair retention systems and prescribed wheelchair user retention systems.
options: The motor vehicle must be equipped with a wheelchair space
The wheelchair must be secured using a wheelchair restraint system
The person must be secured using a wheelchair-user restraint system

text: You are driving a public transport bus. Where may you allow passengers to board and alight the bus?
explanation: You are only allowed to let passengers get on and off the bus at the specified stops to be able to eliminate any danger.
options: At designated bus stops
At red traffic lights
At taxi ranks

text: As the driver of a public transport bus, what should you do when approaching a bus stop?
explanation: When nearing a bus stop, it is important to switch on the blinkers and reduce speed smoothly. Do not open the doors until the bus has come to a stop.
options: I steadily reduce my speed
I open the doors only after the bus has come to a stop
I turn on my indicator in plenty of time

text: You are driving a bus for the occasional carriage of passengers, and you are supposed to convey passengers and luggage. What must you observe?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Including the driver, it is only permitted to convey the maximum number of individuals as seats indicated in the registration certificate Part I
The loading of luggage may not result in the gross axle weight rating and the gross vehicle weight rating becoming exceeded
With duly stowed luggage, the gross vehicle weight rating may be exceeded by 10 %

text: How are you allowed to transport persons on trailers used for agricultural purposes?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Sitting, if they are sitting on adequate seats
Standing up, if this is required to accompany the load
Standing up on empty trailers

text: What safety adjustments may be necessary when loading a motorcycle?
explanation: When increasing the load on your motorcycle, make sure to increase the tire pressure and adjust the chassis/suspension
options: Increase the tyre pressure
Adjust the damping/suspension
Increase the tank volume

text: What should you especially consider when travelling with luggage?
explanation: Adding luggage to your motorcycle will impact its behavior on the road. The additional weight will change the center of gravity of the motorcycle. It will increase the impact of side wind on the motorcycle. Make sure you do not exceed the maximum speed recommended by your manufacturer for driving with luggage.
options: The recommended top speed given in the vehicle manufacturer's operating manual
The affect of the changed centre of gravity on road handling
The increased susceptibility to side wind

text: Where should you stow heavy luggage?
explanation: You should place heavy luggage as close as possible to the center of gravity of your motorcycle to least impact its behavior. Make sure to place it either in the tank-top bag or equally distributed and deep in the panniers.
options: In the tank-top bag
Stow equally on the left and right, and as deep as possible in the panniers
In the handlebar bag

text: How does incorrect loading affect driving stability?
explanation: Incorrectly loading your motorcycle will make your motorcycle less stable. It will make it less stable when braking and could make it vibrate or swing
options: To heavy tail-loading causes the motorcycle to shimmy and swing
Unequally distributed loading can have a negative effect on driving stability when braking
Has no effect

text: What must you be aware of when loading a truck with trailer (truck-trailer)?
explanation: The total length of the train (lorry with trailer) and its load must not 20.75 m passing and the charge is to be distributed so that the operational reliability of the train is not affected and you thus endangering any other participants of road traffic.
options: The total length of the truck-trailer including load may not exceed 20.75 m
The load must be distributed in such a way so as not to interfere with the operational safety of the truck-trailer
Heavy goods should be positioned as high up as possible

text: What is the maximum permissible length of a truck with trailer, including load?
explanation: The charge of the truck, including trailer must be 20.75 meters long at most.

text: You are carrying an additionally attached piece of luggage on your motorbike. What should you take into account?
explanation:
Because of the luggage, your motorbike has a larger surface area to attack, so it is more susceptible to crosswinds. The extra weight also shifts the centre of gravity of your motorbike. You should therefore make sure that the luggage is evenly distributed and adjust your riding behaviour accordingly.
There may be recommendations from the vehicle manufacturer as to how you should adjust your speed to the load. You should follow these. You will find them in the owner's manual.
options: Any possible maximum speed recommendations made by the vehicle manufacturer
Any change in the centre of gravity of the motorbike
Any change in the motorbike’s susceptibility to side winds

text: How does an improperly stowed load affect the driving stability of a motorbike?
explanation:
Too heavy a load at the rear of the motorbike puts too little weight on the front tyres and steering. This makes it easier for the bike to wobble and oscillate. Differently loaded sides have a negative effect on stability and handling. The motorbike will lean more towards the heavier side when braking or cornering.
Light luggage in the tank bag does not affect the riding stability of the motorbike.
options: A heavy load placed on the rear causes the motorbike to wobble and sway at high speeds
A load placed on one side only negatively affects the handling
Light-weight luggage in the tank bag makes skidding more probable

text: What might be needed when a motorcycle is fully loaded?
explanation: If the motorbike is fully loaded, the load exerts more pressure on the tyres. You should therefore check the tyre inflation pressure. The weight of the load could push the chassis down further and must therefore be readjusted. If the load extends beyond the motorbike, you should also readjust the rear view mirrors.
options: An adjustment of the tyre inflation pressure
An adjustment of the chassis
An adjustment of the rear-view mirrors

text: Carrying a rucksack while cycling can affect the handling of your two-wheeler. What can the consequences be?
explanation: By carrying a backpack, you offer a larger surface for crosswinds to attack. Carrying a backpack also shifts your center of gravity upwards. This means you can't steer as quickly.
options: A greater susceptibility to side wind
A displacement of the centre of gravity
An improvement in the manoeuvrability

text: What do white plates with a black "A" on a truck mean?
explanation: A truck with white plates marked with a black "A" transports litter. The white plates with a black "A" must be clearly visible both at the front and at the back of the truck.
options: - is transporting waste materials
- is transporting dangerous goods
- is driven by a beginner

text: What must you bear in mind if you want to carry luggage on the roof of your car?
explanation: Luggage on the roof changes the center of gravity of your vehicle upwards. This has a significant influence on the driving characteristics of the car. The driving characteristics are worse, especially in curves. The vehicle is wind-prone. It must be ensured that the permissible roof load and total mass are not exceeded.
options: The roadhandling characteristics are adversely affected
The permissible total mass must not be exceeded
The maximum roof load stipulated by the car manufacturer (owner's manual) must not be exceeded

text: What must you reckon with when transporting luggage on the roof of your car?
explanation: The luggage on the roof changes the center of gravity of the vehicle - it is raised. This increases the danger of tipping over and the aerodynamic drag increases. As a result, your vehicle is more sensitive to crosswind and air pressure when a wheel or truck overtakes you. In curves the driving stability also deteriorates due to the higher center of gravity. Your vehicle will tilt more.
options: The vehicle inclines more on bends
The vehicle's susceptibility to side wind is greater
The vehicle's roadhandling is improved on account of the higher centre of gravity

text: What must you do when transporting bicycles on the roof of your car?
explanation: Bicycles on the roof require special attention: think of safety regulations and careful attachment. Check the fastenings regularly during driving breaks. Loads on the roof change the center of gravity of the vehicle, they lift it. The driving quality deteriorates especially in curves. Avoid high speeds.
options: Safely attach holding device and bicycles
Avoid driving at high speed
Regularly check the fixing devices

text: What must you check when transporting bicycles on a rear-mounted support system?
explanation: Check if the rear carry system is securely fastened. Likewise, the attachment of bicycles is to be checked. If illuminating devices or the license plate is obscured, technical equipment must be installed at the end of the vehicle system for adequate lighting and/or to attach the license plate number. Back-heavy loading changes the center of gravity of the vehicle. Check the distribution of the load.
options: Whether, according to the manufacturer's instructions, the system is adequate for the vehicle
Whether system and bicycles are fixed safely
Whether lighting equipment or number plate are covered

text: How must a load be marked in darkness or bad visibility when it extends laterally more than 40 cm beyond the side lights of the vehicle?
explanation: In the dark or in poor visibility conditions, a cargo that laterally protrudes more than 40 cm beyond the marker lights of the vehicle must be marked with additional lights. These are to be attached laterally no more than 40 cm from the edge and no more than 1.5 m above the roadway. For the front, a white lamp is required, for the back you need to install a red light. The hazard lights must not be switched on by you as a car driver while driving.
options: By a white light to the front
By a red light to the back
By switching on the hazard warning lights

text: What is the maximum height allowed above the roadway for a red light marking a load extending to the back?
explanation: The maximum height for attaching the lamp is 1.5 meters. This is to ensure that the marking is in the field of vision of other road users. If the red light is higher above the road, it could be overlooked.

text: Up to what height is a load not allowed to project over the front of the vehicle?
explanation: The red lamp, which marks the rear projecting cargo, may be installed at a maximum height of 2.50 m. If it were higher, other road users might oversee it. To prevent a hazard, a maximum height of 2.50 m is set.

text: Under what conditions is a load allowed to project over the front of a vehicle?
explanation: If the cargo is fastened above a height of 2.50 m, it may protrude up to 50 cm from the front of the vehicle. This regulation is intended to reduce the danger and risk of injury from rear-end collisions with cargo. In general, cargo should always be carefully secured so that it can neither slip nor fall.
options: If the load does not project over more than 50 cm and is above a height of 2.50 m
If the load is marked with a red light

text: During a break you find out that one of the lashing straps has torn. What do you do?
explanation: As a car driver, you must ensure that your cargo is properly secured throughout the journey. With a defective strap, you may only continue your journey if proper securing of the cargo is ensured by other securing devices. If this is not the case, you must not continue your journey.
options: Continue your trip after the lashing strap has been replaced
Continue your trip when the load is secured by other sufficient securing means
Continue your trip because a slipping load will be caught by the side panels

text: Do the requirements for properly securing of loads apply to all small transporters?
explanation: Without exception, the requirements for proper securing of the load apply to all vans. Back-heavy loading shifts the center of gravity of the vehicle to the back. As a result, the front wheel is no longer sufficiently burdened and the grip deteriorates. This promotes dangerous pendular movements.
options: They apply to all small transporters
They only apply to small transporters with open loading space
They only apply to small transporters without separation wall to the loading space

text: You want to drive a truck with a gross vehicle weight rating of 5.0 t and bearing an orange warning sign. What conditions must you fulfil?
explanation: The requirement that you should fulfill: You need additional to the required driving license valid ADR certificate. This allows you to transport dangerous goods (orange warning sign).
options: - a valid ADR Certificate
- a valid driving licence for carrying passengers
- valid proof showing you have previously transported hazardous goods

text: What do you have to observe when getting a load ready for safe road transportation?
explanation: A distribution of the charge and the fixing of the selfsame and a backup of the device for securing the load you should be aware so that security is guaranteed. All three answers are correct.
options: The distribution of the load
The fastening of the load
The secure attachment of the load securing devices

text: What should be noted when loading vehicles?
explanation: Cargo may protrude above a height of 2.50 m forward up to 50 cm above the vehicle. If the load protrudes more than 1 m beyond the rear reflectors of the vehicle, the end must be visually marked. Cargo needs to be secured carefully. Back-heavy loading causes dangerous pendular movements when driving faster. For motorcycles, ensure that the load is evenly distributed on the sides.
options: Loads that project beyond the retro-reflectors by more than 1 m, must be labelled
Loads more than 2.50 m high may not project forwards by more than 50 cm
It is not necessary to secure heavy loads

text: What must you ensure when transporting long steel pipes?
explanation: The steel pipes must be secured with appropriate means and are indicated at rear overhang of more than 1 m. If you notice this, you're on the safe side.
options: - be secured by suitable means
- be labelled if the rear overhang exceeds 1 m
- transported using vehicles with no front wall

text: How might an uneven load distribution affect the vehicle and the handling?
explanation: An uneven load distribution of the load can cause the permissible axle loads can be exceeded and affect the steering. The fuel consumption is not critical.
options: The gross axle weight rating could be exceeded
The steering characteristics will be affected
The fuel consumption will be reduced

text: When is a centrifugal force exerted on the load of a truck?
explanation: The centrifugal force affects your truck when cornering. go straight brakes or have no circular motion and are therefore not decisive.
options: When cornering
When braking
When driving straight ahead

text: What can an unsecured load cause when cornering?
explanation: Unsecured load during cornering can result in damage to the vehicle body, facilitate overturning of the vehicle and cause a deterioration of the drivability.
options: - result in damage to the vehicle body
- make it more likely that the vehicle could overturn
- impair the handling

text: What must you be aware of, if you want to transport the load?
explanation: When loading your vehicle, you as a car driver must make sure that the cargo is securely fastened.
