Badly recognizable objects as well as piles, bars or plates must not protrude laterally from the vehicle interior. The cargo must be stored in a way so that it does not cause any avoidable noise.
options: - must be secured
- may not cause avoidable noise
- may have individual bars projecting out to the side

text: You want to transport your holiday luggage on the roof of your fully occupied car. What must you observe?
explanation: Observe the permissible roof load specified by the vehicle manufacturer. This can be found in the operating instructions. In the certificate of registration part 1 the roof load is not noted. The permissible maximum mass of the vehicle must not be exceeded. Unevenly distributed load deteriorates driving stability during braking and in turns.
options: The vehicle manufacturer's roof load specifications in the operating manual
The gross vehicle weight rating of my car
The roof load specifications contained in the registration certificate Part I

text: You want to transport a load. What must you be aware of when doing so?
explanation: When transporting cargo, you must make sure that you are not hindered by it while driving, that the road safety of the vehicle is not impaired and that the cargo cannot slip or fall over while driving.
options: The load must not impede me while driving
The vehicle's road safety may not be negatively affected
The load may not shift or fall over during the journey

text: What load-securing equipment is to be used in the car?
explanation: Load securing means for use in cars are tension belts and safety nets. Wheel chocks are not included.
options: Lashing straps
Safety nets
Chocks

text: You want to transport a load on the roof of your car. How will this influence the handling of your car?
explanation: Your driving behaviour with a load on the roof will affect the braking distance (it will increase) and the acceleration capacity (e.g. when overtaking) will decrease.
options: The braking distance will be extended
The acceleration power will be reduced
The susceptibility to cross-winds will be reduced

text: What can be used to secure loads carried in a car?
explanation: The anti-slip mat prevents the load from sliding. The tensioning straps are for lashing down the load. The luggage net prevents cargo from flying around.
options: The luggage net
The tensioning belt
The anti-slip mat

text: What should you remember when loading luggage into a car luggage compartment?
explanation: In the event of an accident or breakdown, the warning triangle should always be at hand so that the triangle can be set up as quickly as possible. The load should be secured to prevent it from sliding around when accelerating, braking or cornering hard. Heavy luggage should be stowed at the bottom so that it cannot fall down.
options: - stow the warning triangle in an easily accessible place
- place heavy luggage at the bottom
- secure the luggage against slipping

text: How far may a labelled load protrude beyond the rear of your vehicle if your journey is more than 100 km?
explanation: For distances up to 100 Kilometers, the load is allowed to overhang up to 3 meters. For distances over 100 Kilometers, the load is allowed to overhang up to 1.50 meters to the rear.

text: What should you anticipate when you transport a load on the roof of your car?
explanation: The loading of the roof consumes significantly more fuel. The reason is that not the weight, but especially the headwind, affects consumption the most. Due to the additional loading of the roof, the side wind attacks an even larger area. This increases the side wind sensitivity. In addition, the focus of the vehicle shifts upwards. As a result, the vehicle tends to be aside in curves.
options: - tilt more to the side when cornering
- respond more sensitively to sidewinds
- have increased fuel consumption

text: You are transporting furniture in a van. While taking a break you notice that a lashing strap is damaged. Under what condition may you continue driving?
explanation:
As a driver, you are obliged to ensure proper load securing. You can only continue the transport of the furniture if you have exchanged the damaged lashing strap for an undamaged lashing strap or another suitable charge backup.

According to the StVO, the following applies: "§ 22 (1) The charge, including devices for load securing and loading devices, must be stowed and secure so that even when braking or sudden evasive movement, they cannot slip, fall over, fall, fall or to generate avoidable noise . (…)
options: - have replaced the lashing strap
- use other suitable load-securing equipment
- continue driving at a maximum of 50 km/h

text: What should you note regarding the trailer coupling, when transporting pedelecs on a rear-mounted carrier system?
explanation:
Before buying a bike rack for your pedelec for the trailer coupling, a few questions should be clarified. For example, is the support load of my trailer coupling sufficient at all and is the selected rear -bearing system designed for so much weight?
If both questions can be answered with yes and you have chosen a corresponding rear -bearing system, you have to adapt to the tire pressure about the additional loading.
options: - the rear-mounted carrier system must be suitably designed
- the trailer coupling must have a suitable vertical load capacity
- the car’s tyre inflation pressure must be adjusted appropriately

text: Which warning plate is correctly mounted?
explanation: As we need an A for (attention) the right warning sign is in place.
options: The right one
The left one

text: How can you determine that a truck is overloaded?
explanation: To determine an overload, you can weigh again your loaded vehicle or by built-axle load measuring devices.
options: By weighing the loaded vehicle
From built-in axle weight measuring devices
By doing a brake test with the loaded vehicle

text: A truck for exchangeable load carriers (interchangeable containers) has a permissable total mass of 6,000 kg. The interchangeable container has an empty mass of 1,500 kg. Which mass are you allowed to stow in this interchangeable container?
explanation: Empty weight (1500 kg) plus loading (4,500 kg) = payload (6000 kg) 4,500 kg is correct. In other words, payload (6000 kg) minus the empty weight (1500 kg) of the interchangeable container gives the load (4500 kg)

text: What do you understand by form-fit secured load?
explanation: Under a form-locking securing loads (zero) means the application of charge to loading limitations and secured spacers and the direct support cargo against frontal and side walls. The package has nothing to do.
options: Positioning the load directly against front and side walls
The load touches the load area limits and secured spacer blocks
Packaging that is adapted to the shape of the loaded goods

text: What do you understand by form-fit securing of the load?
explanation: The positive load securing means that free spaces are closed between the cargo items by means of suitable filler, and the load is located directly on the end and side wall.
options: The load is positioned directly at the front and side wall
Free space between parts of the load must be filled with appropriate filling
The free-standing load is lashed down to the loading area by appropriate lashing means

text: Who is responsible for the load being sufficiently secured?
explanation: All the transport stakeholders are responsible for adequate cargo securing.
options: All parties involved in the transport process
Only the driver
Only the loader

text: Who is responsible for operating vehicles in regard to its load?
explanation: both the driver and the holder will be responsible for the operation of the vehicles.
options: The driver
The owner
The registration authority

text: What do you have to consider when tipping bulk goods?
explanation: When dumping of materials, please make sure that the vehicle is on sufficiently solid ground, and protective must be released so that the dumping body can be fully tilted.
options: The vehicle must stand on sufficiently firm ground
The relevant safety devices must be unlocked to allow the tipping bridge to be completely tilted
The side walls should only be opened when the tipping bridge is in its tilted end position

text: Why is it necessary to observe the load distribution plan?
explanation: In order to avoid exceeding the axle load, it is necessary to adhere to the load distribution plan. So you can also ensure the steering ability.
options: To prevent exceeding the axle loads
To ensure steering capacity is maintained
To make loading and unloading easier

text: What is the purpose of a load distribution plan?
explanation: The load distribution plan shows how the vehicle must be loaded. If the distribution is uneven, the braking behaviour changes greatly.
options: To help with the road-worthy loading of the vehicle
To avoid falling below the axle load limit of the vehicle
To determine the unloading sequence for the vehicle

text: What could happen if your vehicle is not loaded according to the load distribution plan?
explanation: The load distribution plan shows how the vehicle must be loaded. If the load is unevenly distributed, the braking behaviour will change considerably. Damage to tyres occurs and steering ability is also impaired.
options: The tyres may become damaged
The steering ability may be affected
Its braking performance may be adversely affected

text: What specific information can you find in a load distribution plan?
explanation: The load distribution plan gives information on the load centre of gravity with the maximum permissible load.
options: Information about the centre of gravity of the load at the maximum allowable load limit
Information about securing the load on the load platform
Information about the maximum height of the load on the load platform

text: Who is responsible for securing the load on the vehicle?
options: The driver
The shipper
The receiver

text: What can help with friction-locked load securing?
explanation:
In force-locking load securing, the transported goods are pressed onto the loading surface by means of lashing. This type of lashing is also known as tie-down lashing.
The load usually stands freely on the loading surface and is only secured by the increased force applied. In most cases, the frictional force between the loading surface and the load is increased.
The load is secured with the aid of load securing equipment such as lashing straps, lashing chains, anti-slip mats or cover nets and with the aid of attachment points on the loading surface.
This prevents the load from slipping.
options: Lashing straps
Anti-slip mats
Lashing chains

text: What should be taken into consideration when selecting load-securing lashing equipment?
explanation:
Among other things, the face and shape of the load are decisive for the selection of suitable and necessary lashing equipment. 
Equally important are the requirements of the vehicle, such as the permissible payload and the attachment points.
options: The shape of the load
The weight of the load
The available lashing points

text: You want to secure your load by lashing it down. What should you bear in mind?
explanation: When lashing down, the load is pressed onto the loading area using lashing devices to increase the friction force and prevent slipping. It is important to check the tension of the lashing devices, as the necessary contact force and thus the required friction can only be achieved with sufficient tension. In addition, this method is only suitable for dimensionally stable loads; flexible goods can deform under the tension, which means that the pre-tensioning force is lost and load securing is no longer guaranteed.
options: - regularly check the tension of the lashing equipment
- only secure dimensionally stable loads by lashing them down
- choose the smallest possible lashing angle

text: What is better for reasons of driving safety?
explanation: Since you could load (truck) in a truck with a trailer on the front part of the weight, it is better for the sake of driving safety when the trailer is empty.
options: The truck is loaded and the trailer is empty
The trailer is loaded and the truck is empty

text: What must you remember when you wish to transport animals on a trailer?
explanation: You have to make sure that the maximum authorized mass of the trailer is not exceeded and subject to special rules for the transport of animals in an animal transportation.
options: The special regulations for the transport of animals
The total permissible mass of the trailer must not be exceeded
Animals may only be transported on trailers with air-brakes

text: When must attached working equipment be marked with red-white warning plates?
explanation: A red and white warning board is then to mount when it protrudes rearward more than 1 m on the rear lamps of the tractor if it has traffic hazardous parts and also when it laterally by more than 40 cm beyond the boundary or rear lamps of the tractor protrudes. All three are correct.
options: When it has parts presenting a danger to traffic
When extending laterally more than 40 cm beyond the side lights or rear lights of the tractor
When extending more than 1 m to the back beyond the rear lights of the tractor

text: What duties do you have when driving a loaded vehicle?
explanation: If you lead a loaded vehicle, you are responsible for ensuring that the safety of the vehicle is not affected by the charge and you have to adjust your speed to the load conditions.
options: I am responsible for ensuring that the load does not impair the road safety of the vehicle
I must adjust my speed to the nature of the load
With loads at risking of tipping, I have to arrange for someone to accompany the load on the loading area to ensure it is secure

text: What happens if you do not wear snug-fitting clothing?
explanation: Clothes that are not loose and not snug-fitting will be flapping at high speed which reduces your stability. They could also reduce your rear-view vision. They, however, will not have any impact on air resistance.
options: At high speed, flapping clothing affects road safety
Blown up clothing reduces your vision in the rear-view mirror
Blown up clothing reduces air resistance

text: What must you do before setting off on a journey?
explanation: All three are correct. Make sure that everything is fixed well on your motorcycle. Make sure that you wear adequate clothing, check your helmet visor. And finally, ensure the safety of the road and motorcycle.
options: Check road safety and operational safety of the motorcycle
Check helmet visor and snug-fitting clothing
Check if panniers and top case are fixed correctly

text: Why are motorcyclists required to wear an appropriate protective helmet?
explanation: A helmet is required to protect your head against injuries and potential death
options: To avoid head injuries as much as possible
So it is easier to listen to the radio
To reduce air resistance at higher speed

text: Which items are part of a motorcyclists safety equipment?
explanation: An appropriate jacket, trousers and boots are part of the safety equipment that can protect you in case of accidents and injuries. Gym shoes are not protective equipment
options: Appropriate jacket
Appropriate trousers
Gym shoes

text: Why should you wear appropriate boots when riding a motorcycle?
explanation: Boots do not reduce air resistance. Appropriate boots are a protective that will protect you from injury and undercooling
options: You could suffer considerable foot injuries even if a motorbike just topples over whilst standing
Undercooling due to weather factors can damage your health
Because air resistance is reduced

text: Which motorcycle clothing increases optical perceptibility?
explanation: To increase your visibility, wear bright and light colours. Dark colours are less visible, especially at night.
options: Clothing in bright colours
Clothing in light colours
Clothing in dark colours

text: Why should you regularly apply the brakes with force at standstill?
explanation: When standing still, use your brakes to ensure that the system works correctly (both the braking transmission, connection and the breaks themselves)
options: - whether the mechanical transmission and connection components are in functioning order
- whether a hydraulic braking system has no leaks
- the deceleration of the brakes is adequate

text: What are the effects of a badly scratched helmet visor?
explanation: A badly scratched helmet visor will diminish your vision and will make light more intensely seen with the risk of dazzling
options: The wearer is dazzled more intensely than usual
Own vision is impaired
In daylight, there are no negative effects

text: What is correct for checking the brake light?
explanation: Make sure that the brake light works for the hand brake and foot break separately.
options: Apply hand brake and foot brake one after the other
Apply hand brake and foot brake at the same time
Apply the hand brake only

text: Where are you allowed to store luggage on motorcycles?
explanation: You can store luggage in the tank-top bag, panniers (equally distributed on the right and left), luggage rack, handlebars.
options: In panniers or on the luggage rack
In the tank-top bag
Evenly distributed on the right and left of the handlebars

text: How must you protect yourself from serious head injuries?
explanation: An officially approved protective helmet is required to protect your head against injuries
options: - an officially approved protective helmet
- a steel helmet
- a tested protective work helmet

text: What applies to the installation and use of rear-view mirrors on motorcycles?
explanation: In order to be able to use your rearview mirror, you must ensure that they are well fixed, adjusted, and work (are not cracked, blind)
options: They must be fixed and adjusted properly
They must neither be cracked nor blind
A mirror on the right replaces the look over your shoulder

text: What is required when the motor liability insurance of your vehicle has expired?
explanation: It is required to have an insurance for your vehicle, without one you are not allowed to drive it
options: - may no longer be used in road traffic
- must be submitted to the technical test centre

text: What can prevent you from hearing warning signals?
explanation: Other sounds, such as a loud radio or a loud exhaust, can prevent car drivers from perceiving important warning signals. Also, the use of headphones usually limits the ability to hear. This often means that warning signals are ignored by drivers. Make sure that you can always hear warning signals.
options: Having the radio on too loud
Using headphones
The exhaust being too loud

text: You have sold your vehicle which is still registered. The buyer has paid. What must you do?
explanation: If you have sold your licensed vehicle and received the payment, proceed as follows: 1. You hand over all vehicle documents to the new vehicle owner in exchange for a confirmation of receipt. 2. You report the name and address of the vehicle buyer to the admission office. This way, you protect yourself from unjustified claims that could be caused by traffic violations on the part of the new owner. 3. The inspection plate remains on the vehicle.
options: Inform the registration centre immediately of the buyer's name and address
Hand over the vehicle registration certificate (Fahrzeugschein) and vehicle registration book (Fahrzeugbrief) or permit for use (Betriebserlaubnis) to the buyer against receipt
Remove the test stamp from the official registration plate

text: What is important with regard to the official registration plates?
explanation: For license numbers, it is important that they are placed in the required place. In addition, they must be easy to read and illuminated in the dark.
options: They must be securely attached at the appropriate places
They must always be easily legible
The rear registration plates must be lit up in darkness

text: What is required when your vehicle is no longer covered by motor liability insurance?
explanation: Without a valid liability insurance, a car is not ready to drive and therefore may not participate in public transport. The liability insurance serves to regulate damage that you may be able to inflict on other vehicles. Irrespective of the financial circumstances of the injuring party, compensation for the injured party is thus guaranteed. If there is no liability insurance, the holder must deregister the car at the admission office. Failure to comply with this rule will result in a penalty.
options: - may no longer be used in road traffic
- must be de-registered at the registration centre
- must be submitted to the registration centre

text: What are you allowed to change on the official registration plate?
explanation: A license number is an official document, which may not be altered in any way. Therefore, do not attach any foils or stickers to your license plate.
options: Nothing
Attach a protective foil for the lettering
Attach coloured stickers

text: As a cyclist, what must you check before commencing your journey?
explanation: Before starting your trip, make sure that your lights and tires are in good condition and work properly.
options: Condition of tyres
Lighting
First-aid material

text: What do we mean by the term "blind spot"?
explanation: In blind spots you can not see other road users. Areas around the vehicle that can not be seen even with the vehicle mirrors, count as such. The other two answers are wrong.
options: Areas around the vehicle not visible even with the vehicle's mirrors
Areas in inner cities not accessible to vehicles due to the restrictions on visibility
Areas of the roadway which cannot be driven over due to the wide turning circle of my vehicle

text: While you are driving a car you get a call on your mobile phone. What must you be aware of here, if you do not have a hands-free set?
explanation: You must keep the cellphone ringing. Taking or holding the phone is generally prohibited for motorists and can lead to high fines. If necessary, stop at the nearest convenient location. First turn off the engine. Only now you are allowed to take your phone into your hands.
options: The journey must be interrupted in order to use the telephone
The engine must be switched off in order to use the telephone
A mobile phone may not be used for more than 15 seconds while driving

text: What can be the consequence of your passenger (pillion passenger) on the motorbike not wearing conspicuous clothing?
explanation: If your passenger does not wear highly visible clothes (conspicuous clothes), it will make you less visible for people driving behind you
options: - more difficult to recognise for the following traffic
- more difficult to recognise for the traffic ahead
- more difficult to recognise for oncoming traffic

text: Why can motorcycles be overseen despite having their dipped headlights switched on?
explanation: Motorcycles are easy to miss because they are small and even more so if they are fast and wear clothes that are hard to see
options: Because they are narrower than cars
Because if highly accelerated, motorcycles can approach extremely quickly
Because the persons onboard sometimes drive wearing inconspicuous clothing

text: What may be expected if you do not wear conspicuous protective motorcycle clothing when riding a motorbike?
explanation: If you do not wear highly visible clothes (conspicuous clothes), you will be less visible to other drivers, people on the road and will thus have a higher risk of accidents
options: I am more difficult to see
I have an increased risk of having an accident
I may anticipate no negative effects

text: Why is it extremely advisable to wear protective motorcycle clothing during the journey?
explanation: Protective motorcycle clothes will protect you against injuries in case of an accident. It does not reduce aquaplaning nor protect the motorcycle.
options: Injuries may be reduced in the event of a fall
Aquaplaning can be prevented during rainy conditions
In the event of accidents, the motorbike will be protected from damage

text: What statements apply to the term "blind spot"?
explanation: In the blind spot you can not see by means of mirrors. Especially for bikers, this is particularly dangerous. The navigability of the Tropic has nothing to do with it and is wrong.
options: - is particularly dangerous for cyclists
- is not visible even with mirrors
- cannot be driven over due to the turning circle

text: What lighting is permissible so that you can be seen as early as possible in road traffic during day-light?
explanation: During the day in order to be visible you are permitted to use dipped headlights and daytime running lights
options: Dipped headlights
Daytime running lights
Parking light

text: You want to exit a parking space and drive onto the road. What must you watch out for in particular?
explanation: You should also check on the vehicle especially to children playing. To the possible swiveling out of your vehicle and on the flow of traffic. All three are correct.
options: For children playing around the vehicle
For moving traffic
For my vehicle swinging out sharply

text: Why is it risky to ride without protective motorcycle clothing?
explanation: Wearing protective motorcycle clothing will decrease the risk of injury in case of accident and will also protect you against the weather. In case of an accident insurance cover will be reduce if you do not wear protective clothing
options: - an increased risk of injury
- less protection from weather conditions
- less insurance cover available should a damage event occur

text: Why should you wear protective motorcycle clothing with a high-visibility colouring?
explanation: Wearing highly visible colours will make you easier to see and will thus reduce the risk of accidents
options: Because it means others can see me better
Because it reduces the risk of an accident
Because it means I can still drive home if my lights fail

text: As a motorcyclist what should you do to make yourself more visible to others during the daytime?
explanation: In order to be more visible and reduce the risk of accidents during the daytime, you should wear highly visible protective clothes and use either the dipped headlights or daytime running lights
options: By wearing high-visibility protective motorcycle clothing
By driving with dipped headlight or daytime running lights switched on
By driving with the main beam light on

text: You want to make a right turn within a built-up area. What risks could arise here?
explanation: 3 answers are correct. There is both a danger straight run cyclist to miss, as well as pedestrians and compromising by too wide arc oncoming traffic.
options: - fail to see cyclists travelling straight ahead
- fail to see pedestrians
- endangering oncoming traffic by following an excessively wide turning circle

text: As the vehicle owner, what change must you report to the relevant licensing authority?
explanation: If you change your name or place of residence, you must notify the vehicle licensing authority. However, you do not have to report the change in your liability insurance.
options: - my home address
- my name
- my third-party insurance

text: You are the new owner of a licensed vehicle. What do you have to do?
explanation: When replacing the owner, you do not need to carry out a general inspection. You must inform the vehicle licensing authority that the owner changed and provide them with a third-party liability insurance.
options: - notify the licensing authority of the change in ownership
- present the licensing authority with proof of the existence of liability insurance for the vehicle

explanation: A full-face helmet offers more protection than other helmet models, as full-face helmets are completely closed. text: When riding a motorbike, what makes you more visible to other road users?

explanation:
The motorbike gloves should fit snugly but not be too tight. Your fingers should be slightly bent without the fabric stretching.
The gloves should give you a good grip so that you can operate the brake and clutch levers without any problems.
Choose motorbike gloves made of abrasion-resistant materials such as leather or special textiles in order to be better protected against abrasions and burns in the event of a fall or accident.

- provide a good grip

text: How do you secure a car with a manual gearbox against rolling away on a downhill slope?
explanation: You can prevent a car with a manual transmission from rolling away by engaging a small gear, such as first gear or reverse gear. Use the parking brake and do not place the gearstick in the neutral position.
options: Apply the parking brake
Engage first gear or reverse gear
Put the gear lever in neutral position

text: How do you secure a car with automatic transmission against rolling away on a downhill slope?
explanation: You can secure a car with automatic transmission against rolling away by activating the parking brake and additionally bringing the selector lever into the parking position 'P'. You may not select the position 'N', as this is the same as idling in a vehicle with manual transmission.
options: Apply the parking brake
Put the selector lever in the "P" position
Put the selector lever in the "N" position

text: What must you do when reversing?
explanation: As a car driver, you are only allowed to drive backwards very slowly and with the utmost caution. When driving, look mainly to the back and in all other directions. You do not need to turn on the hazard warning light when reversing.
options: Mainly look to the back; also check the traffic situation at the front and at the side
Drive with particular attention and slowly
Never drive without switching on the hazard warning lights

text: What can interfere with your view?

Smeared windows

text: Your vehicle is snowed under. What do you have to do before you drive off?

- remove ice and snow from the roof of the vehicle

text: Your vehicle is snowed under. What do you have to do before you drive off?

text: What should be observed when positioning the head rests in your car?
explanation: With correctly adjusted headrests the car driver reduces the force on the cervical spine in case of sudden vehicle movements. This makes headrests a direct protection device for the protection of the vehicle occupants in accidents. The headrests that can be adjusted electrically or manually in height and inclination should be adjusted so that the crown height of the head coincides with the top edge of the headrest. In order for their protective function to be fully effective, you should tilt the headrest so that your back of the head is no more than a few centimeters away from it.
options: The top of the head should be level with the upper edge of the head rest
The spacing between the rear of the head and the head rests should be as small as possible
The upper edge of the head rest should conjoin with the upper neck vertebra

text: When should you refrain from using the telephone even if you have a hands-free device?
explanation: Despite the availability of a hands-free system, you are likely to become nervous and anxious during difficult conversations. You will pay more attention to the person you are talking to and concentrate less on the road. Distraction can cause you to miss something in traffic and not be able to react quickly enough. You should also avoid using your phone in difficult traffic situations.
options: When the telephone conversations are stressful
In complicated traffic conditions
If this would distract me

text: You want to use a smartphone mounted on your motor vehicle as a navigation device. What should you observe?
explanation: To protect yourself, you should enter your destination in the stationary vehicle and, if possible, not operate the device while driving. Use the device's voice output. So you are not distracted and can concentrate on the traffic.

text: You are planning a long journey with your motor vehicle. Before commencing the journey, what should you check on the vehicle to avoid endangering yourself and others?
explanation:
You should check your tyres at regular intervals, because wear, damage or incorrectly adjusted air pressure as well as insufficient tread depth represent a major safety risk.
A minimum tread depth of 1.6 mm applies. 
The headlights should also be checked for defects and their correct setting. For example, headlights that are set too high can dazzle oncoming traffic. 
A clear view should be ensured on every journey. This includes not only ensuring that the windscreen is free of dirt, but also that there is still sufficient windscreen washer fluid.

That the windscreen wipers are working properly

text: While driving, the inside of your vehicle’s windscreen begins to mist over. How can you counteract this?

options: By turning on the climate control system

text: Your car is snowed in. What do you need to do before you start your journey?
explanation:

In addition, the snow could slide onto your windshield when you brake, blocking your visibility and making you completely unable to act. Also remove the snow from the lighting equipment so that other road users can see you in good time and you have adequate visibility even in dark lighting conditions. 
Also make sure that no snow covers your license plates. If the license plates are illegible, you risk an administrative offense and a fine.
options: - remove snow from number plate
- remove snow from the vehicle’s roof
- remove snow from the lighting equipment

- proceed and inform the nearest municipal office

text: Your vehicle has left a considerable amount of dirt on the carriageway, causing a risk to road traffic. What do you have to do?
explanation: The following road users will thank you if you eliminate immediately the pollution and the danger point to the elimination doing sufficiently marked. In an easy recognition of the danger spot doing nothing is wrong.
options: - clean up the dirt without delay
- properly indicate the point of danger until the cleaning has taken place
- do nothing if the point of danger is easily recognisable

text: What do you have to do when exiting a construction site in your vehicle?
explanation: When leaving a construction site you should ensure that no charge can fall down and clean the tires and lighting equipment. Also remove jammed stones between the dual tires. All three answers are correct.
options: - clean the tyres and the lighting systems
- remove any stones jammed into between twin tyres
- ensure that none of the load can fall off

text: How should you behave when you leave a construction site with your vehicle?
explanation: When leaving a construction site, it is important to clean the lighting equipment to ensure that you are clearly visible to other road users and that road safety is not compromised. Removing stones trapped between the twin tires prevents them from being thrown out while driving, causing damage to other vehicles or causing accidents. In addition, loaded bulk material must be adequately covered to prevent material from falling onto the road while driving and thus posing a danger to following traffic. These measures serve to protect all road users and help prevent pollution and hazards in road traffic.
options: - clean the lighting equipment
- remove stones stuck between the twin tyres
- ensure that loaded bulk material is adequately covered

text: What must you do to avoid soiling the roadway?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Remove loose earth from the tyres before leaving the field
Clean working equipment before leaving the field
When it rains, only use truck tractors with twin tyres

text: When driving your agricultural vehicle, you could not avoid soiling the roadway. What must you do?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Take immediate measures to clean up the soiled area
Adequately mark the dangerous spot until the soilage is removed
Secure the dangerous spot by a warning triangle until the rain has washed the dirt away

text: You have dirtied the public highway with your agricultural vehicle. This is endangering or impeding traffic. What do you have to do?
explanation: Clean up the area and mark it visibly to eliminate a hazard.
options: - remove such dirt without delay
- adequately indicate the dirty area until the dirt can be removed
- always notifiy the office of public order of such soiling

text: What is the right course of action in this situation?
explanation: It can be seen that the accident scene has already been adequately secured. For this reason, you should not brake sharply as this is unnecessary in this situation. A strong deceleration would only increase the risk of further accidents (especially rear-end collisions), since subsequent motorists do not expect a braking maneuver. While driving, photographing the accident is prohibited.
options: I continue driving as before
I brake hard immediately
I take a photograph of the scene of the accident

text: What is the right course of action now?
explanation: On the right lane there was an accident and you drive towards the still unsecured accident site. Since the situation is not completely clear to you, you must reduce your speed. Drive as far to the left as possible to keep enough distance to the right-hand vehicles.
options: I reduce my speed
I continue driving as far to the left as possible
I continue driving as before

text: What is the right course of action now?
explanation: In the event of an accident, you should always play it safe and increase the safe distance as well as reduce your speed in case someone runs into the lane.
options: I reduce my speed further
I drive as far to the left as possible
I continue driving just as before

text: Your vehicle has collided with a wild animal. What is the right course of action here?
explanation: After a deer accident, you should switch on the hazard warning lights, put on a high-visibility waistcoat and set up a warning triangle to secure the accident site. You should notify the police, describe your accident and give your exact location.
options: I secure the scene of the accident
I notify the police
I load the animal into my vehicle

text: Why should you always carry the European accident report form with you on your journey?
explanation: The European Accident Report should be carried at all times, because it makes it easier to record accidents with people involved in the accident who speak other languages, and it enables the accident to be recorded independently.
options: - makes it easier to document the accident with foreign-speaking parties involved in the accident
- enables the parties involved to independently document the accident
- unambiguously clarifies the issue of liability at the scene of the accident

text: How does an eCall system work in the event of a serious accident?
explanation:
In the event of severe car accidents, for which, for example, airbags trigger, the ECALL system automatically sets a 112 emergency call. He transmits the accident clock time and the exact location.
Alternatively, vehicle occupants can also trigger an SOS signal manually-for example with a heart attack by the passenger.
options: - the position of the motor vehicle
- the time of the accident
- the severity of the injuries of the persons in the motor vehicle

text: In what situation is the eCall system designed to be triggered manually?
explanation: The emergency call system can also be triggered manually in the event of an urgent medical problem, e.g. with a heart attack of the moving, passing or as a helping, in a serious accident.
options: If I am witness to a serious accident
If a passenger suffers a medical emergency
If my vehicle sustains a puncture

text: You have an accident on the autobahn with your truck. In which order do you proceed?
explanation: In an accident with your truck on a highway, you should immediately stop, secure traffic and make out about the accident and potential injuries to help.
options: Stop immediately, ensure traffic safety, check the effects of the accident and help any injured persons
Stop immediately, find witnesses, ensure traffic safety and help injured persons
Stop, call the police, switch on your hazard warning lights and wait

text: While you are travelling on the autobahn, your passengers tell you there is smoke in the bus. What must you do?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Stop immediately on the hard shoulder and secure the vehicle at a sufficient distance
Direct your passengers to a location at a safe distance away from the bus and autobahn
Drive on to the next petrol station to get help

text: Your bus overturns in an accident and you cannot open the doors. What must you do?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Tell the passengers to leave the bus through the emergency windows and emergency doors and to remain calm
Ask uninjured passengers to help bring injured and frail persons and children out of the bus safely
First wait for help

text: You are involved in a pile-up accident on the autobahn in fog. Your bus is wedged in by other vehicles. What must you do?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Take injured persons and passengers to a place at a safe distance from the bus and autobahn and give first aid
Once you have evacuated the passengers to safety, return to the scene of the accident
First, look for witnesses at the scene of the accident

text: You break down and have to stop on the right hand hard shoulder of an autobahn. What must you do?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Switch on your hazard warning lights and place warning signs (safety devices) at a sufficient distance behind the vehicle
Ensure that your passengers remain at a safe distance away from the bus and autobahn
Call for help unless you can repair the vehicle yourself

text: Who is a party involved in an accident?
explanation: A participant in a traffic accident can be a person whose conduct has contributed to the selfsame and a person who caused the accident.
options: A person whose conduct may have contributed to the accident
A person who has caused the accident
A person who is a witness to what happened

text: Does the person involved in an accident have to move his/her vehicle to the side?
explanation: A participant in the accident should drive his vehicle aside if only minor damage. So that traffic can continue to flow.
options: Yes, in the case of minor damage
Yes, in any case
No, never

text: You are involved in a traffic accident. To ensure that passengers are not endangered, they must leave the bus. However, it is no longer possible to open the doors of your bus. What must you do now?
explanation:
If you are involved in a traffic accident and the doors do not open, you should first calm down the passengers.
Ask the passengers to leave the vehicle via the designated emergency outputs and ask the passengers to help each other.
options: - calm the passengers
- request that the passengers use the emergency exits in the event of an emergency
- request the passengers to assist one another

text: While driving your bus on the motorway you become involved in a road traffic accident. The passengers need to disembark from the bus. What is the right course of action?
explanation: The first thing you should do is reassure the passengers and inform them of the situation. Then give the passengers clear instructions, ask them to leave the vehicle via the designated emergency exits and ask them to help each other.
options: I inform the passengers about the situation
I have to issue clear instructions about how to leave the bus safely
I have to remove my driver card from the tachograph

text: What do these signals indicate?
explanation: These permanent lights can either enable or disable the lanes, depending on the traffic. They always relate directly to the lane over which they are mounted. A green sign indicates that you are allowed to drive on the lane, a red cross blocks it, a yellow sign with arrow means for you: lane change.
options: The two lanes on the right are open to traffic
You may not use the two lanes on the left
You may use the two lanes on the left for overtaking only

text: You are travelling at a speed of approximately 40 km/h. The lights change from "green" to "amber" when you are 10 m away. What do you do?
explanation: At 40 km/h, the braking distance according to the rule of thumb is 28 meters. Even with emergency braking, a car driver can barely come to a halt 10 meters in front of a traffic light. To prevent a possible rear-end collision, you should therefore continue driving.
options: Proceed
Stop

text: You are travelling at a speed of approximately 40 km/h. The lights change from "green" to "amber" when you are 40 m away. What do you do?
explanation: According to the rule of thumb, at a speed of 40 km/h your car comes to a stand after 28 meters. The only correct reaction is to stop.
options: Stop
Proceed

text: You are approaching a traffic light which has been "green" for some time. What do you do?
explanation: Since the traffic light has been green for a while, it can switch at any moment. Continue at the same speed, watching the traffic light carefully and be ready to stop. Once you have reached your decision point - distance to the traffic light, from which a normal stop is no longer possible - drive on, even if the traffic light switches.
options: Watch the traffic light closely
Approach but be ready to stop
Accelerate even though the speed limit is exceeded

text: The traffic light has just changed to yellow. What is the right course of action if you are turning left?
explanation: The yellow traffic light indicates that you have to wait before the crossing. Since your distance to the stop line is far enough in this situation, you can safely stop.
options: - stop
- turn

text: What is true of permanently illuminated signs?
explanation: If there are crossed red diagonal beams, drivers on the lane must neither drive nor hold in front of them. A green arrow looking down means: You can drive on the lane. A yellow blinking, obliquely downward looking arrow, you must change the lane in the direction of the arrow.
options: Permanently illuminated signs either block lanes or open them up to traffic
Vehicles may not stop at the side of carriageways with permanently illuminated signs
Permanently illuminated signs apply to multi-track motor vehicles only

text: What do these permanently illuminated signs mean?
explanation: Continuous light signals above a lane inform you as a car driver whether this lane is passable or locked or if you need to leave it. Red crossed bars mean: The lane must not be used. A green arrow looking down means: You can drive on the lane. A yellow blinking, obliquely downward looking arrow, you must change the lane in the direction of the arrow.
options: - 1 may continue driving on it
- 2 must change to the right-side lane
- 3 and lane 4 must stop

text: A vehicle with flashing blue lights and siren sounding is approaching you from the rear. What is the right course of action now?
explanation: The vehicle must be given free access. Therefore, you must reduce your speed and drive as far as possible to the side of the road so that the vehicle with blue flashing lights can continue its way unhindered.
options: I drive over to the right-side as far as possible
I reduce my speed
I stop immediately

text: What do you do when you see this traffic sign on an autobahn?
explanation: Caution of congestion: With this traffic sign you should reduce the speed of your car and increase the distance to the vehicle in front. Get a better picture of the situation by watching the traffic in front of the next vehicle and, if necessary, drive a bit offset in the lane. Turn on your hazard lights when driving towards the end of a traffic jam.
options: Increase your alertness and, as a matter of precaution, increase your distance to the vehicle in front
In case of a traffic jam, brake and switch on hazard warning lights
In case of a traffic jam, move over onto the hard shoulder and proceed

text: What must you do when you see this traffic sign?
explanation: The traffic sign announces a dangerous left turn. Decrease your speed to keep the centrifugal force small. Oncoming traffic could reach your lane due to its centrifugal force. Also, a vehicle could have broken down behind the curve. Drive as far as possible to the right. You follow the road, there's no turn. Therefore, you do not have to indicate.
options: Reduce speed before the bend
Drive as far as possible over on the right-hand side
Indicate left before the bend

text: What do you do within this danger section?
explanation: Attention wild animals crossing: This sign is set up on routes, where a lot of wild animal accidents happened already. As soon as you see this sign, you should reduce the speed and be ready to brake. Pay particular attention to the roadside. If you see an animal, you should brake and dim. If game suddenly jumps in front of you, you should make an emergency brake. Avoid dodging, because then you might get into the oncoming lane.
options: Drive more slowly, watch out for wild animals
Dip the headlights and brake when you see wild animals
Do not avoid hitting wild animals if oncoming traffic would be endangered

text: What must you be prepared for upon seeing this traffic sign?
explanation: This traffic sign indicates a section of the route with crosswinds. This is especially true for bridges and overpasses. If there's strong wind from the side you have to reduce your speed. You need to be prepared to hold on and countersteer to stay in the lane. The traffic sign has nothing to do with air traffic.
options: For side winds
For counter-steering
For aircraft overhead

text: What must you be prepared for upon seeing this traffic sign?
explanation: If you encounter this traffic sign, you have to adjust to strong crosswinds. Most commonly, this traffic sign appears on road sections that are particularly exposed to the wind - for example, on bridges or overpasses. With strong crosswinds, the driver must countersteer in order to stay in the lane. You also need to adjust the speed of your car to the wind conditions.
options: For an alteration in the responsiveness of the vehicle
For the necessity for counter-steering
For the necessity for adjusting speed

text: What should you anticipate when you see this road sign?
explanation: Because of trees, tall vehicles can brake suddenly and swerve. Tall vehicles can tear off branches as they pass, and these then lie on the roadway. Be especially attentive.
options: Vehicles ahead that may swerve out suddenly to the left
Vehicles ahead that may brake suddenly
Tree branches lying on the roadway

text: What must you anticipate with this road sign?
explanation: All 3 answers are correct. Trees may lie in the driveway, branches may lie in the road, and cars may suddenly give way.
options: Trees could protrude into my road area
There could be branches lying on the roadway
Vehicles could swerve suddenly

text: What is correct from this traffic sign onwards?
explanation: This sign indicates that no vehicles can proceed, you therefore cannot ride your motorized bicycle but can still push it
options: You may push your motorized bicycle
You may drive on slowly with your motorized bicycle
You may proceed with your motorized bicycle when the engine is switched off

text: To what does the "12 t" refer on this traffic sign?
explanation: The total mass (12 t) refers to the vehicle including charge.
options: - of the vehicle including load
- of the vehicle excluding load
- of the load excluding the vehicle

text: On your 10 m-long vehicle, the load is projecting 60 cm over the vehicle’s rear edge. What applies to you when this traffic sign is displayed?
explanation: The length of your truck is described as 10.6 m. (10 m + 60 cm truck of the load) which dominates. That's why you must not enter this road as a whole, the length of your truck 10.6 m.
options: - not drive into a street displaying this sign, because, taken together, the vehicle and load are longer than 10 m
- drive into a street displaying this sign, if the load is specially marked
- drive into a street displaying this sign, because the load does not have to be taken into consideration

text: You are driving on this motorway. What is the right course of action?
explanation:
In principle, the right-hand driving rule applies on motorways. You are therefore obliged to drive in the right-hand lane unless you want to overtake. There is no one in front of you to overtake.
The left lane is closed. You may not use it under any circumstances. Not even if you have a breakdown.
options: I move into the right-hand lane
I only use the left-hand lane if there is a breakdown
I remain in my current lane

text: What is the right behaviour now?
explanation: You are allowed to accelerate because you have passed the construction site with the speed limit, moved back into the correct lane and the road in front of you is clear.
options: I accelerate
I maintain my speed
I only accelerate when the speed limit is removed by a road sign

text: What must you remember when you see this traffic sign?
explanation: This traffic sign indicates that the following route can only be used with snow chains. Driving without snow chains is prohibited. The maximum speed with snow chains is 50 km/h. Pay attention to noises. If you hear something or if your car is twitchy you should stop and check the chains. This sign has nothing to do with track vehicles.
options: Use snow-chains
Maximum permissible speed 50 km/h
Track-vehicles have priority

text: Which traffic sign refers to the permissible total mass?
explanation: As a car driver you should note that this traffic sign can be read in two ways. On the one hand, t 'stands for tons and thus refers to the actual weight. However, the traffic sign may also refer to the permissible total weight if the 't' is additionally marked by a white symbol.

text: Which traffic sign refers to the actual mass?
explanation: If the symbol 't' for tons is in the traffic sign, it refers to the actual weight. The actual weight is calculated from the empty weight of the vehicle plus the current load. The empty weight of the vehicle is noted in the vehicle documents. As a car driver, you are required to know the weight of your vehicle.

text: Which vehicles are prohibited from using a road sign-posted like this?
explanation: The traffic sign prohibits vehicles from traveling on the route that exceed the weight indicated on the traffic sign. The weight specification refers to the actual axle load. It must not be exceeded. The red round circle in the traffic sign always indicates a ban.
options: - with an actual axle weight exceeding 2 t
- with a permissible axle weight exceeding 2 t
- with a permissible total weight not exceeding 2 t

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: The traffic sign "Width Limit including load" indicates road constrictions and bottlenecks on the subsequent section of the road. The track is not passable for vehicles that are wider than indicated on the sign including their cargo. In this case, the permissible width is 2 m.
options: A prohibition for vehicles more than 2 m wide including load
A roadway 2 m wide
You must keep a lateral distance of at least 2 m from other vehicles

text: Which vehicles can cause serious accidents when this traffic sign is ignored?
explanation: This traffic sign is aimed at trucks and warns of height-limited passages - in front of tunnels, bridge constructions or heavy current overhead wires of trams. The height limit is indicated by the black triangles, here it is 3.8 m. If a vehicle higher than 3.8 m ignores this sign, serious accidents may occur. The truck may get caught or stuck in the overhead wires or the underpass. Length and width are not relevant.
options: Length 8 m, width 2.5 m, height 4 m
Length 10 m, width 3.9 m, height 3 m
Length 4 m, width 2.5 m, height 2.5 m

text: With which vehicles are you not allowed to drive on a road sign-posted like this?
explanation: The red round circle in the traffic sign always indicates a ban. Vehicles whose actual length exceeds 10 m may not drive on this road. Even vehicles with trailers whose total length exceeds 10 m may not continue on this road. This indicates road conditions that are not passable with longer vehicles.
options: Car with caravan trailer, total length of the combination 11 m
Tractor with trailer, total length of the combination 12 m
Truck with a length of 9 m including load

text: What vehicles may you overtake when this traffic sign is displayed?
explanation: You are not allowed to overtake, neither single nor multi-lane vehicles.
options: No vehicles
Single-track vehicles
Multi-track vehicles

text: What motor vehicles are subject to the no-overtaking rule indicated by this sign?
explanation: This traffic sign prescribes a ban on overtaking for motor vehicles with a permissible total weight of more than 3.5 t. The additional sign also prescribes overtaking for buses and cars WITH trailers.
options: Coaches or buses
Single-track motor vehicles
Cars without trailers

text: Which vehicles are prohibited from using a road sign-posted like this?
explanation: The road marked on the sign you darst not drive when you are driving tractors or trucks t with a maximum mass of more than 3.5. Cars with trailers are allowed to drive here.
options: Trucks with a permissible total mass exceeding 3.5 t
Truck tractors
Cars with trailers

text: Which vehicles must keep the minimum distance of 70 m here?
explanation: Both tractors and trucks t with a maximum mass of more than 3.5. Map for these special rules. Cars are not included.
options: Trucks with a permissible total mass exceeding 3.5 t
Truck tractors
Cars

text: Which vehicles are not allowed to overtake here?
explanation: Trucks and trucks with a gross vehicle mass exceeding 3.5 tonnes and tractors may not overtake at the sign.
options: Trucks and trucks with trailers with a permissible total mass exceeding 3.5 t
Truck tractors
Cars

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign indicates a ban on labeling requirements vehicles carrying dangerous goods. All other permitted in this zone.
options: Motor vehicles with mandatory markings carrying dangerous goods are prohibited
Vehicles with an actual axle weight exceeding 3.5 t are prohibited
Trucks and combinations of vehicles are prohibited

text: You want to enter a road displaying this road sign. To what does the information "12 t" refer?
explanation: This sign refers to the actual mass of the vehicle, including cargo. Please mind that.
options: - actual weight of the vehicle
- gross vehicle weight rating of the vehicle
- unladen weight of the vehicle

text: On this road traffic sign, to what does the information “12 t” refer?
options: - actual mass of the vehicle
- maximum authorised mass of the vehicle
- actual mass of the load

text: You are driving a road haulage combination vehicle with a maximum authorised mass of 30 t. When may you continue driving after seeing this road traffic sign?
explanation: You may only drive on this road if you have to deliver a load to a resident or if this is a designated diversion route.
options: - have to deliver the consignment to a local resident
- am driving on a designated diversionary route
- am able to comply with the driving and rest periods by doing so

text: You are driving a vehicle combination comprising a motor vehicle and trailer, and you want to enter a road that has this signpost. What does the reference to “5.5 t” mean?
explanation: The traffic sign refers to the actual mass of each individual vehicle, the vehicle combination, including charge.
options: - actual mass of each individual vehicle in the vehicle combination
- actual total mass of the vehicle combination
- maximum authorised mass of the towing vehicle

text: When you see this road sign, what is the situation in which you must keep a minimum distance of 70 metres from the vehicle in front?
explanation: As a driver of a truck with a maximum permissible mass of over 3.5 tonnes or as a driver of a tractor, I must keep a distance of at least 70 meters if there is a truck in front of me with a permissible maximum mass of over 3.5 tonnes.
options: - am driving a lorry with a permissible total weight of over 3.5 t behind another lorry with a permissible total weight of over 3.5 t
- am driving a tractor unit behind a lorry with a permissible total weight of over 3.5 t
- am driving a lorry with a permissible total weight of over 3.5 t behind a car with a trailer

text: What motor vehicles are prohibited from driving on a road where this sign is displayed?
explanation:
This road sign describes a driving ban for tractors with a design-related maximum speed up to 25 km / h, as well as for motor vehicles with a trailer with a permissible maximum speed up to 25 km / h. 
This does not apply to tractors with a maximum design speed of more than 40 km/h.
options: Tractors with a type-specific maximum speed of 25 km/h
Motor vehicles with trailers with a maximum permissible speed of 25 km/h
Tractors with a type-specific maximum speed in excess of 40 km/h

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign is at the end of the motorway.
options: The end of the autobahn
The end of the clearway for motor vehicles only
Temporary closure of the autobahn

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign is placed at the end of a highway. It means: From here on the advisory speed limit no longer applies. It does not indicate a ban on motor vehicles.
options: The end of the clearway for motor vehicles only
The end of the autobahn
Motor vehicles prohibited

text: What do such traffic signs indicate?
explanation: A white number on a blue background with a white outline indicates the number of the motorway you are currently on.
options: The number of an autobahn
The distance to the next petrol station
The number of a European road

text: What does the figure "26" indicate in this traffic sign?
explanation: All motorway exits are numbered for better orientation. As a car driver, you can recognize the freeway exit ramp by the number 26. On road maps, in road atlases and in the common navigation devices, these numbers can also be found again.
options: Autobahn exit number 26
The A 26
The distance from the exit to Düsseldorf-Benrath

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign refers to a detour for freeway traffic. It is set up in the event of a traffic jam, for example. If the car driver follows the detour, he/she returns to the freeway.
options: A diversion for autobahn traffic when required
An underground station
Federal road (Bundesstrasse) 22

text: What applies from this traffic sign onwards?
explanation: This traffic sign is subject to regulations that apply to traffic within built-up areas. This includes limiting the maximum speed to 50 km/h. Free choice of lanes applies only to vehicles up to 3.5 t permissible maximum mass. Vehicles with more than 3.5 t drive on the right.
options: Maximum permissible speed 50 km/h
Free choice of marked driving lanes for motor vehicles with a permissible total mass up to 3.5 t
Free choice of marked driving lanes for all motor vehicles

text: What applies when you see this traffic sign?
explanation: In towns, you are allowed to deviate from the requirement to drive on the right, i.e. you are free to choose your lane on multi-lane roads. On two-lane roads in towns, vehicles in the right lane may also drive faster than vehicles in the left lane, but you are still not allowed to drive faster than 50 km/h in towns.
options: - choose whatever lane I wish for my direction of travel
- drive more quickly in the right-hand lane than vehicles travelling in the left-hand lane
- drive faster than 50 km/h because this is a multi-lane carriageway

text: What applies from this traffic sign onwards?
explanation: Car drivers recognize from this traffic sign that the regulations for traffic within closed villages apply. You must not announce overtaking maneuvers by honking, as this is only allowed outside closed villages. In general, it is forbidden to drive with parking lights. Parking cars may be secured with the parking light.
options: You may not sound your horn to signal your intention to overtake
Parking cars may be safely marked with parking light
You may drive with parking light in the darkness

text: How are vehicles with a permissible total mass up to 2.8 t allowed to be parked here?
explanation: This traffic sign signals to the vehicle driver that vehicles up to 2.8 t of permissible total mass may only be parked in accordance with the illustration. However, smaller cars also have to comply with these regulations as well.
options: The car as shown in the picture
The caravan as shown in the picture
Small cars also diagonally to the driving direction

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: The square traffic sign with a blue border indicates that there is a refuel possibility for hydrogen-powered vehicles in the immediate vicinity. These cars are still relatively expensive, but are considered the vehicles of the future.
options: - hydrogen filling station
- natural gas fuel station
- auto gas filling station

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: This traffic sign points out a natural gas filling station where drivers can refuel their natural gas-powered vehicle. The abbreviation CNG stands for the term compressed natural gas.
options: - natural gas fuel station
- hydrogen filling station
- auto gas filling station

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: The inscription LPG on the square traffic sign is an abbreviation for Liquefied Petroleum Gas. This traffic sign signals to the car driver that there is an LPG station.
options: - auto gas filling station
- natural gas fuel station
- hydrogen filling station

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: You will see a plug with cable on the sign. It shows you a nearby charging station for electric vehicles such as electric cars, e-bikes or electric scooters. There you can charge your powered vehicle.
options: A charging station for electric vehicles
A danger of explosion at a filling station through electric devices
A facility for charging mobile telephones

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?
explanation: The traffic sign P + R on a blue background stands for "Park and Ride". It identifies a parking lot with public transport connection. The parking lot is continuous or temporary.
options: A carpark with connections to public transport ("Park + Ride")
A filling station with carwash ("Care + Clean")
A car hire centre with repair workshop ("Breakdown service + Repair")

text: You are driving a toll-chargeable truck and are approaching the displayed traffic sign. What should you do?
explanation: You can only continue if the toll was paid for using the route and you should check whether it is correctly set the correct number of axles here without on-board unit (OBU). If not, ask me correctly.
options: I check the on-board-unit (OBU), to see if the number of axles is set correctly
I may continue driving without an on-board-unit (OBU), only if a toll was paid for using the route
I pay the toll at the toll station upon leaving the toll route

text: What is correct in this situation?
explanation: Driving a protective strip continuously is not permitted. Protective strips have a dashed mark and can be driven by car if necessary, especially to avoid oncoming traffic. But you can only do that if bicycle traffic is not endangered.
options: - allowed to drive on the advisory bike lane after I have ruled out any risk to cyclists by carefully observing the road traffic situation
- allowed to drive on the advisory bike lane only until I am past the truck
- not allowed to drive on the advisory bike lane

text: Which document allows you to park here?
explanation: You are allowed to park in the parking lot with this sign if you yourself have an EU parking permit for severely disabled people or if you are transporting a person with an EU parking permit for severely disabled people.
options: My EU parking card for people with severe disabilities
The EU parking card of a severely disabled person whom I am transporting
My residential parking permit

text: You need assistance on the autobahn. Which information does the arrow on the roadside marker give you?
explanation: Arrows on the reflector posts on the edge of a freeway point towards the nearest emergency services pillar. If you need help, follow the arrows to reach an emergency pillar as quickly as possible.
options: Nearest emergency call telephone in the direction of the arrow
Nearest car park in the direction of the arrow
Next exit in the direction of the arrow

text: What can you do to avoid unnecessary noise?
explanation: To avoid unnececessary noise, avoid making high revolutions with your engine and do not modify either the intake/exhaust system. Removing fairings do not impact noise.
options: Avoid high engine revolutions
Do not modify intake and exhaust systems
Remove the fairings

text: What can you do to avoid noise pollution?
explanation: To avoid above normal level of noise called noise pollution, do all of the above.
options: Don't drive off with spinning wheels
Avoid "power sound" through loudspeakers
Push the vehicle on residential premises, if possible

text: How can you save fuel?
explanation: You as a car driver can save fuel when you are traveling with your vehicle at low speeds. You should shift as early as possible into a higher gear and switch back as late as possible to keep the engine speeds low.
options: Change to a higher gear earlier
Change to a lower gear later
By driving frequently at high revolutions

text: How can noise be avoided?
explanation: Noise is generally generated by the running engine of a car. Driving at high speeds and strong acceleration contributes to increased noise. Stop the engine if you wait or park your vehicle somewhere for a longer amount of time.
options: If possible, avoid strong acceleration
By switching off the engine if you have to wait or stop for a longer period
By driving at high revolutions

text: How is avoidable noise caused?
explanation: Avoidable noise can be caused by driving with a defective exhaust system or by "playing" with the gas while standing. If a car driver honks because of a dangerous situation, this does not count as avoidable noise, but serves to avert danger.
options: By driving with a defective exhaust
By "playing" with the accelerator when standing still
By sounding your horn when in danger

text: Why should you avoid driving off at a rapid pace?
explanation: Making a racing start is an additional noise pollution for other road users. You as a car driver damage your vehicle as well as the tires due to high wear and abrasion with a racing start. The environment is additionally burdened. On the other hand, the rear-wheel brake is no longer and not any less loaded when starting.
options: Because the noise you cause annoys others
Because of heavier tyre wear
Because this is a great strain on the rear brake

text: How can you avoid pollution of the environment and benefit your engine after a cold start?
explanation: If possible, do not allow your vehicle to warm up while you are stationary as this will damage the engine and the environment. If warming up is done at low engine speeds, you will help to protect both. The engine is only fully resilient after reaching the operating temperature (green area).
options: Set off at low revolutions per minute without running the engine until it warms up
Do not accelerate, let the engine warm up while the vehicle is stationary
Accelerate several times when stationary so that a favourable operation temperature is quickly reached

text: Which vehicles are allowed to enter this environmental zone?
explanation: Motor vehicle drivers are only allowed to drive their vehicles into an environmental zone if the vehicle has a valid sticker visibly attached to it, which at least corresponds to the qualifying plate (red, yellow, green). Motorcycles and vehicles with special rights are excluded from this regulation.
options: A car with a red emissions sticker
A motorcycle
A car which meets the requirements for a green sticker even if it does not have an emissions sticker

text: What is caused by driving with winter tyres during the summer months?
explanation: Every car driver should know that winter tires are designed for use in cold and snowy streets. By using them in summer months, the driving stability decreases. Greater rubber abrasion and tire wear lead to increased fuel consumption.
options: - the fuel consumption
- tyre wear
- driving stability

text: What motor vehicles may enter an environment zone that has this sign?
explanation: The additional sign shows which motor vehicles with which sticker may enter. Motorbikes may enter in any case.
options: Motor vehicles with a green particulate emissions sticker
Motorcycles
Motor vehicles that meet the requirements for a green particulate emissions sticker, even if no such sticker is attached

text: You want to wash your car. Where should you do this in the interests of environmental protection?
explanation: You should always wash your vehicle in a car wash. There, the wastewater is disposed of by the operators in an environmentally friendly manner. On the other hand, if you wash your vehicle on the road or in a parking lot, the water gets into the ground untreated.
options: At a carwash
In a carpark
On an open road

text: What increases the fuel consumption of your vehicle considerably?
explanation: Turning on the seat heating or air conditioning of your vehicle consumes a lot of energy and increases the fuel consumption of your car significantly. Navigation devices require relatively little power compared to these devices.
options: - heated seats
- the air-conditioning
- the navigation device

text: What can reduce the fuel consumption of a commercial vehicle?
explanation: A reduction can cause all three answers. The use of louvers on the vehicle, the driver & predictive operation, even the use of special tires.
options: Fitting air cowls to the vehicle
The farsighted driving style of the driver
The use of special tyres

text: What are the effects of driving at high speed in motor vehicles with combustion engines?
explanation: Be aware that fast, high-speed driving results in high fuel consumption and high exhaust emissions. This also leads to more noise and to a not lower noise level.
options: Fuel consumption increases
The emission of harmful substances increases
The noise level is reduced

text: When riding a motorcycle, what can you do to avoid unnecessary noise?
explanation:
Improper exhaust systems lead to higher noise pollution. 
Uneven driving, such as frequent braking and then accelerating hard again, leads to unnecessary noise.
High-speed starting leads to unnecessary noise.
options: By only using permissible exhaust systems
By driving off at high speed
By adopting an uneven driving style

text: Why is an environmentally considerate driving style also beneficial for road safety?
explanation: Alternative fuels can also be used to drive fast. However, you will be driving in an environmentally friendly way if you avoid high speeds, if you drive with foresight and thus avoid, for example, braking hard and starting again.
options: - driving in a far-sighted manner
- avoiding high speeds
- that with alternative fuels it is only possible to drive slowly

text: What must you know about catalytic converters?
explanation: Vehicles with a catalytic converter should not be towed away. As a result, unburned fuel can flow into the catalytic converter and lead to damage or destruction of the catalyst. If the engine of the vehicle does not start even after several start attempts, the same consequences can occur.
options: A catalytic converter can be damaged or destroyed when the car is towed to start
A catalytic converter can be damaged when the engine starts after many unsuccessful attempts
Unburned fuel in the catalytic converter cannot cause any damage when the engine starts

text: Tyre wear is a burden to the environment. What can extend tyre life?
explanation: The wear of tires is the lowest when the tires are used as intended. Winter tires that are used in summer wear faster due to their material properties (rubber compound). Even with too little air pressure tires wear faster. Starting with high-speed and squealing tires wears tires due to increased abrasion.
options: Avoiding high speeds
Observing the tyre pressure indicated in the owner's manual
Using winter tyres (M+S) in the summer

text: How can you save fuel when driving a motor vehicle with automatic transmission?
explanation: Avoid the kick-down. The high-speed acceleration gear causes increased fuel consumption. For overtaking or merging on the freeway, however, it can be useful. With P, Parking, a vehicle with automatic transmission cannot be driven. Changing gears early to a higher gear also saves fuel.
options: By not using the "kick down" facility, if possible
When driving in town traffic, always keep the selector lever in the lowest gear
By driving in gear "P", if possible

text: How can you keep the burden on the environment low?
explanation: In order to relieve the environment, you should form carpools with others as a car driver. The environment is particularly burdened by the number of moving vehicles. In addition, you should avoid a concentrated accumulation of several vehicles such as traffic jams.
options: By forming car pools
By avoiding peak traffic periods
By avoiding roads with frequent traffic jams

text: What results in increased fuel consumption of your car?
explanation: Increased fuel consumption can be expected if, for example, you install roof or ski racks or if you load your vehicle with unnecessary objects. Increased tire pressure, on the other hand, does not matter for fuel consumption, even if it should be avoided altogether.
options: A roof rack or ski rack
Transporting unnecessary objects
Excessive tyre pressure

text: How can you save fuel?
explanation: Additional load and additional attachments such as roof racks or ski holders increase fuel consumption: when not in use, remove them. You save fuel when driving low-speed: shift up the gear early. Turning off the air conditioning system saves fuel, as does maintaining tire pressure according to the manufacturer's specifications. Because too little tire pressure increases the rolling resistance.
options: By observing at least the tyre pressure indicated in the owner's manual
By removing roof racks or ski racks
Avoid driving in top gear

text: What should you avoid for reasons of environmental protection?
explanation: After starting the engine, you as a car driver should start immediately in a low-speed driving style. Warming up the engine while stationary is not permitted. Driving at high speeds, extending gears and switching late, wastes fuel. Unnecessary driving causes avoidable exhaust emissions.
options: Letting the engine warm up when the vehicle is stationary
Unnecessary trips
Loud music with windows opened

text: Which conduct shows awareness of the environment?
explanation: Avoid driving around aimlessly. Private transport pollutes the environment. Make carpools as often as you can. If possible, use public transport. If you are stuck in a traffic jam, do not run the engine unnecessarily, turn it off.
options: Changing to public transport at collective parking areas ("P + R")
