text: What happens if you engage too low a gear and quickly release the clutch when driving at high speed?
explanation: If you engage a gear that is too low and release the clutch, your motorcycle will brutally decelerate and could cause you to fall or slip sideways
options: The rear wheel locks and can slip sideways
A fall is often unavoidable
The front wheel lifts off the ground

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What must you check on your motorcycle before you set off?
explanation: Before starting to drive, make sure that the rearview mirrors are correctly installed, adjusted and work properly (not broken, blind) and that the breaks work properly
options: The adjustment of the rear-view mirrors
Brake fluid level, lever travel
Setting of the camshaft

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: When do you have to increase tyre pressure?
explanation: Tire pressure need to be increased if driving with more weight (additional passenger, heavy luggage) or when driving for long distances especially at high speed
options: When you have a passenger
When driving on autobahns for longer periods of time at high speed
When driving with heavy luggage

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What must you remember when taking a passenger?
explanation: A passenger increases the weight on your motorcycle. This makes accelerating and thus overtaking longer. It increases the centrifugal force when turning and increases the braking distance.
options: Driving characteristics change on bends, particularly when entering and leaving the bend
Under the same conditions, overtaking requires a longer distance
Under the same conditions, the braking distance is reduced

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What must you do to be ready to brake?
explanation: By placing your hand on the handbrakes and foot over the brake pedal you improve your reaction time to break
options: Place your hand on the handbrake lever
Position your foot over the brake pedal
Change to a higher gear

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Why does the rear wheel of a motorcycle tend to lock when braking rather than the front wheel?
explanation: When breaking, more weight is applied on the front wheel and less on the back wheel which can lock the back wheel
options: - the load on the rear wheel is reduced
- the rear wheel is still propelled
- the load on the rear wheel increases

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What is correct when driving round bends on downhill slopes?
explanation: When going downhill you need to break more than on bends on flat areas. You should therefore break enough before the bend, you should also keep your distance from the demarcation line from the oncoming traffic in case you need to tilt your motorcycle more
options: Brake adequately before the bend so that no additional braking is needed on the bend
Start taking the bend so that you do not get into the area of oncoming traffic even when you are leaning far over
When you do not see any oncoming traffic, follow the ideal line and use the whole width of the roadway

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are driving round a bend at a brisk pace which is tighter than you first thought. What do you do?
explanation: In this situation, making a sharp steering movement will be dangerous and could lead to a fall. You should decelerate gradually and lean further to turn more. If you brake sharply while turning, a torque force would tilt you from leaning to one side to a more upward position which will increase the radius of your turn
options: Throttle back, lean further over
Do not brake sharply
Make an immediate sharp steering movement

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What must you particularly remember when raising motorcycles onto their stands (centre stands)?
explanation: To avoid the motorcycle to tip over or fall, you must ensure that the ground is firm, even and not too steep on a downward slope
options: - must be hard and even
- should not slope steeply downwards
- must not slope upwards

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Why is the rule of having to adapt your driving to your visibility particularly important in bends?
explanation: In a bend, there is limited visibility due to the curvature of the road. You should reduce your speed as unforeseen risk factors such as dirt on the road, obstacles or tighter bends could appear
options: Because bends can be tighter than expected
Because dangerously soiled roadways may be recognized too late
Because otherwise you lose too much momentum

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: How can you counteract centrifugal force?
explanation: The centrifugal force can be either reduced by driving at a slower speed or be counteracted by leaning over more. Accelerating will do the opposite and increase the centrifugal force
options: By leaning over
By reducing speed
By accelerating rapidly

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What can happen if a motorcycle is accelerated rapidly?
explanation: Accelerating while turning will increase the centrifugal force which will increase the radius of your turn. This could result in being directed in incoming traffic or on the pavement. In a straight line accelerating rapidly decrease stability
options: If turning left, the motorcycle could leave the roadway and endanger pedestrians on the pavement
If turning right, the motorcycle can veer into the path of oncoming traffic
If driving straight ahead, driving stability is increased in any case

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What must be changed before driving with a heavy load?
explanation: When driving with heavy loads, make sure to increase the tire pressure and adjust the pre-tension in the suspension springs
options: Pre-tensioning of the springs
Tyre pressure
Chain tension

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Which checks are particularly important before setting off?
explanation: All three are important to check before starting to drive. Make sure your visor is in good condition and not damaged or scratched. If you carry weight, make sure it is evenly distributed to not impact your center of gravity and do not impact your stability. Also ensure that the rear tire is in good condition.
options: Profile of the rear tyre
Even load (front/rear, right/left)
Condition of your visor

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: In which cases should you apply the brakes only very carefully?
explanation: You should break carefully on slippery surfaces such as wet roads, tram tracks, sewer covers, lane markings but also dirt roads, roads with sand, stones as well as when driving with new tires
options: On roadways with loose chippings or sand
On tram tracks, sewer covers and lane markings
When driving for the first time with new tyres

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What is the normal braking procedure for motorcycles?
explanation: You should apply both brakes which will result in a shorter stopping distance than only applying one of the breaks
options: Applying both brakes
Applying the rear brake only
Applying the front brake only

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Why must both brakes on a motorcycle always be in perfect working order?
explanation: Both brakes are required to function in case one of them suddenly fail, the other one can take over. Additionally using both brakes diminish the stopping distance compared to breaking with just one break
options: To achieve the shortest possible braking distance
To be able to brake if one of the brakes fails
To safely park the motorcycle on a downhill slope

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Is there a difference in the tendency of the wheels to lock?
explanation: When breaking, more weight is applied on the front wheel and less on the back wheel. For this reason, the back wheel tends to lock first
options: Yes, as a rule, the rear wheel locks first
Yes, as a rule, the front wheel locks first
No, as a rule, both wheels lock at the same time

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Is there a difference in the braking action?
explanation: When breaking, more weight is applied on the front wheel and less on the back wheel thus the front brake provides more braking power
options: Yes, as a rule the front wheel brake has greater braking action
Yes, as a rule the rear wheel brake has greater braking action
No, as a rule, both brakes have the same braking action

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You come unexpectedly upon a stretch of road with loose chippings. What do you do?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: Reduce speed cautiously
Avoid braking hard and leaning over
Apply the front brake only

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Your vehicle was parked for a long time in the open in moist weather. What must you reckon with when applying the brakes for the first time?
explanation: When wet, brakes are less effective and the wheels will have a tendency to lock more. It has however no impact on braking of the engine on a lower gear.
options: The wheels have a dangerous tendency to lock
Reduced braking action
Reduced braking action of the engine

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What can be the reason for a motorized bicycle skidding on bends?
explanation: Skidding risk is increases because of slippery surfaces such as wet road, ice, sand, dirt, leaves, cobblestones, manholes. It can also be created due to heavy braking.
options: Heavy braking
Wet or icy road surface
Sand or loose chippings

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: When does the braking distance increase?
explanation: The heavier the vehicle, the longer will be the braking distance. Downward slopes as well as slippery surfaces also increase the braking distance
options: When driving down slopes
When carrying heavy luggage
When there is headwind

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What particular characteristics of disc brakes must you remember when driving on a wet road surface?
explanation: As a car driver you have to take into account that when the street is wet the effect of the disc brakes usually takes effect much later than on a dry road.
options: As a rule, the effect of disc brakes starts later than on a dry road surface
As a rule, the effect of disc brakes starts earlier than on a dry road surface

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What increases the danger of "flying out" of a bend when driving at high speed?
explanation: Decelerating or accelerating your car will result in less steering effort. As a result, there is an increased danger of "flying out" of the curve at high speed. Uncouple to get more steering power.
options: Braking
Accelerating
Disengaging the clutch

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What must you take into consideration when checking tyre pressure?
explanation: When checking tire pressure, you must also take into account the temperature and load of the vehicle. These can influence the tire pressure. By contrast, the material of the wheel rim doesn't matter.
options: Load/Number of passengers in the car
Tyre temperature
Material of the wheels (steel/aluminium)

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You drive round a bend once at 30 km/h and again at 60 km/h. How does the centrifugal force change?
explanation: The centrifugal force quadruples when the speed is doubled, that is, when you take the curve at 60 km/h the second time.
options: - is four times as high
- is twice as high
- is the same

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What increases the effect of centrifugal force on the vehicle when driving round bends?
explanation: The speed has an immediate effect on the level of centrifugal force. Your braking distance quadruples when you drive at twice the speed. The centrifugal force increases the smaller the curve radius. The tire pressure has no effect on the centrifugal force.
options: Higher speed
Smaller radius of a bend
Higher tyre pressure

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are driving a motorcycle with sidecar on the right. Which driving technique must you use on bends?
explanation: Driving with a sidecar increase your weight, you thus need to go slower when turning
options: Moderate throttle on right-hand bends
Release throttle and brake lightly on left-hand bends
Always disengage the clutch on all bends

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Where should a passenger on a motorcycle with sidecar sit to reduce the risk of tipping over on bends?
explanation: In order to keep a motorcycle with a sidecar stable, the weight should be equaly distributed on each side of the center of gravity. The second passenger therefore should sit in the sidecar
options: In the sidecar
On the motorcycle
The position of the occupants has no significance

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What can you do if the sidecar lifts off the ground on a right-hand bend when you are driving a motorcycle and sidecar (sidecar on the right)?
explanation: When turning right, a torque force will push the sidecar up. To reduce this torque you can slow down, shift your body weight to the right and make a wider turn.
options: Release throttle, brake, shift your body weight to the right
Reduce steering lock angle, trace a wider arc within the lane you are travelling
Increase steering lock angle, accelerate

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What can happen to a motorcycle with a sidecar attached on the right when driving too fast round a right-hand bend?
explanation: When turning right, a torque force will push the sidecar up. At high speed the sidecar could be lifted-up, loose contact with the ground and tip over.
options: The sidecar lifts off the ground and the combination tips over
The motorcycle lifts off the ground and the combination tips over to the right

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: So far, you have only driven solo motorcycles. You now change over to a combination (sidecar on the right, unbraked). How does driving differ?
explanation: As the sidecar is attached to your right, you cannot lean right and need to steer instead. When accelerating the sidecar tends to be pulled to the right. When breaking the sidecar will be pulled to the left
options: When accelerating, the combination pulls to the right
When driving on bends, you must steer instead of leaning over
When braking, the combination pulls to the right

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: So far, you have only driven solo motorcycles. You now change over to a combination (sidecar on the right, unbraked). What is different?
explanation: As the sidecar is attached to your right, you cannot lean right and need to steer instead. When turning right, a torque force will push your sidecar up. At high speed the sidecar could be lifted-up, loose contact with the ground and tip over. When accelerating the sidecar tends to be pulled to the right. When breaking the sidecar will be pulled to the left
options: When braking, the combination pulls to the left
The sidecar may lift off the ground on right-hand bends
You must not drive with dipped headlights during daytime

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What should you know about using the emergency operation of bus doors?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: - should enable anyone on the bus to open the doors following accidents and breakdowns
- if misused, can lead to the doors being opened when the bus is moving
- can only be released by the driver

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What can happen if you accelerate very rapidly when moving off on your motorbike?
explanation: Fast and sudden accelerations could lead to the front wheel lifting off the road, passenger falling and losing control overt the motorcycle as there is less or no steering due to less or no contact between the front wheel and the road
options: The passenger can fall off
The front lift can lift up from the road surface
I can lose control over the motorbike

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are driving a local transport bus and want to drive away from a bus stop. What must you look out for?
explanation: Coming soon...
options: - all doors are properly closed
- no persons are directly in front of the bus
- flowing traffic is not endangered

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are driving in the wet in a car with trailer on a narrow rural road and are approaching a clearly visible but tight left-hand bend. What should you do?
explanation: Decrease your speed before the turn. Take the weather conditions into account. Keep in mind that the centrifugal force grows twice as fast as the speed. You should only accelerate again in the curve vertex.
options: I reduce my speed before the bend
I remain in the centre of the lane and only accelerate again once I am back on the straight
I only brake once I have reached the apex of the bend

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What do you have to pay attention to, when jacking up a motorbike on its centre stand?
explanation: Setting a motorcycle on its centre stand requires more effort and can be difficult when on a steep slope. It is also sensitive to tipping over when tilted on the side
options: - can tip over even when just slightly tilted
- can be difficult to jack up when on a steep gradient
- is best jacked up from a seated position

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What should you do if your motorbike starts to wobble?
explanation: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, decelerate, disengage the clutch and brake. Do not accelerate as it might increase the wobble and lead to an accident. Also do not try to compensate it as it is dangerous and could also lead to an accident
options: - throttle back, disengage the clutch and brake carefully
- change down gears and accelerate as quickly as possible
- compensate wobbling by quickly counter-steering

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are driving a motorbike equipped with an anti-lock braking system (ABS). How do you perform an emergency braking manoeuvre?
explanation: Breaking both foot and hand brake will result in the shortest stopping distance. ABS improves the stopping distance by un-blocking the wheels during strong brakes
options: Effect the best-possible deceleration using hand and foot brake
Do not press the foot brake lever, because the ABS only functions at the front
Operate the hand and foot brake lever intermittently ("intermittent braking")

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: How can driver assistance systems be helpful?
explanation: Driver assistance systems assist the car driver and increase traffic safety when the navigation device is programmed before driving. However, driver assistance systems can not compensate for an unfitness to drive.
options: In increasing road safety
In assisting the driver
To compensate for unfitness to drive

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What must you be aware of, if you have to brake sharply while in a bend?
explanation: If you have to brake sharply in a curve, make sure that your motorcycle straightens up (inertia force). You have to turn harder to maintain the curve line.
options: My motorcycle will become upright
I have to steer more strongly in order to maintain my cornering line
My cornering line decreases

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What must you be aware of when driving a quad?
explanation: Reduce speed when turning, as quads tend to tip over due to their high centre of gravity.
options: Wearing a suitable crash helmet is mandatory
Quads are prone to tipping over when driving through tight bends
The handling characteristics are similar to those of a car

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What should be observed when driving a quad?
explanation: The quad has no steering assistance, so steering may be more difficult than driving a car.
options: Protective motorcycle clothing should be worn
A warning triangle must be carried on the quad
The necessary steering force can be significantly greater than with a car

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are driving a motorbike with a manual gearbox. What do you have to do in order to be ready to brake?
explanation: Put your foot and hand already over the brake levers to initiate the braking process more quickly.
options: I place my hand on the handbrake lever
I place my foot over the brake pedal
I change up to a higher gear

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You want to use a carrying case or pannier affixed to the side of your motorcycle. What must you be especially aware of?
explanation: Make sure that the weight is evenly distributed to stabilise the driving behaviour. Stow heavy luggage as far down as possible to keep the centre of gravity as low as possible.
options: An unequal distribution of weight should be avoided
Heavier pieces of luggage should be stowed as close to the bottom as possible
The gross vehicle weight rating of the motorcycle may not be exceeded

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Your motorbike is equipped with a traction control system (TCS). What is the system designed to do?
explanation: Slippage" is the sudden increase in the speed of a drive wheel when it loses grip because you have accelerated too much. This triggers the anti-slip control, which prevents the wheel from spinning by braking.
options: - prevents the rear wheel spinning when moving off
- stabilises the motorbike during an emergency braking manoeuvre
- prevents the front wheel from locking during braking

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are driving around a bend in the road, and the turning radius becomes smaller as the bend progresses. You had reckoned that the turning radius would be larger. How must you now react?
explanation:
If you have estimated the cornering radius to be larger, you should reduce your speed; by reducing your speed, you can drive a smaller cornering radius. 
You can also increase the lean angle in the bend so that you can take tighter bends.
options: I increase my inclined position
I reduce my speed
I activate the emergency stop switch

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What should you take into account when you have to brake unexpectedly sharply while driving around a road bend?
explanation: When you brake in a bend, your motorbike is lifted up by the force of inertia. You have to counteract this by counter-steering with feeling. Otherwise you will continue straight ahead and not make the bend.
options: My motorcycle tends to drive straight ahead
I should counter-steer gently
The driving line of my motorcycle remains unchanged

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: In bends with poor road conditions, what increases the risk of skidding?
explanation:
Ideally, all wheels should press on the road with the same force to ensure optimum grip and handling. If this is not the case, it can increase the risk of skidding in poor road conditions.
The suspension, for example, has the task of keeping all tyres on the road with the same force. If the suspension is damaged, it can no longer do this. The risk of skidding also increases if the tyre pressure is incorrect or if the vehicle is incorrectly or unevenly loaded.
This is because the tyres cannot apply the same force to the road and you lose grip more quickly.
options: Having a damaged chassis
Having the wrong tyre inflation pressure
Having a wrongly loaded cargo

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are travelling along a winding road with a steep gradient. Your motorbike is fully loaded. What is the right course of action?
explanation:
Avoid speeding up between bends, because speeding up would put even more strain on the brakes. Therefore, ride downhill without speeding up. 
Use the front and rear brakes evenly and try to use the braking effect of the motor to relieve the brakes. The higher the engine speed, the greater the braking effect.
options: I drive in a low gear in order to use my engine’s braking action
I avoid accelerating to high speeds between bends in the road
I brake using the front-wheel brake only

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: When is there a risk that the front wheel of the motorbike will lose contact with the carriageway?
explanation:
When speeding up, the weight shifts to the back. Extreme speeding in a low gear shifts the centre of gravity behind the rear axle and the front wheel lifts off.
A passenger also shifts the weight to the rear when speeding up. This weight shift relieves the front wheel and can cause it to lift off.
options: - accelerate in a low gear
- accelerate while carrying a pillion passenger
- brake using the front-wheel brake

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What might happen if you shift to a low gear while travelling at a high speed?
explanation: The sudden, rapid increase in engine speed when engaging the clutch creates a braking effect. The engine braking force can cause your rear wheel to lock up or slip and lose grip on the road. You could lose control of your motorbike and crash.
options: The rear wheel may lock
There is a high risk of crashing to the ground
The front wheel may lift up from the road surface

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: How should you respond if your motorbike begins to wobble?
explanation: By reducing the speed immediately, you can reduce swaying and increase driving stability. Swaying occurs at high speeds. So avoid driving very fast when continuing your journey.
options: - immediately release the accelerator and slow down
- avoid high speeds as I continue my journey
- counter-steer right now

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What is the purpose of an emergency stop switch on a motorbike?
explanation: The emergency stop switch switches off the engine. You can use it to switch off the engine quickly in dangerous situations without having to turn the key.
options: - turns off the engine
- turns off the lights
- triggers the eCall system

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What applies to the effectiveness of the front and rear wheel brakes, especially at higher speeds?
explanation: When braking, the weight shifts forward, which puts greater strain on the front wheel. That's why the front wheel brake is usually designed for higher braking effects in order to make the greater load easier to control.
options: - of the front brake is larger
- of the rear wheel brake is larger
- of the front and rear wheel brakes are equally powerful

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What can cause a motorcycle to oscillate at high speed?
explanation:
At high speeds on uneven roads or if the wheels are not balanced, your motorcycle tends to "sway" more quickly because the unevenness changes the road's position.
If you have a heavy load on the rear of your motorcycle, there will be less weight on the front wheel. At high speeds, your motorcycle may sway, making it harder for you to control your motorcycle.
options: - with unbalanced wheels
- on uneven road surfaces
- with heavy luggage at the rear

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What changes when a caravan trailer is towed?
explanation: If you drive with a caravan, not only does it increase the risk of skidding, the overtaking and braking distances will be longer as well. This is due to the additional load to be pulled and the pulling motion of the trailer.
options: The distance for overtaking increases considerably
Hasty movements of the steering wheel increase the danger of skidding
The braking distance is reduced considerably

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What changes in a car when towing a two-axle trailer?
explanation: The combination of car and trailer requires more space when driving on bends and when turning. Likewise, the mass changes the accelerating ability. It is decreasing significantly.
options: More space is needed when turning and driving round bends
Acceleration capacity is reduced
Driving stability increases

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are in your car towing a trailer on a road with oncoming traffic and want to turn left. What must you particularly remember when you set off again?
explanation: With a trailer you have a lower accelerating ability, changed mass and a greater total length. This must be taken into consideration when you're starting your car again. Oncoming traffic must not be warned in this case by using the flash light.
options: Think about the length of your car and trailer combination
Consider the reduced acceleration capacity
Warn oncoming traffic by flashing your lights

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are in your car towing a trailer which has no brakes and you approach a long steep downhill slope. What is correct?
explanation: Reduce your speed on time. Us a gear as low as possible. The thus activated engine brake supports the braking action of the pedal braking. By no means you should put your car in idling. This would make the vehicle faster.
options: Reduce speed, if necessary, engage low gear in time, be ready to brake
Make allowance for the pushing effect of the trailer
Relieve the car brakes by disengaging the clutch at frequent intervals

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What must you check on a car with a caravan trailer before setting out on a journey?
explanation: Caravans restrict the view to the back. Therefore, you must check before the start of the journey, if the mirrors provide sufficient visibility to the back. You also need to make sure that the illuminating devices are working.
options: Whether the lights of the trailer are working
Whether the view through the rear-view mirrors is adequate
Whether the passengers in the caravan trailer have put on their safety belts

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are in your car towing a fully loaded trailer which has no brakes. What is correct?
explanation: Note that a fully loaded trailer without its own brake extends the braking distance and thus the stopping distance by the respective trailer load. The thinking distance does not change in this case.
options: Braking distance increases
Reaction distance increases
Stopping distance reduces

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You want to tow a singe-axle caravan trailer behind your car. What must you check?
explanation: The caravan reduces the view to the back. You as a car driver have to check whether the rear view through the existing mirrors is sufficient. You may need to attach extra mirrors to your car. Towing vehicle and trailer must always be coordinated.
options: If the permissible trailer load or the permissible coupling of the car are exceeded
If additional rear-view mirrors must be mounted because of the width of the trailer
If the trailer is licensed to transport passengers

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You want to set off in an automatic car (hydraulic converter). What must you know?
explanation: If you give a "go" with an engaged gear as a car driver in a vehicle with automatic transmission it will try to start driving. This can only be prevented by operating the service brake. The selector lever can and may be operated with the engine stationary and running.
options: When selecting a gear, the car must, as a rule, be held by the service brakes
The selector lever must only be moved when the engine has stopped
The engine revolutions must be raised considerably so that the engine does not stall

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What must you remember with regard to tyre pressure?
explanation: By regularly checking the air pressure of the tires, tire damage can be avoided, but fuel can also be saved. If you put your vehicle under a greater burden, you need to adjust the tire pressure.
options: To check the air pressure regularly, including that of the spare wheel
To increase the pressure to the level stated in the vehicle manual when the vehicle is heavily loaded
To reduce the air pressure before longer trips

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You had a tyre failure and must mount the emergency wheel. What is prohibited when you continue to drive?
explanation: Emergency wheels have a different design than conventional wheels and are only allowed up to a speed of 80 km/h. They have worse operating characteristics. You should only drive with them as far as necessary. Taking other people with you is allowed.
options: Driving faster than 80 km/h
Driving longer than necessary with the emergency wheel
Taking passengers

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: When driving, you notice that the car constantly pulls to the left. What could be the cause of this?
explanation: If your vehicle pulls to the left so that countersteering is required, too little air pressure in the left tire could be the cause or a different wheel setting. A badly worn tire usually does not have this effect.
options: Too little air in the front left tyre
Incorrect wheel adjustment at the front axle (track, wheel camber)
The left rear tyre is extensively worn

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What does a front-wheel drive car tend to do if you accelerate too much on a bend?
explanation: As a car driver, you must always expect your vehicle with front-wheel drive to swing off in front if you over-accelerate on a turn. Your vehicle will more likely under than oversteer.
options: The front end tends to turn out to the side
The vehicle tends to oversteer
The rear end tends to turn out to the side

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What does a rear-wheel drive car tend to do if you accelerate too much on a bend?
explanation: You should always expect your vehicle with rear wheel drive to swing off to the back if you over-accelerate on a turn. It is more likely to oversteer than understeer.
options: The rear end tends to turn out to the side
The front end tends to turn out to the side
The car tends to understeer

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What are the advantages of an anti-slip device (ASR)?
explanation: The traction control system (TCS) of a car prevents the wheels of the vehicle from spinning, especially when accelerating faster. Slipping away to the side when starting to drive on slippery roads is thereby largely prevented.
options: No wheelspin when setting off
Reduced danger of sliding sideways when setting off on a slippery roadway
No locking of the wheels when braking

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You want to couple up a trailer with ball coupling. What is correct?
explanation: In a trailer with ball clutch, the clutch dog must firmly enclose the spherical head. The fuse must engage. Make sure the electrical connection works. The support wheel must not run while driving. It must be locked in high position.
options: The claw of the coupling must fit securely around the ball. The locking device must engage
The electrics must be connected
The jack wheel must be set so that it can also run when driving

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What must you do after coupling up a single-axle trailer with overrun brakes?
explanation: The breakaway cable must be hung on the coupling device of the towing vehicle. With an overrun brake, the trailer brakes automatically when the connection to the towing vehicle breaks off. The function of the brake must be checked. The support wheel must not run while driving, so it should be brought to the upper position.
options: Check that the brakes are working
Raise the jack wheel, if fitted, to the highest setting
Attach the brakeaway cable to the coupling of the motor vehicle

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What must you bear in mind when loading a single-axle trailer?
explanation: When loading a single-axle trailer, you must ensure to comply with the total mass and that your load does not exceed the permissible axial load and bearing load.
options: - axle load
- load on the coupling
- total mass

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You want to park your single-axle trailer (overrun brakes, 1000 kg permissible total mass) on a slope. What must you do?
explanation: You must always secure your trailer against possibly rolling away. To do this, you must use the parking brake and place the wheel chocks in front of the wheels. Usually such trailers have no reverse lockout.
options: Pull the parking brake
Place wheel chocks under the wheels
Engage the reverse lock

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Which dangerous defects can have occurred on a trailer with overrun brakes which has been parked for some time?
explanation: If you leave a trailer standing somewhere for a long time, the weather can cause damage: electrical connections can be damaged, rust can form on the brakes. Sun exposure does not increase the tire pressure too much, so that no dangerous defects occur.
options: The brakes may not work because of rust
Cable connections can be defective
Tyre pressure may have increased greatly due to exposure to the sun

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What must you remember when loading a trailer?
explanation: Always pay attention to the proper securing of your cargo. In order not to endanger yourself and other road users, you must always have a clear view and full control over your vehicle. The cargo must be marked at the rear and may not protrude more than 50 cm at the front.
options: - must be securely packed
- must not project more than 1 m beyond the rear reflectors, unless specially marked
- must not project more than 1 m beyond the front of the towing vehicle

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Why should you not press the clutch and switch off the engine at the same time when driving down a long slope?
explanation: When the engine is off, the engine brake (brake booster) cannot work. Even power steering is not turned on then. To respond quickly and effectively to dangerous situations, you may need both.
options: The steering of vehicles with servo-assisted steering immediately becomes unusually heavy
Full braking power cannot be reached in vehicles with brake booster system despite great force being applied to the pedal
The battery will be overcharged

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Why should you not apply the clutch when driving on a long, steep downhill slope?
explanation: If you step down the clutch, the engine brake will not work and you will have to use the service brake more. As a result, overheating and increased brake wear can occur.
options: Because the braking action of the engine will have no effect
Because this causes unnecessary wear of the brakes
Because in this case the brake servo unit will no longer function

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What is correct when coupling a full trailer?
explanation: You should make sure that a suitable person in the viewing area is about you and instructor you and that this person obstacles and road users that you can not see, warns you of a Mehrachsanhängers when coupling.
options: - should be positioned in the driver's line of vision and guide him
- warns of obstacles and road users not visible to the driver
- hold the drawbar until it has locked into the hitch

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are driving in a pair with a load. What should be noted when performing an emergency stop?
explanation: If you are driving with more weight, you should apply more braking force. Due to the additional weight, the rear wheel brakes will brake more as well
options: - have to apply more braking force
- that the rear-wheel brakes may operate more powerfully
- have to apply less braking force

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You suddenly have to brake when cornering on a wet carriageway. What special aspects exist with a vehicle equipped with an anti-lock braking system (ABS)?
explanation: On wet roads, the antilocking system prevents the wheels from locking and shortens the braking distance. In addition, the vehicle remains more steerable when braking. On gravel or snow, the braking distance can certainly be much longer.
options: The steering capability is retained for longer
The vehicle will always remain stable
It is not possible for the vehicle to skid out of the bend

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What is the effect of the cornering characteristics of a combination vehicle (car towing a caravan) when taking a turn?
explanation: Despite careful driving, it is possible that the trailer cuts the curve or even swings out. The car driver must therefore proceed with caution in order to exclude hazards to others.
options: - can jut out
- can cut the corner
- generally follows the track of the car

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You experience pendular movements on your motorbike. What could be the cause of these?
explanation: If your entire motorcycle swings to the front and back, this could be caused by heavy load or imbalance in the wheel
options: The load
A wheel imbalance
Driving at low revs

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What can restrict the functionality of a lane departure warning system?
explanation: The function of the lane departure warning system may be limited if the system cannot properly pick up lane signals. This is, because the computer-controlled system works on the basis of different optical systems. There are no signals from the guardrails. Another name for the lane departure warning system is: Lane Keeping Assist (active lane departure warning system with steering assistance).
options: A dirty road surface
The absence of road markings
The absence of guardrails

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What information should you obtain before undertaking a journey with a purely electric vehicle?
explanation: The car driver should inform himself about the range of the electric vehicle before starting the journey. This differs significantly from the range of conventional vehicles and more frequent stops to recharge the batteries are necessary. You should also take into account that there is more technology in an electric vehicle. Although it is generally true that electric vehicles are just as safe as conventional cars. But in their bodies usually run cables that are designed for enormously high voltages.
options: The locations at which I can charge the vehicle
What I have to do following an accident
Factors that influence the range

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are planning a longer journey with a purely electric vehicle. What should you be aware of?
explanation: If you are planning a longer journey with a purely electric vehicle, you should consider that your car has a much lower range compared to conventional vehicles. In addition, the capacity of the batteries is influenced by the outside temperature.
options: The availability of electric charging stations
The battery charging time
The influence of external ambient temperatures on the range

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What should you be aware of when charging purely electric vehicles?
explanation: When charging pure electric vehicles, you must be aware that they cannot be recharged at every gas station. Only use the charging cables approved by the manufacturer. Depending on the power connection, the charging time varies.
options: The charge time depends on the power supply
Charging should only be performed with a charging cable approved by the manufacturer
Charging is available at every filling station

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: How is a purely electric vehicle different from a vehicle with a combustion engine?
explanation: Pure electric vehicles are almost noiseless. These vehicles also have no direct exhaust emissions. The aerodynamic drag depends on the volume of the body and not on the type of drive.
options: - have a lower engine noise
- do not have any direct exhaust emissions
- have a lower aerodynamic drag

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are driving a purely electric vehicle in a residential area. What should you be aware of due to your lower engine noise?
explanation: With a pure electric vehicle, you are almost noiseless on the road and you can acoustically be hardly perceived by other road users. Especially cyclists are at risk if they hear no engine noise. Without looking back, they often turn.
options: Pedestrians will not notice me or will do so later than usual
Cyclist travelling ahead will turn left, without looking behind them
Vehicles following behind will tailgate me

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are driving a motor vehicle fitted with anti-lock braking system (ABS). How do you achieve the shortest possible braking distance?
explanation: If you drive a car with an automatic anti-lock braking system, you achieve the shortest braking distance by braking abruptly and with maximum pedal force. The ABS prevents the wheels from locking during braking.
options: - suddenly and with maximum force
- carefully and then increasingly harder
- multiple times at quick intervals and with maximum force

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: A lane assist system with corrective steer control can help you when driving. What should you be aware of?
explanation: A prerequisite for a perfect function of the lane departure warning system are good road markings. Keep in mind that technical driving assistants cannot compensate for inability to drive. As a car driver, you must be able to intervene into the driving experience at all times.
options: - keep the vehicle in lane if the road markings are clear
- not function if the road markings are poor
- compensate for a lack of fitness to drive (e.g. tiredness)

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are driving at high speed into a bend. What could happen if you had to brake suddenly?
explanation: If you drive fast into a tight curve, you lose road grip when you brake hard and slide out of the curve. (Centrifugal force)
options: - could lose its grip on the road
- could skid out of the bend
- will constantly maintain its driving stability with the stability control

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What can result in your motor vehicle skidding while driving round a bend?
explanation: If you turn sharply, your vehicle may start to skid on bends. This can also happen if you drive too fast. Adjust your speed when cornering.
options: Heavy oversteer
Driving too fast
Gently accelerating at the exit of the bend

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: The lane keeping assist system warns you with acoustic, haptic or optical signals. What might be the cause of this?
explanation: If you drift out of your lane, the lane departure warning system detects this by recognising that you are approaching the lane marking. The permissible total mass must not be exceeded.
options: My vehicle is getting close to the road markings at the side of the road
My vehicle is undercutting the safety distance to the vehicle ahead
Another vehicle is overtaking me with not enough side clearance

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: In what situation can the lane keep assist system with steering override help you?
explanation:
On motorways and country roads, steering intervention by the lane departure warning system can be helpful, as the markings are clearly visible there.
Due to poor markings and narrow lanes in roadworks, steering intervention by the lane departure warning system is not possible as it will most likely not be detected correctly.
options: - on motorways
- on rural roads
- in constricted roadworks sites with poor road markings

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: With which driving task can the lane keep assist system with steering override help the driver?
explanation:
If the lane markings are good, Lane Keeping Assist with steering intervention can help you to keep the vehicle on the lane when driving straight ahead.
When turning, you cross lanes and markings; the lane departure warning system cannot intervene to support you here. When overtaking, you signal to the lane departure warning system by flashing that you are crossing the lane markings intentionally. Thus, it does not intervene during the overtaking process.
options: When driving in a straight line
When turning
When overtaking

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What can negatively affect the functioning of the lane keep assist system?
explanation:
If the lane markings are in a poor condition, the lane keeping assistant cannot recognise where the lane to be maintained is. Due to additional lane markings in construction areas, it is not obvious which is the lane to be kept to.
Weather conditions can affect the sensors of the lane departure warning system. In addition, water or snow can distort the markings.
options: The weather conditions
The condition of the road markings
Additional road markings within a roadworks site

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Under what conditions will the lane keep assist system with steering override function optimally?
explanation:
The lane keeping assistant works best with clear lane markings. 
Poor or additional markings in roadworks will not allow the lane departure warning system to intervene, as it will most likely not be detected correctly.
Weather conditions can affect the sensors of the lane departure warning system. In addition, snow can distort the markings.
options: Where there are clear road markings
Where there are patches of snow on the road surface
Where there are additional roadworks markings

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What driver assistance system offers a high degree of road safety potential?
explanation:
The Autonomous Emergency Brake Assist constantly detects the traffic in front of the vehicle. If a hazard is imminent, the Emergency Brake Assist can carry out an emergency braking manoeuvre. 
Braking too late or too timidly are often causes of traffic accidents. Brake assistants usually react faster than humans and thus offer more safety.
options: The brake assist
The autonomous emergency brake
The cruise control system

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: How can driver assistance systems help you?
explanation:
In critical traffic situations, driver assistance systems can react quickly and intervene automatically by steering or braking etc..
If danger is imminent, they can warn you with light, sound and haptic signals. Driver assistance systems can also help you with driving tasks, such as keeping in lane.
options: - warn me of danger
- help me perform driving tasks
- intervene automatically in critical road traffic situations

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What can result if you accelerate too hard when driving a front-wheel drive car through a road bend?
explanation: If you give a front-wheel drive car too much gas in a bend, it can swerve over the front axle. The front tyres lose their grip on the road and your vehicle can no longer be steered, but continues straight ahead and breaks away.
options: - The front of the car can swerve
- Steerability can be reduced
- The rear of the car can swerve

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Under what conditions can an active lane change assist system perform a lane change?
explanation: The Active Lane Change Assistant only performs a lane change when it cannot detect any vehicle in the relevant safety zone. For an active lane change, the assistant must first detect a marked lane with several lanes.
options: - has detected an adequately marked carriageway with multiple lanes
- has not detected any vehicles in the relevant safety zone
- has detected a sufficiently large gap in the oncoming traffic

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Your motor vehicle is equipped with an active lane keep assist system. What information can be indicated by the status display of this system?
explanation: The system must be able to display when it is switched on, switched off or has a malfunction, as this is important for the driver.
options: - is activated
- is deactivated
- has a fault

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Your motor vehicle is equipped with a lane keep assist system. In what situation can this system help you?
explanation: Lane Keeping Assist helps you stay in lane. It warns you if you unintentionally leave the lane.
options: - I depart from my lane unintentionally
- the maximum permissible speed is exceeded
- the vehicle is driving too quickly over ruts in the road

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You have the lane keep assist system activated in your motor vehicle. It emits a warning signal while you are driving. What could be the cause of this?
explanation: Lane Keeping Assist warns you if you unintentionally leave your lane. If you forget to indicate when changing lanes, Lane Keeping Assist recognizes this as unintentionally leaving your lane and warns you.
options: I forgot to switch on my indicator when changing lane
I have unintentionally departed from my lane
I undercut the minimum distance between me and the vehicle ahead

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are using your motor vehicle’s lane keep assist system while driving. The system does not respond when you depart from the lane. What could be the cause of this?
explanation: Due to missing lane markings, insufficient road illumination and heavy precipitation, the sensors of the lane departure warning system are impaired, which means that the lane is not reliably detected.
options: Inadequate road illumination
Heavy precipitation
A lack of lane markings

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Your motor vehicle is equipped with a lane change assist system without steering intervention. While driving, the warning light flashes on the left-hand exterior rear-view mirror. What is this warning light indicating?
explanation: If there is a vehicle in the monitoring area, this is signaled by the warning lamp lighting up on the exterior mirror.
options: Another vehicle is located within the monitored area
You may not now perform a lane change to the left
You can now perform a lane change to the left without any risk

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: While driving, you are using your motor vehicle’s active lane keep assist system. How can you manually override this driver assist system in the event that it intervenes?
explanation: Countersteering and activating the indicator overrides the intervention of Lane Keeping Assist.
options: By counter-steering
By activating the indicator
By accelerating

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: In which situation is it purposeful to use an active lane change assist system?
explanation: On motorways or motorway-like roads, the lane markings are clearly visible and the lanes are usually straight. This is where Active Lane Change Assist comes in handy.
options: - motorways
- motorway-like roads
- roads without markings

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You want to overtake and you have initiated a lane change using the active lane change assist system. What is correct?
explanation: The Active Lane Change Assistant can change lanes automatically after initiation. However, you must always monitor this, as e.g. safety distances are not always maintained automatically.
options: The systems independently performs the lane change
I have to monitor the lane change
The system always maintains all safety distances independently

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Which driver assistance systems do you have to manually activate to assist you in specific situations?
explanation: The active parking assistant and the adaptive cruise control system do not count as safety-relevant assistants. Therefore, you can activate them manually.
options: The active park assist
The adaptive cruise control (ACC)
The emergency brake assist

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You want to transport furniture in the van shown here (up to 3.5 t). Compared to driving a car, what do you have to be aware of?
explanation: A van is much higher, longer and wider than a normal car. Therefore, you should always pay attention to the signage of the passage height. You should also make sure that you adjust your speed in curves, as vans could overturn more easily. In addition, the side wind attacks an even larger area, which significantly increases the risk of being pressed out of the lane.
options: - can roll over more easily when cornering
- requires special attention regarding vertical clearances
- is vulnerable to sidewinds

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: How does the active park assist help you when parking?
explanation: The active park assistant must be activated manually by you. After activating the assistant, the system supports you in finding a suitable parking space.
options: - detects sufficiently large parking spaces
- detects all obstacles during the parking manoeuvre
- checks if parking is permissible at a particular place

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Why might a turn assist system not always detect that a cyclist is present?
explanation: A turning assistant can work incorrectly due to various circumstances. So it is possible that a cyclist or a pedestrian is not recognized by the system if there are obstacles between you and the cyclist. For example, such can be parked vehicles or trees on the side of the road. Likewise, the pollution or damage to the sensor can easily be the reason for an incorrect function.
options: There is dirt on the sensor
Parking cars conceal the cyclist
The sensor is damaged

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What must you note when using the active park assist?
explanation: After activating the active park assistant, the system supports you in finding and parking a suitable parking space. Nevertheless, you still have to observe the traffic and intervene manually when the dangers arise.
options: - must be overridden if hazards exist
- means I no longer have to pay attention to other road traffic
- reliably detects all obstacles during the parking manoeuvre

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: You are driving an electric vehicle. When can recuperation inhibit the braking action?
explanation: By recuperation, the engine of the electric vehicle works like a generator when braking. The braking therefore generates electricity and automatically loads the car battery. So if the battery of the electric vehicle is already fully charged, the vehicle cannot regain the energy and the braking effect through recuperation may not be available. Instead, the vehicle has to fall back on conventional brakes. The recuperation can also be reduced or deactivated if the battery is too cold. This can reduce the braking effect through recuperation.
options: - with a fully charged battery
- at less than the battery’s operating temperature
- in eco mode

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Your vehicle is equipped with a hill-start assist. What benefit does this assist system provide?
explanation: The hill assist can make it easier for you to start off on a hill by releasing the brakes, thus preventing unintentional rolling back.
options: - prevent my vehicle from rolling backwards unintentionally
- assume control of releasing the brakes
- drive all wheels simultaneously

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What applies when using driver assistance systems for longitudinal and lateral control of your vehicle?
explanation:
Before using the driver assistance system, you should understand the system's limitations. This way you know exactly which dangerous situations and malfunctions you need to pay more attention to. 
If you notice a driver assistance system malfunction, you should oversteer as quickly as possible. Through targeted oversteering, any errors in the driver assistance system during longitudinal and lateral guidance can be responded to manually. Oversteering can usually be triggered by gently pressing the accelerator and brake or by carefully counter-steering.
options: I need to know the system limits of the driver assistance system
I must override the driver assistance system immediately in the event of a malfunction
When I am tired, I can let the driver assistance system take care of longitudinal and lateral control

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique

explanation: When a tank vehicle that you drive with partially loaded chambers, you need to adjust to increased risk of skidding and increased danger of tilting in curves.
options: A great danger of tipping over when taking bends
A great danger of skidding
Heavy steering when driving down slopes

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: How can you avoid excessive wear of the service brakes on a long downhill slope?
explanation: By timely switch back, you can conserve avoid heating the service brake. The use of the retarder is also helpful. The parking brake, however, is not right.
options: Change gears down in time
Apply the retarders
Apply the parking brake

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique

explanation: If your vehicle was several days, you should make sure that the pressure warning device is no more signals. The compressed air system has most likely lost air pressure while standing.

When the spring-loaded brake releases automatically
When 3 bar reserve pressure is shown

Tighten the wheel nuts again after driving a short distance
Inform the garage workshop that the wheel has been changed

explanation: In a puncture on the lifting axle you need to perform this vehicle and the truck breakdown service call to change a wheel according to the manual. to lift the axle and continue the journey is not right.

Call the truck breakdown service
Raise the lift axle and continue your journey

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique

explanation: In the road haulage law stipulates that industrial goods transport vehicles that do not exceed including trailers a permissible overall weight of 3.5 tonnes.
options: The commercial transport of goods in trucks whose permissible total mass including their trailers does not exceed 3.5 t
The commercial transport of goods in trucks with a permissible total mass of up to 7.5 t
The commercial transport of bulk goods

options: Tightening the wheel nuts with the prescribed torque
The alternative tightening of the wheel nuts
Checking the wheel nuts only after having driven 500 km

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: What must you be aware of when operating your motor vehicle in wintry conditions?
explanation: To ensure safety, you must drive with winter tyres, have sufficient antifreeze and clear the steps of ice and snow.
options: My vehicle must be fitted with winter tyres
All entry/exit steps must be clear of snow and ice prior to use
The vehicle must be filled with a sufficient amount of windscreen antifreeze

explanation: Shift down to increase the engine braking effect.

I use the permanent brake
I use the parking brake

chapterName: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
text: Why might your turn assist system emit a warning?
